- `project-design/appendices/stale-claims-register.md` (SC-025, SC-026, SC-027)
- `project-design/appendices/env-and-config-matrix.md`
- `project-design/appendices/api-route-matrix.md`

## 10. Change history

- 2026-11-03: Initial canonical security part written against `5a24f6f+working-tree`; records actual MFA/revocation/IP enforcement and the merchant authorization gap.

## 11. Security hardening (2026-11-05)

### Authentication and authorization (core)
- MFA challenges are `mfa_challenges` rows (opaque UUID, HMAC-stored code, single-use, channel-bound, 5 guesses then a 15-minute cool-down, 5-minute expiry). Login throttles (per identifier, per IP, MFA per IP) use the shared auth state (`core-back/lib/auth/sharedState.ts`): Redis when `REDIS_URL` is set (shared by every core instance), otherwise, or when a Redis call fails, per-process memory; the DB attempt counter on `mfa_challenges` is the durable guarantee (GAP-027).
- Principal separation: staff and merchant principals cannot cross routers (`STAFF_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED`, `MERCHANT_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED`); API tokens may only call `/external/*`. Merchant authority catalogue, escalation guards and token expiry are described in the core API part.
- Authorities remain enforced by core. The edge guard is advisory but now deny-by-default. `*` is honoured at the edge only because core re-verifies; the edge cannot verify signatures because the key lives in core.

### Edge client IP and headers
- `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` defaults to loopback only (`127.0.0.0/8,::1/128`; deploy sets `127.0.0.1/32,::1/128` plus the node's own private address, `<NODE_PRIVATE_IP>/32`, because nginx proxies to the address the backend binds to; with loopback only, `x-real-ip` was ignored on a multi-host deploy and every client looked like the nginx host). `resolveClientIp` honours forwarded headers only from trusted peers and requires a single valid IP (`x-real-ip` preferred, `x-real-client-ip` fallback). The edge always overwrites `x-real-client-ip` towards core.
- Hand-written security headers on all edges: `nosniff`, `no-referrer`, `X-Frame-Options`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, CORP, default `no-store`.
- Redaction now covers PII keys (email, phone, msisdn, iban, account number, names, identity, national id, passport, dob, address). `redactUrl` masks sensitive query values and path tokens (inbound path tokens, link keys, attempt tokens, `/logs/` ids, `/external/links/` keys).
- Limiters key on the resolved client IP, with an extra per-account limiter on admin login/MFA and merchant auth POSTs. Window envs: `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`, `ADMIN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`, `API_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`, `EXTERNAL_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`, `INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`.
- Ops note: cross-origin development frontends need `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.

### Outbound and inbound engine controls
See the core engine part: empty `allowed_hosts` fails closed, unkeyed SHA256 webhooks are rejected, timestamp requirements and capped unverified inbound storage.

### Still open
Fake Rails tester tokens stay in localStorage (GAP-019 residual); httpOnly cookies are opt-in (`SESSION_COOKIE_MODE`, default off); throttle and revoke state degrade to per-process memory without Redis (GAP-027 residual); the core-back PAN guard (GAP-026 residual). The `x-real-client-ip` trust in core still depends on the private mTLS boundary.

## Gap resolutions (2026-11-05)

- **Session identity, revocation and per-channel audience (GAP-019, GAP-020; RESOLVED).** `signSession(claims, channel)` mints HS256 tokens with a unique `jti` and the audience of the channel: `admin` -> `payment-gateway-admin`, `merchant` -> `payment-gateway-merchant`, `checkout` -> `payment-gateway-checkout` (`SESSION_AUDIENCES`). `verifySessionToken(token, channel?)` accepts any of the three audiences, or exactly the given channel, and exposes `jti`, `exp` and `channel` on `SessionClaims`. Because the audience changed, **sessions issued before this deploy (audience `payment-gateway-edge`) are rejected and every admin and merchant user must sign in again.** Revocation: `POST /internal/{admin,merchant}/auth/logout` calls `revokePrincipalSession`, which stores `revoked:<jti>` in the shared auth state until the token's own expiry (`core-back/lib/auth/revocation.ts`, 12 h bound), and `resolveSessionPrincipal` refuses revoked sessions. The edges proxy `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/logout` and the merchant equivalent; `admin-front` calls the admin logout best effort from its user store and always clears the local session.
- **Optional httpOnly session cookie (GAP-019).** `SESSION_COOKIE_MODE` (`true`/`false`, default `false`) and `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` (default `true`; set `false` only for plain-HTTP local development) are validated in the admin-back and merchant-back env. In cookie mode login/MFA responses set the token as an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` cookie (`pg_admin_session` path `/api/v1/admin`, `pg_merchant_session` path `/api/v1/merchant`, 12 h, `Secure` unless disabled) and the body carries `sessionCookie: true` instead of `token`; the edge turns the cookie back into the `Authorization: Bearer` header it forwards to core when the caller sent none, so core verifies the same JWT. Cookie-authenticated unsafe methods must carry the `x-pg-csrf: 1` header (`403 CSRF_HEADER_REQUIRED`). The cookie is ignored entirely when the mode is off, and login/MFA are exempt from the CSRF conversion so a stale cookie cannot block a new sign-in. The fronts keep a non-secret `cookie-session` sentinel (`utils/security/sessionToken.ts`) and send the CSRF header instead of a bearer token. Bearer headers keep working unchanged in both modes. The mode is off by default; enabling it needs HTTPS (or `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=false` locally). The frontend logout revoke call has a 5-second timeout and clears the local session regardless.
- **Shared throttle state (GAP-027).** `core-back/lib/auth/sharedState.ts` exposes an `AuthStateStore` (`incrWindow`, `setFlag`, `flagRemainingMs`, `del`, `clear`) backed by Redis when `REDIS_URL` is configured and by a bounded in-memory store (20,000 entries, oldest half dropped under a key flood) otherwise or when a Redis call fails. Login, MFA and the revoke list use it; keys are hashed, never a clear identifier. The policy is availability over strictness: login keeps working during a Redis outage.
- **PCI scope (GAP-026, partially resolved).** `deploy/docs/pci-scope.md` is the normative scope statement: the gateway is out of PCI DSS cardholder-data scope by design (no PAN, CVV/CVC, PIN or track data is received, processed, stored or logged; only opaque processor tokens, statuses and at most last four digits plus brand). `deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` `panRailGuardProblems` makes `loadDeployConfig` reject any `deploy.env` key naming a PAN/CVV/card-number rail and any value holding a Luhn-valid 13-19 digit token. **Still open:** the core-back guard (rejecting PAN-capable rails at registration and PAN-shaped request fields, and redacting PAN-shaped log strings) is not implemented.
- **Still open.** GAP-023 (operator-supplied SHA256 values) and GAP-025 (real malware scanner).

## Remediation round 2 (2026-11-08): account lockout, staff invitation, uploads, revocation durability

- **Login throttle (GAP-053).** The lock is keyed on `identifier|ip` (`LOGIN_PAIR_POLICY`: 5 failures / 15 min, 15 min lock) with a much larger identifier-only ceiling (`LOGIN_IDENTIFIER_POLICY`: 50 failures). An anonymous caller can no longer lock a known account for its real user from another address; a successful login clears the pair bucket (`recordLoginSuccess(identifier, ip)`). The admin and merchant edges mirror this with `createAccountLimiters(accountOf)` (`{ perAddress, ceiling }`, failures-only counting via `skipSuccessfulRequests`) in `lib/authLimiters.ts`.
- **Staff creation (GAP-052).** A maker no longer chooses a staff member's password or phone. `POST /internal/admin/users` creates an `INVITED` user; the invitee sets their own password and phone through a single-use, vault-sealed invitation token (`POST /internal/admin/auth/accept-invitation`, public and rate-limited). The `status: ACTIVE` approval is refused until the invitation is completed, and the checker context shows the masked phone and the invitation state.
- **Uploads (GAP-054).** Both edges verify the session shape and expiry and apply a per-address limiter and a `Content-Length` pre-check before multer buffers a byte (`uploadGuards`; admin limit `UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, default 20 per window).
- **Revocation durability (GAP-058).** A revoked session is written atomically to Redis (`SET ... PX`) and to the `session_revocations` table, so a Redis eviction or restart cannot resurrect it; the lookup falls back to the table. See `core.data` section 13.

## v38 execution-plane security (2026-11-13)

API tokens are bound to a plane: `pg_live_*` is refused on SANDBOX with `401 LIVE_TOKEN_ON_SANDBOX_PLANE` and `pg_test_*` is refused on LIVE with `401 SANDBOX_TOKEN_ON_LIVE_PLANE`; core also compares the token row's `env`. A session minted by Live is accepted on the Sandbox core only after the signed claims are mirrored into the sandbox database (merchant envelope and user with the signed authorities); authorities never come from a header. The edge-to-core channel remains mTLS with the existing per-role client certificates; the sandbox pool uses the same client material but a separate URL set.

> **Part ID:** `platform.runtime` · **Status:** `partial` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-13 · **Verified against:** `19d6a54+working-tree`

# Runtime and Configuration

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part describes how the platform processes start, how configuration is read and validated, in which order core composes its TLS server, storage engine and workers, how health and degradation are reported, how request IDs and logging work, how the invalidation bus is wired, and which runtime/deploy flags exist.

It covers `core-back` startup in detail and summarizes the edge and Fake Rails env surfaces. Full key-by-key values are generated in `project-design/appendices/env-and-config-matrix.md`; this part records the grouping, defaults, consumers and known unused keys.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The historical design requires:

- A private-LAN `core-back` process that reads its database and KMS configuration only from its own env.
- Edge processes with no database or KMS variables; their only upstream configuration is the core URL pool and their mTLS material.
- PostgreSQL 18 through `@prisma/adapter-pg` and `pg`; no MySQL/MariaDB runtime path.
- A unified storage engine with `UnitOfWork`, `ReadStore`, cache/velocity, audit and log ports.
- Durable workers that start with core and claim work with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.
- A queue-drainability guard: queue-only routes must not accept work when no worker can drain it.
- Redis Pub/Sub invalidation across core nodes when Redis is available, with a local fallback.
- Request IDs propagated from edge to core and returned in responses.
- Dedicated audit and log databases; logging must never block or fail a payment.
- Build-time UI flags injected by the deploy engine and runtime-config values written into the deployed release.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Environment loader

`core-back/lib/env/index.ts` defines a `z.strictObject` schema. The loader only reads keys that exist in the schema; unrelated process env keys are ignored. Values are parsed through:

- `booleanFromEnvironment` for `true/1/yes` and `false/0/no`.
- `postgresUrl`/`optionalPostgresUrl` for PostgreSQL URLs only.
- `filePath` for non-empty cert paths.
- Coercion and defaults for numeric limits.

The exported `env` is a Proxy that parses lazily and caches outside tests. In `NODE_ENV=test` the cache is bypassed so multiple test files can boot different configurations in one process. If the test environment is missing configuration, the loader prints one warning and returns a full fallback object with a local test database, test master key and worker defaults; non-test invalid configuration prints the invalid key names and exits with code 1.

`envSummary()` redacts `DATABASE_URL`, `LEADER_ELECTION_DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY` and `MTLS_SERVER_KEY_PATH`. Replica/audit/log URLs and other certificate paths are not redacted by that helper. It is not an HTTP route.

Edge env loaders follow the same pattern: strict-ish Zod object, cached outside tests, explicit `process.exit(1)` on invalid production config. `admin-back` additionally parses `CORE_BACK_URLS` into a de-duplicated HTTPS list.

| `checkout-back` | `PORT` (`4103`), `BIND_HOST` (`0.0.0.0`), core URL(s), mTLS paths, `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (`30000`), `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, `MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES` (`1048576`), `MAX_INBOUND_BODY_BYTES` (`1048576`), `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL`, `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH` (`/pay/status`), `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_*`, `INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_*` (each with `*_WINDOW_MS`), `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` |
| `fake-rails-back` | `HOST` (`127.0.0.1`), `PORT` (`4104`), `LOG_LEVEL`, `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED` (`true`), `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION`, `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (`http://127.0.0.1:8444`), `FAKE_RAILS_DATA_DIR` (`shared/data`), `CORE_INBOUND_BASE_URL` (`http://127.0.0.1:4103/api/v1/inbound`), admin credentials, JWT secret, seeder token, allowed CIDRs, webhook timeout, max body, portal rate limits |

The Fake Rails loader refuses to start without a strong non-default admin password, a seeder token and a JWT secret, and refuses production unless `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION=true`.

### 3.4 Startup order

`core-back/index.ts` `start()` executes in this order:

1. **Queue-drainability assertion.** `assertBackgroundJobQueueDrainable` throws if `WORKER_ENABLED` or `WORKER_BACKGROUND_JOBS_ENABLED` is false. The statement upload and dispute intake are queue-only routes, so booting without a drain would strand accepted work.
2. **Redis invalidation transport.** `configureRedisInvalidation()` takes `REDIS_URL` or the first `REDIS_NODES` entry, creates a publisher and a duplicate subscriber, connects both, and configures the global `invalidationBus`. On failure it logs a warning and disables the transport.
3. **TLS server object.** `createHttpsServer()` calls `createApp()`, reads the server key/cert/CA (failing fast if missing), creates the plain HTTP server and the TLS server, bridges `secureConnection` into the HTTP server, installs error handlers, and returns a small wrapper with `listen`, `close`, `address` and `on`.
4. **Storage engine.** `getStorageEngine()` creates the process singleton: primary Prisma client, replicas, read store, unit of work, cache/velocity adapter, audit driver and log sink. The LSN monitor starts inside the read store.
5. **Platform runtime wiring.** `setPlatformStorage(storage)` gives the rail runtime access to the storage engine; `setAccessLogSink(storage.logSink)` routes access logs to the dedicated log database when configured.
6. **Worker runtime.** When `WORKER_ENABLED` is true, `createProductionWorkerRuntime()` builds the worker set with the Prisma client, storage engine, intervals, batch sizes, retention flags and background-job settings, then starts every worker.
7. **Listen.** The TLS server listens on `HOST:PORT`; the callback logs the TLS 1.3 client-certificate requirement.
8. **Signal handlers.** `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` stop workers, clear the access log sink and platform storage, close the invalidation transport, shut down the storage engine (flushing logs and closing pools) and close the server.

The storage engine is constructed before `listen`, but after the server object is created. If `listen` fails, the worker runtime has already been started and is not stopped by the rejection path; that is a narrow startup-failure window.

### 3.5 Schema version check

`core-back/prisma/schemaVersion.ts` defines `REQUIRED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 37`. `core-back/prisma/client/index.ts` exports `ensureSchemaVersion()` which connects, runs:

```sql
SELECT "version" FROM "schema_versions" WHERE "id" = 1
```

and throws if the version is not 37. The check is invoked by `prisma/seed.ts`, `prisma/seedFakeRails.ts` and `prisma/syntheticSeeder/index.ts`. It is **not** invoked by `core-back/index.ts`, so the API can boot against a stale schema and fail later at query time. Migration deployment is an external deploy step (`bunx prisma migrate deploy`).

### 3.6 Worker composition

`createProductionWorkerRuntime()` wires real ports:

- `ExpirySweeperWorker` with an inquiry port backed by `platform.engine.inquire`.
- `PollWorker` with the same inquiry port.
- `InboundInboxWorker` with a handler that resolves the channel and calls `platform.engine.verifyCallback`.
- `OutboxNotificationWorker` with a notification transport (webhook or log).
- `LedgerInvariantWorker`.
- `JoinRequestExpiryWorker`.
- `PeriodicScreeningWorker` using `platform.screening`.
- `KybExpiryWorker` with its own interval and batch.
- `RetentionWorker` only when retention is enabled.
- `OutboxRelayWorker` and `AuditShipperWorker` only when a storage engine is supplied; the audit shipper additionally requires a `DedicatedAuditDatabaseDriver`, which exists only when `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL` is set.
- `BackgroundJobWorker` when background jobs are enabled, with `RECONCILIATION_RUN` and `ADJUSTMENT_EXECUTION` handlers.

Workers are in-process. Non-singleton workers rely on database claim semantics (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, conditional terminal updates and leases). Singleton workers (`ExpirySweeper`, `InboundInbox`, `JoinRequestExpiry`, `KybExpiry`, `LedgerInvariant`, `PeriodicScreening`, `Retention`, `LedgerCheckpoint`, `LedgerShardScaler`) additionally hold a PostgreSQL session advisory lock through `LEADER_ELECTION_DATABASE_URL`. That endpoint is a PgBouncer `pgw_session` alias with `pool_mode=session` when `PGBOUNCER_ENABLED=true` (or a direct PostgreSQL URL); core refuses the transaction-pooled `DATABASE_URL`, probes the session at boot and re-proves backend/lock ownership on every tick (fail closed).

### 3.7 Health and degradation

`GET /health` on the core listener:

- Computes `workersEnabled = WORKER_ENABLED && WORKER_BACKGROUND_JOBS_ENABLED`.
- Reads `background_jobs` count and oldest `QUEUED` age with `readBackgroundJobQueueHealth`.
- Treats a database read failure as `queueReachable = false` and returns a zeroed queue with `error: "QUEUE_HEALTH_UNAVAILABLE"`.
- Degrades when workers are disabled, the queue is unreachable, or the oldest queued job exceeds `WORKER_BACKGROUND_JOBS_MAX_QUEUE_AGE_MS`.
- Always responds HTTP 200 with `{ msg, status, service, queue }`.

It does not probe the storage engine, replicas, Redis, audit/log databases, backup daemon or external gateways. It also does not expose counts of `RUNNING`/dead jobs, only `QUEUED` and oldest age.

### 3.8 Request IDs and logging

`requestIdMiddleware`:

- Accepts an incoming `x-request-id` only if it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$`.
- Otherwise generates a UUID.
- Stores it on `request.requestId` and returns it as the `x-request-id` response header.

`requestLoggerMiddleware` creates a console logger with its own short six-character id and records request-scoped info/warn/error lines. It logs one header line with timestamp, method, path, status, duration, content length and IP. On response finish it writes an `http_access_logs` record through the access-log sink:

- `requestId` is the middleware `x-request-id` value (not the console short id).
- `channel` is derived from the path: `/internal/admin` -> `admin`, `/internal/merchant` -> `merchant`, `/internal/checkout` -> `checkout`, otherwise `webhook`.
- `routePattern` is `req.route?.path ?? req.path`.
- `statusCode`, duration, `dbQueries: 0` and `dbDurationMs: 0`.
- `actorId: null`; no actor is attached to the access record.
- `clientIp` from `x-real-client-ip` (validated as an IP by `edgeReportedClientIp`) first, then `req.ip`.

`LOG_LEVEL` is not consulted. Console correlation and access-log correlation can differ because of the separate short id. The access log write is wrapped in a try/catch and never fails the request.

The dedicated log sink buffers step logs and access logs, flushes every 250 ms, caps the step buffer at `STORAGE_LOG_BUFFER_MAX`, drops access records when the buffer is full, and inserts up to 500 rows per flush. When `LOG_DATABASE_URL` is absent, step logs are retained in a bounded in-memory map for attempt lookups and access logs are discarded.

### 3.9 Raw body handling

`rawBodyMiddleware` is mounted before JSON parsing and applies to:

- `/internal/checkout/inbound` and its subpaths.
- `/internal/merchant/onboarding/kyb-documents`.
- `/internal/admin/reconciliation/upload`.
- `/internal/admin/join-requests/:id/kyb-documents` by pattern.

The collector is `express.raw({ type: () => true, limit: "25mb" })`. Everything else uses JSON/urlencoded parsers with a 1 MiB core limit.

### 3.10 Invalidation bus

`core-back/lib/invalidationBus/index.ts` exports a process singleton `InvalidationBus`:

- Local `EventEmitter` plus an explicit subscription map.
- Namespace default `payment-gateway`; channel format `${namespace}:invalidation:${topic}`.
- Trailing-`*` wildcard subscriptions (`credential:*`, `gateway:*`).
- Cross-node de-duplication by event id with a 2048-id seen set.
- Topics used in production: `attempt:transition`, `credential:<id>`, `gateway:<id>`, `configuration:<scope>`.
- `ConsumerRegistry` subscribes to `credential:*` and invalidates cached consumers; admin gateway activation publishes gateway invalidation; governance publishes attempt transitions.

When Redis is configured, publisher/subscriber clients are connected at startup. A publish does both local delivery and Redis publish; a received Redis message is ignored unless its namespace matches and its id is unseen. When Redis is absent or fails to connect, invalidation is process-local only.

### 3.11 Deploy-injected runtime flags

The deploy engine injects admin UI flags rather than requiring a committed frontend `.env`:

- `ADMIN_SHOW_CHECKLISTS` (optional) and `ADMIN_SHOW_SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_CHECKLIST` (default true) control checklist visibility. `adminChecklistsVisible()` prefers the former.
- `ADMIN_SHOW_HELP_PANELS` (default true) controls help panels.
- Build constants `VITE_SHOW_CHECKLISTS`, `VITE_SHOW_SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_CHECKLIST` and `VITE_SHOW_HELP_PANELS` are injected into the `admin-front` build.
- Runtime config `showChecklists`, `showSnapshotExportChecklist` and `showHelpPanels` is written into the deployed admin release and takes precedence at boot.
- `APP_RELEASE` and `APP_COMMIT` are injected by `deployService()` into every core/edge/Fake Rails environment. `/health` exposes `release`/`commit`; the deploy batch and final verification require the expected release so a stale listener cannot pass health checks. They are additive response fields and are not part of the core/edge env schemas.

These are deploy/frontend flags; they are not core-back env keys.

## 4. Contracts and invariants

1. **Invalid production config does not boot.** The env loader exits with code 1 and prints only the failing key names.
2. **Queue-only routes require a drain.** Core refuses to boot when workers or background jobs are disabled.
3. **The storage engine is a singleton per process.** `getStorageEngine()` and `setStorageEngine()` are the only supported lifecycle.
4. **No log write may fail a payment.** Step/access log writes are best-effort; failures are swallowed.
5. **The raw body is preserved before JSON parsing.** Webhook signatures and uploaded document bytes must be exact.
6. **A request id is always returned.** Invalid or missing client values are replaced with a UUID.
7. **Redis is never authoritative for money.** When Redis is unavailable the cache/velocity adapter falls back to memory and invalidation stays local.
8. **Schema version 37 is the contract.** Seeders enforce it; migrations are deployed separately.
9. **Workers are stateless across nodes.** Coordination is by database claims, not by an in-memory scheduler.
10. **The admin UI flags are deployment-owned.** A source build uses the frontend defaults; a deployed build receives the deploy engine's values.

## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface

### 5.1 Runtime surfaces

- core TLS listener: `HOST:PORT`.
- core health: `GET /health`.
- core channel healths: `GET /internal/{admin,merchant,checkout}/health`.
- edge healths: `GET /health` on `4101`, `4102`, `4103`.
- Fake Rails healths: `GET /health`, `GET /hosted/health`.
- backup daemon: `GET /health`, `/v1/overview`.
- storage ports: primary, replicas, cache, audit, logs, unit of work.
- invalidation channels: `payment-gateway:invalidation:<topic>`.

### 5.2 Startup dependencies

| Dependency | Required | Failure behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| mTLS server key/cert/CA | Yes | Startup throws with a clear message |
| PostgreSQL primary | Yes | Startup succeeds until a query; `/health` reports queue unavailable |
| Redis | No | Warning, memory cache and local invalidation |
| Audit DB | No | Audit store is null; audit shipping is not started |
| Log DB | No | Step logs stay in memory; access logs are dropped |
| Backup daemon | No | Backup routes return 503 |
| Notification webhook | No | Log transport reports SENT |
| Fake Rails | No | Only required by synthetic seeding/seeding routes |
| Schema version 37 | Yes at seed time | Seeders fail; server boot does not check |

### 5.3 Config consumers outside the env proxy

- `core-back/lib/kybScan.ts` reads `KYB_SCANNER_MODE` directly.
- `core-back/prisma/syntheticSeeder/**` and `prisma/seedFakeRails.ts` read Fake Rails variables directly.
- `deploy/deploy.ts` reads the deploy config and injects frontend build/runtime flags.
- The backup daemon has its own env schema in `deploy/backup-daemon/src/config.ts`; it is not validated by the core schema.

## 6. Operational usage

### 6.1 Start core locally

```bash
cd core-back
bun run generate-mtls-certs
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/payment_gateway_monolith
bun run migrate-deploy
bun run db-seed
bun run start
```

`db-seed` calls `ensureSchemaVersion()`, so a fresh database that has not had migrations applied fails before seeding. `bun run start` does not perform that check.

### 6.2 Configure storage

- Set `DATABASE_URL` to the primary URL.
- Set `DATABASE_REPLICA_URLS` to a comma-separated list to enable replica reads.
- Set `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL` and `LOG_DATABASE_URL` to enable the dedicated adapters; otherwise audit shipping is skipped and log records stay in memory.
- Set `REDIS_URL` or `REDIS_NODES` for cross-node cache/velocity and invalidation.
- `STORAGE_SHARD_COUNT` is only the INITIAL width of system GL accounts (default 16, range 1..256, the same range in core env, the DB check and the deploy schema). The shard scaler widens hot accounts afterwards; the scaler is ON by default (`LEDGER_SHARD_SCALER_DRY_RUN=false`) with conservative thresholds; calibrate `LEDGER_SHARD_UP_LINES_PER_SEC` on the target hardware, and set the flag to `true` to watch proposals without widening anything.

### 6.3 Diagnose degradation

1. `GET /health` on core over mTLS.
2. If `queue.error` is `QUEUE_HEALTH_UNAVAILABLE`, the database read failed; check the primary and connection pool.
3. If `queue.oldestQueuedAgeMs` exceeds threshold, check `BackgroundJobWorker` progress, leases and handler failures.
4. If `queue.enabled` is false, the process would not have booted under the current guard; check whether the env changed after boot.
5. `/health` does not tell you about replica lag, Redis or audit/log health; query the storage engine from an operational shell or extend the health contract.

### 6.4 Rotate config

- Env is cached per process outside tests; restart the process after a change.
- Redis invalidation transport is configured once at startup; a Redis URL change requires a restart.
- Storage engine pools are created once; URL changes require a restart.
- Worker intervals and flags are read at startup.
- Deploy frontend flags require a rebuild or a runtime-config update, depending on which value is being changed.

## 7. Status and deviations

### Implemented

- Strict core env schema with PostgreSQL-only URL validation.
- Lazy/cached env proxy with a test fallback.
- TLS server, storage engine, platform runtime and workers composed in a defined order.
- Queue-drainability boot guard.
- Queue health in `/health`, including degraded state and safe error reporting.
- Redis-optional invalidation bus with local fallback.
- Request ID propagation and access-log sink.
- Raw body preservation for webhook/upload routes.
- Dedicated audit/log adapters selected by env.
- Deploy-owned admin UI flags.

### Partial

- **Schema-version enforcement.** Only seeders call `ensureSchemaVersion`; the server does not.
- **Logging.** `LOG_LEVEL` is unused; console ids differ from request ids; no structured JSON log contract; database query counts are always zero.
- **Worker controls.** `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` and `WORKER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` are parsed but not wired to the production worker runtime.
- **Health.** Only the background-job queue is checked; storage, replicas, Redis, audit/log and backup are not.
- **Env secrecy.** `envSummary` redacts `DATABASE_URL`, `LEADER_ELECTION_DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY` and `MTLS_SERVER_KEY_PATH`; replica/audit/log URLs and many certificate paths are not redacted by that helper.
- **Fake Rails CIDR.** `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS` is accepted but not consumed by the engine guard.

### Missing / deferred

- Prometheus/OpenTelemetry metrics and traces.
- Structured log levels and a request-scoped actor id in access logs.
- A startup migration/version gate.
- A disk spool for log backpressure; the buffer drops records instead.
- A runtime config reload endpoint; all settings are process-start values.
- A `/health` contract that covers storage and backup.

### Known bugs / risks

- **Code gap:** a stale schema can boot and fail later, because no boot-time schema check exists.
- **Code gap:** `LOG_LEVEL` is a no-op, so production cannot change console verbosity through config.
- **Code gap:** console log correlation uses a different id from the response/access log, which makes cross-referencing harder.
- **Code gap:** the `BackgroundJobWorker` starts before `listen`; a listen failure does not stop it in the rejection path.
- **Risk:** `TRUST_PROXY` defaults to false, but the access logger prefers `x-real-client-ip` regardless; only the edge/private boundary makes that safe.
- **Documentation gap:** historical designs describe a full metrics/alerting stack and hourly Redis snapshots; neither is part of the current runtime.

New core keys: `EXECUTION_PLANE` (`LIVE`|`SANDBOX`, default `LIVE`), `PLANE_FENCE_ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_ON_LIVE` (development escape hatch, default false), `FAKE_RAILS_CONTROL_URL` and `FAKE_RAILS_CONTROL_TOKEN`. The edges add `SANDBOX_CORE_BACK_URL`/`SANDBOX_CORE_BACK_URLS`; an empty pair means the sandbox is not configured and the sandbox routes answer `503 SANDBOX_NODE_UNAVAILABLE`. Deploy adds `SANDBOX_ENABLED`, `SANDBOX_NODE`, `SANDBOX_CORE_PORT` (4005), `SANDBOX_DB_NAME` (`payment_gateway_sandbox`), `SANDBOX_REMOTE_DIR` and `SANDBOX_CORE_BACK_URLS`. The deploy planner emits a second core service `pg-core-sandbox` with `EXECUTION_PLANE=SANDBOX`, sandbox `DATABASE_URL`/session leader URL, Fake Rails control URL/token, backups disabled and its own release tree; the PostgreSQL provisioner creates the database and `pgw_sandbox`/`pgw_sandbox_session` PgBouncer aliases.

# Observability

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part documents what the platform actually exposes and records for operations: the `/health` contract, queue health, request and access logging, step logs, the dedicated audit and log databases, the storage health method, backup observability, and the gaps against the historical SLO/metrics design.

It covers core and edge health endpoints and the backup daemon overview. It does not define on-call procedures, alert routing or dashboards that are not in the repository. The historical SLOs and runbooks are design intent, not current automated behavior.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The historical design requires:

- Liveness/readiness distinction and a health endpoint that detects a stuck queue.
- Per-route metrics: initiate/confirm success rates, latency percentiles, OTP send failures, `UNKNOWN` count and age, webhook lag, polling load, breaker state, fee variance and settlement lag.
- Alerts for stale `UNKNOWN`, late success, conflicting signals, rejected callbacks from unlisted IPs, signature-failure spikes, unmapped response codes, reconciliation mismatch, token-refresh failures, credential-check failures, clearing drift and merchant receivable above ceiling.
- Dashboards for volume/success by gateway, rail and merchant; funnel by collection mode; operator queues.
- A dedicated audit database with an append-only SHA-256 hash chain and an integrity verifier.
- A dedicated operational log database with monthly-partitioned `attempt_step_logs`, `http_access_logs` and `gateway_wire_logs`, fed by a non-blocking bounded buffer every 250 ms.
- A backup control plane with WAL lag, target health, run catalog, drill reports and an admin overview.
- SLOs: attempt initiation availability 99.9%, OTP confirmation p95 < 4 s, webhook processing p95 < 30 s, 95% of `UNKNOWN` resolved within 24 h, reconciliation freshness 99% within 4 h, and zero ledger drift.

The code implements the health contract, the log/audit planes and the backup overview. It does not implement the metrics/alerts/dashboards or the `gateway_wire_logs` table.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Core `/health`

The only core health route is `GET /health` on the TLS listener, registered before the routers. It is not exposed by an edge and is not a public endpoint.

It computes:

```text
thresholdMs = WORKER_BACKGROUND_JOBS_MAX_QUEUE_AGE_MS
workersEnabled = WORKER_ENABLED && WORKER_BACKGROUND_JOBS_ENABLED
queue = readBackgroundJobQueueHealth(client, { now, thresholdMs })
degraded = !workersEnabled || !queueReachable || queue.degraded
```

`readBackgroundJobQueueHealth` issues two queries:

1. `count` of `background_jobs` where `state = 'QUEUED'`.
2. `findFirst` of the oldest `QUEUED` job, ordered by `createdAt` ascending, selecting `createdAt`.

It computes `oldestQueuedAgeMs` and marks `degraded` when that age exceeds the threshold. On a database exception the route catches the error, sets `queueReachable = false`, and returns a zeroed queue with `error: "QUEUE_HEALTH_UNAVAILABLE"`. It does not leak the exception text or tenant rows.

The response shape is:

```json
{
  "msg": "OK" | "DEGRADED",
  "status": "ok" | "degraded",
  "service": "core-back",
  "queue": {
    "enabled": true,
    "queued": 0,
    "oldestQueuedAgeMs": null,
    "thresholdMs": 300000,
    "degraded": false,
    "error": "QUEUE_HEALTH_UNAVAILABLE"
  }
}
```

The `error` key is present only when the queue is unreachable. HTTP status is always 200, so a load balancer cannot distinguish degraded from healthy by status code.

What it does **not** check:

- PostgreSQL primary/replica latency or lag.
- Redis reachability.
- Audit or log database reachability.
- Storage engine health (`engine.health()` exists but is not called by the route).
- Backup daemon health.
- Worker heartbeat or last successful tick.
- `RUNNING` jobs whose lease expired, or failed jobs.
- Outbox/audit shipper lag.
- External gateway health or circuit breakers.

### 3.2 Channel and edge health

Each internal router has a trivial health route:

| Route | Auth | Response |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `GET /internal/admin/health` | mTLS channel only, before `requireAuthentication` | `{ status: "ok", channel: "admin" }` |
| `GET /internal/merchant/health` | mTLS channel only, before `requireAuthentication` | `{ status: "ok", channel: "merchant" }` |
| `GET /internal/checkout/health` | mTLS channel only | `{ status: "ok", channel: "checkout" }` |

Each edge has an unauthenticated `GET /health` returning `{ status: "ok", service, uptime }`. The edge health route does not check core reachability, certificate expiry or the route pool. A healthy edge can be serving 502s because core is down.

The backup daemon has `GET /health` returning its status, engine mode and version, and `GET /v1/overview` returning engine mode, WAL health, targets, schedule/policy, recent backups and drills.

### 3.3 Request logger and access log

`requestLoggerMiddleware` attaches a console logger to each request. The console format is a timestamped header with a six-character random id, method, path, status, duration, content length and client IP, followed by request-scoped info/warn/error lines. Status >= 500 or an error line goes to `console.error`; status >= 400 or a warning goes to `console.warn`; otherwise `console.log`.

On response finish, the middleware writes one access record to `LogSinkPort.writeAccessLog`:

```ts
{
  requestId: req.requestId,
  channel: "admin" | "merchant" | "checkout" | "webhook",
  method,
  routePattern: req.route?.path ?? req.path,
  statusCode,
  durationMs,
  dbQueries: 0,
  dbDurationMs: 0,
  actorId: null,
  clientIp: x-real-client-ip ?? req.ip,
  createdAt: new Date()
}
```

Important actual behavior:

- The console id is generated independently from `x-request-id`, so console lines and `http_access_logs` rows do not share a correlation id.
- `dbQueries` and `dbDurationMs` are hard-coded zeros; there is no query instrumentation.
- `actorId` is always null; the principal/user is not attached to the access record.
- `routePattern` uses Express `req.route.path`, which is the matched route pattern for the final handler, not necessarily the full internal namespace path.
- The channel is inferred from the path prefix, not from the certificate.
- The access-record write is best-effort; exceptions are swallowed.
- There is no sampling, rate limiting or body capture.
- `LOG_LEVEL` is not consulted, so console verbosity is fixed by the logger implementation and the console stream used.

### 3.4 Step logs

`DynamicRailEngine.recordStepLogs` sends each `StepExecutionResult.logs` entry to `LogSinkPort.writeStepLog` when a log sink is configured. The record contains:

- `attemptId`, `gatewayVersionId`, `phase`, `stepId`, `stepOrder`.
- `redactedRequestJson`, `redactedResponseText`.
- `httpStatus`, `durationMs`, `outcome`, `createdAt`.

Redaction happens before the sink call through `Vault.redactPayload` with the literal secrets. The engine catches sink exceptions so logging cannot fail a payment.

`StepExecutor` also calls its optional logger with redacted request/response data. In the production runtime the sink is the dedicated DB adapter; the executor logger is not configured with a separate transport in the current composition.

The log database adapter:

- Buffers step logs up to `STORAGE_LOG_BUFFER_MAX`.
- Flushes every `STORAGE_LOG_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS` (default 250 ms) and immediately when the step buffer reaches 250 records.
- Inserts at most 500 step rows and 500 access rows per flush.
- Inserts into `attempt_step_logs` with `ON CONFLICT (id, created_at) DO NOTHING`.
- Inserts into `http_access_logs`.
- On a step insert failure, unshifts the batch back if the buffer has room; otherwise the batch is lost.
- Drops access records when the access buffer is full.
- Keeps an in-memory bounded map of step logs per attempt when there is no log DB, and for a short window when there is one.

There is no `gateway_wire_logs` table and no disk spool. The historical design's "gateway wire logs" and "spool to disk under pressure" are not implemented.

### 3.5 Audit database

When `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL` is set, core constructs a `DedicatedAuditDatabaseDriver`. Admin writes call `writeAudit`/`writeAuditLog`, which inserts into the transactional `audit_outbox` in the same transaction as the business change. The `AuditShipperWorker` then:

1. Claims a batch of `audit_outbox` rows where `shipped_at IS NULL`, ordered by `created_at` and `id`, using `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.
2. Appends the batch to the audit database with an idempotent source id.
3. Updates `shipped_at = now()` for the batch.

The audit database stores an append-only SHA-256 chain: each row's `row_hash` covers the previous hash and the row identity/action/entity/before/after payload. `verifyHashChainIntegrity` recomputes from `seq_no` order and reports the first broken id. The schema and provisioner enforce append-only behavior (no update/delete) for the application role.

Important actual behavior:

- Shipped `audit_outbox` rows and processed `outbox_events` rows are pruned by the relay/shipper after `STORAGE_AUDIT_OUTBOX_RETENTION_MS` / `STORAGE_OUTBOX_RETENTION_MS` (default 1 h; 0 disables). Shipping uses a lease column (`audit_outbox.lease_until`).
- If the audit database is absent, `auditStore` is null and `AuditShipperWorker` is not started.
- Admin audit searches use the dedicated audit store when `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL` is configured; otherwise they read the primary `audit_log` table through Prisma.
- Audit logs are not a substitute for step logs; step logs are operational, audit logs are governance evidence.

### 3.6 Storage health method

`StorageEngine.health()` exists and returns:

- Primary: ok flag, latency, optional detail.
- Replicas: per-replica ok, healthy, lag ms and last replay LSN.
- Cache: ok, driver (`redis` or `memory`), optional detail.
- Audit: ok, configured.
- Logs: ok, configured.

It probes with bounded timeouts (2 s for DBs, 1 s for cache). The method is called by tests and is available to code, but there is **no HTTP route** that calls it. `/health` does not invoke it. An operator cannot inspect storage health through the public/channel API.

### 3.7 Backup observability

The core backup router is mounted at `/internal/admin/system/backups` after admin authentication:

| Route | Authority | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `GET /overview` | `security:read` or `gateway:read` | Calls daemon `/v1/overview` when configured; reads local `backup_catalog_runs` and `backup_restore_drills`; returns configured/reachable/error, engine mode, healthy, WAL, targets, schedule, policy, backups, latest drill, drills and local catalog |
| `POST /trigger` | `security:write` | Requires daemon; queues full/delta for `all`, `postgres_core`, `audit_db` or `redis`; writes a local `backup_catalog_runs` row |
| `POST /drill` | `security:write` | Requires daemon; queues a restore/invariant drill; writes a local `backup_restore_drills` row |
| `PUT /policy` | `security:write` | Without `approvalRequestId`, creates a `BACKUP_POLICY` approval; with an approved request, checks maker != checker and calls daemon `/v1/policy` |
| `GET /catalog` | `security:read` or `gateway:read` | Returns local runs/drills only |

The admin edge proxies `/overview`, `/trigger`, `/drill` and `/policy`; `/catalog` is not proxied by `admin-back`. When the daemon is not configured, the overview still returns the local catalog with `configured: false`, `daemonReachable: false` and `daemonError: "BACKUP_DAEMON_NOT_CONFIGURED"`; writes return 503.

The daemon's own overview includes:

- `engineMode` (`wal-g`, `barman`, or `none`).
- WAL archive lag, current LSN, last archived LSN, lag bytes.
- Targets with kind (`s3`, `ssh`, `redis`, `database`), health and detail.
- Schedule/policy.
- Backups and drills.

The daemon scheduler is UTC and supports full/delta/drill crons. It does not run an hourly Redis BGSAVE; Redis is a backup target when triggered.

### 3.8 What the admin audit/step views can show

- `GET /internal/admin/audit-logs` reads the configured audit store with filters, pagination, summary and export.
- `GET /internal/admin/audit-logs/:id` returns one audit row.
- Attempts expose step logs to the extent the admin routes call the log sink; the engine itself writes them to the sink.
- `GET /internal/admin/attempts/:id` returns attempt state and related data; the admin attempt detail view may call `queryStepLogsForAttempt`.

The access-log table is operational evidence, not a business audit. It records route/status/duration and a client IP but not the actor or request body.

## 4. Contracts and invariants

1. **Core health is private.** It is served only on the mTLS listener.
2. **Core health always responds 200.** Degradation is in the JSON, not the status code.
3. **Queue health reads only aggregate data.** It never returns tenant rows.
4. **A database failure in health does not crash the process.** It reports `QUEUE_HEALTH_UNAVAILABLE`.
5. **Logging never blocks a payment.** Engine and access-log writes are best-effort.
6. **Step logs are redacted before persistence.** The request/response payloads pass through the vault redactor.
7. **Audit outbox shipping is idempotent.** The audit database ignores duplicate source ids, and `shipped_at` is only set after append.
8. **Audit rows are retained.** `shipped_at` is a marker; there is no delete.
9. **Storage health is not an HTTP contract.** It is an internal method.
10. **Backup writes require the daemon.** The local catalog alone is not a control plane.

## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface

### 5.1 Observability endpoints

| Surface | Method/path | Auth | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Core | `GET /health` | mTLS client cert only | Queue health/degradation |
| Admin channel | `GET /internal/admin/health` | mTLS CN `admin-back` | Channel liveness |
| Merchant channel | `GET /internal/merchant/health` | mTLS CN `merchant-back` | Channel liveness |
| Checkout channel | `GET /internal/checkout/health` | mTLS CN `checkout-back` | Channel liveness |
| Admin edge | `GET /health` | None | Process liveness/uptime |
| Merchant edge | `GET /health` | None | Process liveness/uptime |
| Checkout edge | `GET /health` | None | Process liveness/uptime |
| Backup daemon | `GET /health` | mTLS (or insecure dev mode) | Daemon liveness/engine mode |
| Backup daemon | `GET /v1/overview` | mTLS | Full backup/PITR overview |
| Fake Rails | `GET /health`, `GET /hosted/health` | None/internal | Emulator liveness |

There is no `/metrics`, `/debug/vars`, `/ready` or `/version` route in core.

### 5.2 Log and audit stores

| Store | Driver | Tables | Enabled by |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Core operational log DB | `DedicatedPostgresLogSink` | `attempt_step_logs`, `http_access_logs` | `LOG_DATABASE_URL` |
| Dedicated audit DB | `DedicatedAuditDatabaseDriver` | audit append-only table with `prev_hash`/`row_hash` | `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL` |
| Core transactional outbox | `outbox_events` | CQRS projector input | always (ledger/attempt writes) |
| Core transactional audit outbox | `audit_outbox` | shipper input | always for audited writes |
| In-memory step fallback | bounded map | per attempt | no log DB or read fallback |

### 5.3 Backup surface

| Core route | Admin edge route | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `GET /internal/admin/system/backups/overview` | `GET /api/v1/admin/system/backups/overview` | Requires `security:read` or `gateway:read` |
| `POST .../trigger` | `POST /api/v1/admin/system/backups/trigger` | Requires `security:write`; relays 202 |
| `POST .../drill` | `POST /api/v1/admin/system/backups/drill` | Requires `security:write`; relays 202 |
| `PUT .../policy` | `PUT /api/v1/admin/system/backups/policy` | Requires `security:write`; maker-checker |
| `GET .../catalog` | not proxied | Local catalog only |

### 5.4 Relevant env keys

- `WORKER_BACKGROUND_JOBS_MAX_QUEUE_AGE_MS` for health degradation.
- `LOG_DATABASE_URL`, `STORAGE_LOG_BUFFER_MAX`, `STORAGE_LOG_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS` for logs.
- `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL` for the audit store.
- `BACKUP_DAEMON_URL`, `BACKUP_DAEMON_*` cert paths and timeout for backup.
- `LOG_LEVEL` (declared, unused).
- `PORT`, `HOST`, `MTLS_*` for the listener.

## 6. Operational usage

### 6.1 Check health over mTLS

```bash
curl --cert certs/admin-back-client.crt \
     --key certs/admin-back-client.key \
     --cacert certs/internal-ca.crt \
     https://127.0.0.1:4000/health
```

A healthy response has `status: "ok"` and `queue.degraded: false`. A degraded response has `status: "degraded"` with either `queue.enabled: false`, `queue.error: "QUEUE_HEALTH_UNAVAILABLE"`, or a too-old oldest queued job.

### 6.2 Inspect the queue

The health route only exposes the oldest queued age and count. For a deeper diagnosis, query `background_jobs` directly with the core database credentials:

```sql
SELECT state, count(*), min(created_at), max(created_at)
FROM background_jobs
GROUP BY state;
```

`RUNNING` jobs with an expired `locked_at` are re-queued by the worker; `/health` does not show them.

### 6.3 Inspect step and access logs

With `LOG_DATABASE_URL` set:

```sql
SELECT phase, step_id, http_status, outcome, duration_ms, created_at
FROM attempt_step_logs
WHERE attempt_id = $1
ORDER BY step_order, created_at;

SELECT request_id, channel, method, route_pattern, status_code, duration_ms, client_ip, created_at
FROM http_access_logs
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

The access table has no actor id and no query timing, so it answers "what route and status", not "who did it and how expensive was it".

### 6.4 Verify the audit chain

Use `DedicatedAuditDatabaseDriver.verifyHashChainIntegrity(limit)` from an operational script or test. It returns `{ verifiedCount, valid, firstBrokenId? }`. A broken chain should be treated as a P1 evidence incident.

### 6.5 Inspect backups

1. Ensure `BACKUP_DAEMON_URL` and the mTLS material are configured.
2. `GET /internal/admin/system/backups/overview` (or the admin edge route) for engine mode, WAL lag, targets, schedule/policy, backups and drills.
3. `POST /trigger` for a full/delta run, `POST /drill` for a restore/invariant drill.
4. `GET /catalog` for the local catalog when the daemon is unavailable.
5. Policy changes require a `BACKUP_POLICY` approval; the route refuses self-check.

### 6.6 What to monitor with an external system

Because there is no metrics endpoint, an external monitor can only poll:

- Core `/health` JSON over mTLS.
- Edge `/health`.
- Backup daemon `/health` and `/v1/overview`.
- PostgreSQL/Redis directly with their own exporters.
- The `background_jobs`, `outbox_events`, `audit_outbox` and `inbound_events` tables directly.

The historical alerts on gateway signature spikes, attempt latency, `UNKNOWN` age, clearing drift and credential-check failures are not emitted by the application.

## 7. Status and deviations

### Implemented

- Core queue health/degradation with a safe database-failure response.
- Channel and edge liveness endpoints.
- Console request logging with request-scoped messages.
- Access-log records to a dedicated log database.
- Redacted step logs with a dedicated log database and an in-memory fallback.
- Dedicated audit database with SHA-256 hash chaining and an integrity verifier.
- Transactional audit outbox with idempotent shipping.
- Storage health method with primary/replica/cache/audit/log probes.
- Backup overview, trigger, drill and policy control plane.
- Local backup catalog fallback.

### Partial

- **Access logs.** Zero query counts, no actor, separate console id, no sampling or retention.
- **Audit retention.** (Closed 2026-11-04) `audit_outbox` is pruned after the retention window; the dedicated audit database is the durable copy.
- **Storage health.** Implemented but not exposed over HTTP.
- **Backup health.** Core `/health` does not include the daemon; operators need the overview route.
- **Step log durability.** No disk spool; a full buffer drops records.
- **Log levels.** `LOG_LEVEL` is unused.
- **Metrics/alerts.** The SLO and alert catalog is design-only.

### Missing / deferred

- Prometheus/OpenTelemetry metrics and distributed tracing.
- `gateway_wire_logs`.
- A `/metrics` or `/ready` endpoint.
- A storage-health HTTP route.
- Per-route latency/error metrics, gateway success rates, `UNKNOWN` age metrics, webhook lag, polling load and circuit-breaker gauges.
- Disk-spooled log backpressure.
- Outbox/audit retention and partition maintenance automation.
- A worker heartbeat/last-tick metric.
- A backup daemon health proxy on core `/health`.

### Known bugs / risks

- **Code gap:** core `/health` stays HTTP 200 when degraded, which can mask a dead queue behind a naive load-balancer probe.
- **Code gap:** console log ids and `x-request-id` differ; cross-referencing requires the access table, not the console.
- **Code gap:** audit outbox rows and shipped audit rows have no retention; storage growth is unbounded in code.
- **Code gap:** log buffer overflow silently drops records; there is no counter for dropped logs.
- **Operational risk:** a healthy edge `/health` does not imply core reachability or certificate validity.
- **Documentation gap:** historical runbooks and SLO dashboards are not implemented as code or configuration.

## Security hardening (2026-11-05)

Redaction was extended to PII keys (email, phone, msisdn, iban, account number, names, identity, national id, passport, dob, address) and `redactUrl` masks sensitive query values and path tokens (inbound path tokens, link keys, attempt tokens, `/logs/` ids, `/external/links/` keys). Edge limiters and access logs use the resolved client IP. Core's access-log client IP is the edge-reported `x-real-client-ip` only when it is a valid IP, otherwise `request.ip`. MFA SMS codes no longer appear in `notifications.payload_json`.

> **Part ID:** `platform.sandbox` · **Status:** `partial` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-13 · **Verified against:** `working-tree`

# Parallel Sandbox Execution Plane

## 1. Purpose and scope

`v38` makes Sandbox a physically separate world instead of a per-row flag:

- **Live:** `pg-core-back` with `EXECUTION_PLANE=LIVE` against `payment_gateway_prod`.
- **Sandbox:** `pg-core-sandbox` with `EXECUTION_PLANE=SANDBOX` against `payment_gateway_sandbox`, with every outbound rail routed to `fake-rails-back`.

The separation is enforced in four layers: separate database, separate process, database trigger fence, and edge route namespaces. A missing `WHERE env = 'LIVE'` can therefore never leak sandbox wallets, attempts or journal lines into Live reports, cash-outs or reconciliation.

This part owns the plane model, the fence, the sandbox control API, the edge routing, the Sandbox Studio UI and the Fake Rails v2 stateful accounts. Fake Rails protocol/chaos behaviour remains in `parts/06-fake-rails/**`; deploy topology remains in `parts/07-deploy/**`.

## 2. Non-negotiable rules

1. **Live and Sandbox never share operational tables.** `payment_gateway_prod` contains only LIVE rows; `payment_gateway_sandbox` contains only SANDBOX rows.
2. **The environment is the process plane, never a merchant status.** `core-back/lib/executionPlane.ts` resolves `EXECUTION_PLANE` (default `LIVE`, invalid values abort). `checkout.ts` and `merchant.ts` no longer contain `resolveEnvironment(merchantStatus)`.
3. **No implicit OD-10 fallback.** A `PENDING`, `SUSPENDED`, `DRAFT` or `PENDING` wallet/application is refused on both planes with `409 MERCHANT_NOT_ACTIVE` / `APPLICATION_NOT_ACTIVE` / `WALLET_NOT_ACTIVE`. A pending Live merchant trains on the Sandbox plane through an ACTIVE sandbox envelope.
4. **A sandbox link is `sbx_*`; a Live link is `pl_*`.** `checkout-back` selects the pool from the prefix; it never falls back to Live for a sandbox link.
5. **API tokens are plane-bound.** `pg_live_*` is refused on the SANDBOX plane with `LIVE_TOKEN_ON_SANDBOX_PLANE`; `pg_test_*` is refused on the LIVE plane with `SANDBOX_TOKEN_ON_LIVE_PLANE`. The core also checks the token row's `env` column.
6. **The checkout inspector only exists on `sbx_` links.** Three gates: the front end requires `env === "SANDBOX"`/`sbx_`, `checkout-back` refuses any other link key, and core mounts the sandbox routes only on the SANDBOX plane.

## 3. Schema v38-v39

Migration `20261113120000_v38_sandbox_execution_plane` (schema version 38) and `20261114090000_v39_sandbox_studio` (schema version 39) add:

- `payment_links.env` and `access_tokens.env` (`GatewayEnvironmentType`, default `LIVE`); `payment_attempts.env` already existed.
- `system_execution_plane` singleton (`id = 1`, `plane`, `allow_fake_rails`, `live_sync_revision`, `last_synced_from_live`).
- `sandbox_sync_audits` (blueprint sync, demo seed, reset, wallet top-up).
- `enforce_execution_plane_env_fence()` attached to `payment_links`, `payment_attempts` and `access_tokens`.
- `enforce_no_fake_rails_on_live_plane()` attached to `gateways` and `gateway_environments`.
- v39 Studio parity: nullable `wallets.name`, `payment_links.title` and `payment_links.description`; both were accepted by portal contracts but discarded before v39.

A SANDBOX database always rejects LIVE rows. A LIVE database rejects SANDBOX rows in strict mode (`app.plane_fence_strict=true`), which the migration stores at database level for real deployments. The test suite deliberately disables strict mode because it keeps both kinds of rows in one throwaway database; `test/sandboxPlane.test.ts` re-enables it per transaction and proves both directions. `PLANE_FENCE_ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_ON_LIVE=true` is the development-only escape hatch that lets a single-box Live process keep using the emulator (deploy sets it only outside production).

`verifyExecutionPlaneFenceOnBoot()` runs before Express listens. It refuses a process whose plane differs from `system_execution_plane.plane`, and refuses `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true` on LIVE without the development escape hatch.

## 4. Sandbox control API (`core-back/api/internal/sandboxControl.ts`)

Mounted at `/internal/sandbox` for the merchant and admin edges only, and guarded by `isSandboxPlane()`:

| Route | Behaviour |
| :--- | :--- |
| `GET /merchant/overview` | Creates the merchant sandbox envelope on first use and returns wallet/application/link/attempt/token counts and live wallet balances. |
| `POST /merchant/wallets/:walletId/balance` | `CREDIT`, `DEBIT` or `SET_EXACT`; posts a balanced `ADJUSTMENT` journal entry (`DR TREASURY / CR wallet` or the reverse) and audits `WALLET_TOPUP`. Negative results are refused. |
| `POST /merchant/seed-demo` | Creates a funded 5,000 LYD wallet (opened with a real journal entry), an ACTIVE application, three `sbx_` links, a POS terminal and a one-time `pg_test_` token. |
| `POST /merchant/seed-history` | Adds 1-100 balanced historical sandbox payments (`PAYMENT_ATTEMPT` journal entries) for the merchant's first demo link, for realistic tables/charts. |
| `POST /merchant/reset` | Deletes only that merchant's sandbox attempts, links, applications, wallets, tokens, webhooks, disputes and dependent rows; the append-only journal is retained as the sandbox history. |
| `GET /merchant/wallets/:walletId`, `GET /merchant/wallets/:walletId/ledger` | Wallet detail, live balance and paginated shard ledger. |
| `GET /merchant/payments/:attemptId`, `POST /merchant/payments/:attemptId/refund`, `POST /merchant/payments/:attemptId/simulate-dispute`, `POST /merchant/disputes/:disputeId/resolve` | Payment detail, real sandbox ledger refund, dispute simulation and resolution (lost dispute books a chargeback through governance). |
| `GET/POST/PATCH /fake-rails/accounts*` | Proxies the Fake Rails v2 account controller with merchant scoping; shared presets are read-only and cloned into merchant-owned copies. |
| `POST /merchant/reconciliation/import-fake-rails` | Generates the merchant's synthetic clearing CSV, ingests it through `StatementIngestor`, marks the entries statement-included and returns matched/mismatch/missing counts. |
| `POST /merchant/webhooks/test-ping` | Queues a test delivery to every ACTIVE merchant webhook endpoint. |
| `GET/POST /fake-rails/clearing/*` | Pools, synthetic clearing statement and settle. |
| `GET /admin/overview`, `GET /admin/merchants`, `GET /admin/merchants/:id/overview`, `POST /admin/reset` | Staff inspection and scoped/global reset (staff principal required). |
| `GET/PUT /admin/fake-rails/scenarios*`, `GET/POST /admin/fake-rails/transactions*`, `GET/POST /admin/fake-rails/webhooks*`, `GET/POST /admin/fake-rails/statements*` | Staff Fake Rails control center: chaos profiles, transaction actions, webhook replay/fire, tester statements. |

The core trusts the edge identity (mTLS) and the signed session. On the SANDBOX plane, a merchant or staff session minted by Live is mirrored into the sandbox database on first use (merchant envelope + user with the signed authorities), so no second login is needed and a pending Live merchant can train immediately.

## 5. Edge routing

- **merchant-back:** `/api/v1/merchant/sandbox/*` → `SANDBOX_CORE_BACK_URLS` via `api/sandboxProxy.ts`. `/overview`, `/seed-demo`, `/seed-history`, `/reset`, `/wallets/:id/*`, `/payments/:id/*`, `/disputes/:id/resolve`, `/reconciliation/*`, `/fake-rails/*` and `/webhooks/test-ping` map to the sandbox control routes; list/create resources (`/wallets`, `/applications`, `/links`, `/payments`, `/tokens`) map to the sandbox core's `/internal/merchant/*` (same router, separate database). `/mirror/*` is a raw forward to `/internal/merchant/*` for Live-parity pages. The external API accepts both `pg_live_*` and `pg_test_*` and selects the pool from the prefix.
- **admin-back:** `/api/v1/admin/sandbox/*` → sandbox core only (`overview`, merchant overview/reset, wallet balance, fake-rails accounts/clearing/scenarios/transactions/webhooks/statements). `/mirror/*` raw-forwards to `/internal/admin/*` for Live-parity pages.
- **checkout-back:** `sbx_*` links and `SANDBOX` inbound webhook environments → sandbox core. `pl_*` and LIVE inbound → Live core. The inspector routes (`sandbox-accounts`, `sandbox-inspector`, `sandbox-simulate`) refuse a non-`sbx_` key with `403 SANDBOX_INSPECTOR_FORBIDDEN_ON_LIVE_LINK`.
- All three edges keep one connection pool per URL set; a failure inside the sandbox pool never fails over to Live (and the reverse). An unconfigured sandbox node answers `503 SANDBOX_NODE_UNAVAILABLE`.

## 6. Sandbox Studio UI

- **merchant-front:** a separate sidebar section "Sandbox Studio (Testing & Training)" with `/sandbox/overview`, `/wallets`, `/wallets/:id`, `/applications`, `/links`, `/payments`, `/payments/:id`, `/accounts`, `/tokens`, each wrapped in the amber `SandboxBanner`. Wallet detail has balance controls, a simulated cash-out and the sandbox ledger; payment detail has refund, dispute simulation/resolution, inspector secrets and journal lines. A "Sandbox Live Mirror" section reuses Live pages under `/sandbox/mirror/*` (cash-outs, disputes, POS, credentials, team, webhooks, tokens, statements, reports); the API interceptor rewrites Live paths and the router aliases Live navigation into the mirror.
- **admin-front:** `/sandbox/overview`, `/sandbox/merchants`, `/sandbox/merchants/:id` and `/sandbox/fake-rails` (accounts/clearing/chaos/transactions tabs), all built with the standard ApiTable/TableFilters/SummaryExportCard/detail-drawer system, plus a "Sandbox Live Mirror" section for merchants, wallets, applications, transactions, approvals, audit log, operator cases, disputes, adjustments, cash-outs, reconciliation, pricing, profitability, liquidity, journal entries, invariant, credential sets, gateways/routes, reports, platform settings, jobs/outbox and object storage.
- **checkout-front:** `SandboxCheckoutInspector` renders only when the summary is `env: "SANDBOX"` or the key starts with `sbx_`. It lists Fake Rails test accounts, auto-fills the rail form, reveals the live OTP/hold/QR/deep-link/redirect data, offers the push/QR/webhook simulator, creates merchant test accounts, shows account movements and can freeze or drain a merchant-owned test account without leaving checkout.
- The Admin Guide context map's `Sandbox` screen covers the Studio and all mirror routes; the guide extractor count is regenerated by `content:guide`.

## 7. Stateful Fake Rails v2

`fake-rails-back/engine/accounts/AccountLedgerService.ts` adds `fake_accounts`, `fake_account_holds`, `fake_account_movements`, `fake_merchant_clearing_pools` and `fake_clearing_entries`. Five default personas are seeded per rail (high balance, standard, low balance 5 LYD, daily-limit-exhausted, frozen), plus ad-hoc auto-enrolment with a 2,500 LYD default.

- INITIATE reserves atomically (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`), checking status, available balance and daily limit.
- SUBMIT/APPROVE captures and credits the per-rail clearing pool; CANCEL/DECLINE/expiry releases.
- REFUND credits the customer and refuses a cumulative refund above the captured amount (`REFUND_EXCEEDS_CAPTURED_AMOUNT`).
- `fake_transactions.account_id`/`held_amount_lyd` link the rail transaction to the account.
- The control plane at `/control/*` is shared with `core-back` (`x-fake-rails-control-token` when configured); the tester portal keeps its JWT.

## 8. Deploy configuration

`deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` adds `SANDBOX_ENABLED` (default false), `SANDBOX_NODE`, `SANDBOX_CORE_PORT` (4005), `SANDBOX_DB_NAME` (`payment_gateway_sandbox`), `SANDBOX_REMOTE_DIR`, `SANDBOX_CORE_BACK_URLS` and `FAKE_RAILS_CONTROL_TOKEN`; validation requires Fake Rails, a distinct database/remote dir/port and HTTPS edge URLs. `sandboxDatabase()` derives the transaction (`pgw_sandbox`) and session (`pgw_sandbox_session`) PgBouncer aliases. `postgres18Provisioner` creates the database and writes both aliases; `hostPlanner` emits a second core `ServicePlan` (`pg-core-sandbox`, port 4005, own release tree, sandbox `DATABASE_URL`/`LEADER_ELECTION_DATABASE_URL`, Fake Rails enabled, backups disabled) on `SANDBOX_NODE` or the first core node, with its own firewall rule and core certificate SAN. `deployService` migrates/seeds that database with the direct sandbox owner URL carrying `app.execution_plane=SANDBOX` (PgBouncer rejects custom startup options, so migrations deliberately bypass the pooler); the seed path runs `db-seed` and `seed-fake-rails`, and the Fake Rails seeder stamps an existing sandbox database row as SANDBOX only when `current_database()` equals `SANDBOX_DB_NAME`. Edges receive the sandbox URL list when enabled. The sandbox database and Fake Rails SQLite are deliberately not backup targets.

## 9. Verification

- Core: `sandboxPlane.test.ts` (plane resolution, token prefixes, boot fence, strict DB fence both directions, Fake Rails gateway fence), `fake-rails-control-client.test.ts`, `phase1-mtls-and-schema.test.ts` (v39 migration is newest), commerce/guard regressions.
- Fake Rails: `accountsAndInspector.test.ts` (personas, reserve/capture/release/refund/over-reserve, auto-enrolment, merchant reset, clearing statement) and the v2 control/inspector tests in `api.test.ts`.
- Edges: `sandbox-routing.test.ts` in merchant-back and admin-back, merchant `sandbox-proxy.test.ts` (control vs resource vs mirror routing). checkout-back routes are covered by its sandbox routing suite.
- Deploy: 708 tests including sandbox database creation, PgBouncer aliases, host planning and PKI SAN; `./deploy.sh --dry-run` shows `pg-core-sandbox :4005`.
- Root unit: guide context map, route-authority coverage and i18n catalogues include the sandbox screens/keys.

## 10. Gaps

See the frontmatter. Deployment now provisions/migrates/seeds the second core and database, and the synthetic clearing statement is ingested through `StatementIngestor`. Remaining: Live-to-sandbox sync of operator-customised reference data (GAP-070), a dedicated Fake Rails challenge table, and sandbox role preview. Both deployment and the full Live mirror require a live two-database run that has not been performed in this workspace.
