```bash
cd admin-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
```

- `admin-back/test/admin-surface.test.ts`: route surface and forwarding behavior.

The tests use a local HTTPS/HTTP stub and do not require PostgreSQL or Redis. A live mTLS check is part of `deploy/lib/healthVerifier.ts`.

## 10. Change history

- 2026-11-03: initial canonical part at `5a24f6f+working-tree`.
- 2026-11-06: removed the arbitrary `page <= 10000` cap from `zListQuery`; the admin journal-entries last-page jump (page 23397 on the stress dataset) was rejected with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` before reaching core. `pageSize` stays capped at 200. Regression test added to `admin-back/test/admin-ui-completion.test.ts`.

## Security hardening (2026-11-05)

- **authorityGuard.** Rejects `alg: none` and non-HS256 tokens and bad signature segment shape; requires `typ`, `iss`, `aud` and `exp` and enforces `exp`/`nbf`. `ADMIN_AUTHORITY_HINTS` (default empty) can only restrict, never skip a guard. Matching is case-sensitive. `requireSession` returns `401 AUTH_INVALID` for tokens that are not live core-shaped sessions. `*` is honoured at the edge; core re-verifies (the edge cannot verify signatures because the key lives in core).
- **Deny-by-default any-of authority lists** on: users, join-requests, kyb-documents, merchants suspend/close, approvals, gateways, gateway-versions, rails, routes, assets, credential-sets, reconciliation, settings (restore-preview is a read, restore-apply a write), audit-logs, operator-cases, gateway-inquiries, attempts, disputes, adjustments, cashouts, commission-profiles, velocity-rules, finance and system/backups. Search, academy, options and stats are left to core.
- **Backups.** Policy cron is validated (5 fields; minimum gaps full 60, delta 5, drill 60 minutes) and `alertLagSeconds` must be >= 1. Retention is NOT floored at the edge: every policy change is a maker-checker proposal, and the maker must be able to propose a low-retention policy for the checker to review. Trigger/drill are rate-limited by `BACKUP_JOB_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (6 per 10 minutes); an `Idempotency-Key` is relayed when supplied, but core has no replay store yet, so it is not an idempotency guarantee.
- **KYB uploads.** Upload runs `assertAllowedUpload` (png/jpeg/pdf) plus zod validation; the content route forces `Content-Disposition: attachment`, a CSP sandbox and a Content-Type allow-list. `logoUrl` must be http(s).
- **Limiters** key on the resolved client IP plus a per-account limiter on login/MFA. Admin `x-pg-min-lsn` is validated (400).
- **Logout and session cookie (GAP-019, RESOLVED 2026-11-05).** `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/logout` (public router, `logoutHandler`) forwards to core `POST /internal/admin/auth/logout`, which revokes the session `jti`, and clears the session cookie. With `SESSION_COOKIE_MODE=true` (default `false`) login and MFA responses move the token into the `pg_admin_session` HttpOnly, `SameSite=Strict` cookie (path `/api/v1/admin`, 12 h, `Secure` unless `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=false`, default `true`) and return `sessionCookie: true` instead of `token` (`captureSessionToken`); the `cookieSession` middleware, mounted first on the admin router, converts the cookie into the `Authorization: Bearer` header only when the mode is on and the caller sent none, and requires `x-pg-csrf: 1` on unsafe methods (`403 CSRF_HEADER_REQUIRED`). Login/MFA are exempt from the cookie conversion so a stale cookie cannot block a new sign-in; logout is outside the auth limiter. Both settings are validated by `admin-back/lib/env`.
- **Session audience and breaker (GAP-020, GAP-021).** The advisory authority guard now requires `aud=payment-gateway-admin`. The core upstream client removes a node from rotation only after `CORE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 3` consecutive failures. Sessions minted before the audience change are rejected and administrators must sign in again.

## Admin UI completion forwards (2026-11-06)

New `coreForward` routes (new files `wallets.ts`, `applications.ts` (applications + `paymentLinksRouter` + `posTerminalsRouter`), `transactions.ts` (transactions + `inboundEventsRouter`), `system.ts`, plus additions to `merchants.ts`, `gateways.ts`, `settings.ts`, `finance.ts`, `aml.ts`) registered in `protected/index.ts` with the same any-of authorities core enforces:

| Mount | Read | Write |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `/wallets` (+ `/:id/statement`, `/:id/audit-events`), `/applications`, `/payment-links`, `/pos-terminals` | `merchant:read` | `merchant:write` |
| `/transactions` | `attempt:read`, `merchant:read`, `finance:read` | n/a |
| `/inbound-events` | `attempt:read`, `case:read` | n/a |
| `/system/*` (jobs-outbox, jobs, outbox, audit-outbox, notifications), mounted after `/system/backups` | `security:read` | `security:write` |
| `/finance/journal-entries`, `/finance/gl-accounts/:id` (+ `/lines`) | `finance:read` | checkpoint, `/shards/scale`, `/shards/:shardId/repair` and `/repair/request` `finance:write` (`/repair-plan` `finance:read`) |
| `/gateways/:id/health` | `gateway:read` | n/a |
| `/settings/notification-templates` | `settings:read` | `settings:write` |
| `/merchants/:id/beneficial-owners`, `/merchants/:id/revalidations` | `merchant:read` or `kyb:read` | `kyb:write` or `merchant:write` (the rest of `/merchants` stays `merchant:write`; `kyb:write` does not unlock suspend) |
| `/aml/reporting-rules/:id/promote`, `/finance/route-caps` | already in core; now forwarded | |

Contracts enforced at the edge: bodies are `.strict()` zod; `reason` is `z.string().trim().min(10).max(500)` (shared `mutationSchemas.ts`; also required on job requeue, notification retry and GL checkpoint); mutation enums are the safe subsets (wallet `FROZEN|ACTIVE`, application `SUSPENDED|ACTIVE`, POS `INACTIVE|BLOCKED|ACTIVE`, link `CANCELLED`); path ids must be UUIDs; list queries pass through every scalar filter. `zListQuery` requires `page >= 1` and caps `pageSize` at 200 but has no upper page bound, so a "last page" jump on a multi-million-row ledger is forwarded instead of failing validation; deep offset pages remain an offset-pagination cost (GAP-006). `relayStatus` passes core's 200/201/202 to the client unchanged (202 = submitted for approval). There is no outbox retry route (core has none).

## Remediation round 2 (2026-11-08): limiters, uploads, invitation routes

`api/public/auth.ts` wires `createAccountLimiters` (per `identifier|ip` and an identifier ceiling, failures only) and the public `POST /auth/accept-invitation` route; `api/upload.ts` exports `uploadGuards` (limiter, `Content-Length` pre-check, session-shape check before multer) and is used by the reconciliation and join-request uploads; `api/protected/users.ts` and `api/contract.ts` carry the invitation-based create and re-invite contracts (no password or phone in the create body).

## Report engine forwards (2026-11-10)

`/api/v1/admin/report-engine/*` forwards the core report-engine routes. The catalog forwards `audience`, `page`, `pageSize`, `search`, `sortKey` and `sortDirection`; the chrome registry forwards `type`, `includeArchived`, `page`, `pageSize`, `search`, `sortKey` and `sortDirection`; and `POST /chrome/:id/archive` is proxied. The edge authority guard accepts `report:review`, `report:approve`, `report_engine:author`, `report_engine:run`, `gateway:write`, `security:read`, `security:write` and `reports.draft` for reads, and `report:approve`, `report_engine:author`, `report:review`, `security:write` and `reports.draft` for writes.

## Reporting Studio, incidents and filing adapters (2026-11-10)

`admin-back/api/protected/aml.ts` forwards the new reporting surface to core; every route remains behind `requireAuthorities("COMPLIANCE", "MLRO", "aml:read", "aml:write")` and core re-checks the authority:

- template/studio: `POST /report-schemas/:id/template/analyze`, `POST /report-schemas/:id/template/upload`, `DELETE /report-schemas/:id/template`, `GET|PUT /report-schemas/:id/template`, `POST /report-schemas/:id/workbook/preview`; the XML/XLSX/DOCX schema enums accept `DOCX`.
- rule bindings: `PUT /reporting-rules/:id/schema-bindings` relays the core 202 (approval request), not 200.
- incidents: list/create/detail/update and transition, timeline, responders and responder acknowledgement/release, actions, links, communications and `POST /incidents/:id/report`.
- filing: `GET|POST|PATCH|DELETE /filing-adapters`, `GET /reports/:id/submissions` and `POST /reports/:id/file`; file relays core's 202/502 status and never exposes the adapter secret.

The edge validates identifiers, enums and body shapes, but keeps the core as the authority for maker-checker, schema lifecycle, output readiness and adapter authority matching.

## Final AML forwarding sweep (2026-11-10)

- `GET /aml/incidents` now has an explicit query schema and forwards `search`, `page`, `pageSize`, `status`, `severity` and `category`; without it `coreForward` dropped every filter.
- Incident writes, filing-adapter create/update/disable and `POST /reports/:id/file` relay core's 202 instead of returning a false 200.
- The new AML routes remain behind the shared `amlConfidential` guard; the edge only validates shapes while core remains the authority for maker-checker, submission readiness and adapter matching.

## Object & asset storage proxy

`admin-back/api/protected/objectStorage.ts` forwards the console API:
`GET /object-storage/summary`, `GET /object-storage/objects`,
`GET /object-storage/objects/:id`, `GET /object-storage/access-logs`,
`POST|DELETE /object-storage/objects/:id/legal-hold` and
`POST /object-storage/maintenance/:job`. It is mounted with
`system:storage:read`/`system:storage:admin`/`system:storage:legal-hold`
read/write guards. `assetsRouter` additionally exposes binary
`POST /assets/upload` (multipart `file` + `name`) and
`GET /assets/:id/content`, forwarding raw bytes to core.

## v38-v39 sandbox proxy (2026-11-13)

`/api/v1/admin/sandbox/*` forwards only to `SANDBOX_CORE_BACK_URLS` (no Live fallback): overview, per-merchant overview/reset, wallet balance, global reset and Fake Rails accounts/clearing/scenarios/transactions/webhooks/statements. `/mirror/*` raw-forwards to `/internal/admin/*` for the Live-parity pages; report-engine mirror bodies use the 24 MB parser. The staff session is mirrored by the sandbox core. The Studio routes are open to signed-in staff; the sandbox data is isolated. An unconfigured sandbox node answers `503 SANDBOX_NODE_UNAVAILABLE`.

<a id="edgemerchant"></a>

> **Part ID:** `edge.merchant` · **Status:** `partial` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-13 · **Verified against:** `5a24f6f+working-tree`

# Merchant Edge BFF

## 1. Purpose and scope

`merchant-back` is the public merchant edge. One Bun/Express process serves two audiences:

- the authenticated merchant portal under `/api/v1/merchant/*`;
- the merchant server API under `/api/v1/external/*`, authenticated by a `pg_live_` bearer token and a core-side IP allowlist.

It owns request validation, edge translation to the canonical core contract, upload verification, rate limiting, the public merchant API shape and mTLS forwarding to `/internal/merchant/*`. It owns no database connection, no Prisma client, no `DATABASE_URL`, no `KMS_MASTER_KEY` and no authority decisions.

The merchant vhost serves the SPA through Nginx. The backend itself binds to loopback in deployment.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The design splits the merchant experience into a portal API and a server-to-server API. The portal covers registration, identity verification, login/MFA, KYB onboarding, wallets, applications, links, POS terminals and cashier screens, payments, disputes, cash-outs, API tokens, credential sets, team users and overview statistics. The external API covers link creation/inspection/cancellation and payment lookup using a long-lived merchant token.

All operations are forwarded over mTLS 1.3 with `CN=merchant-back`. The edge validates multipart KYB documents for MIME type, magic bytes and size before forwarding raw bytes to core. The portal may accept amounts and currencies when the merchant owns link creation; the edge never performs money arithmetic and core re-validates every monetary field. The external API is meant to enforce a `pg_live_` bearer token and an IP allowlist, with core as the authority.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Process, listener and middleware

`merchant-back/index.ts`:

- disables `x-powered-by`;
- sets `trust proxy` to false;
- emits no CORS headers unless `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is set (no credentials), plus hand-written security headers;
- installs request logging;
- serves unauthenticated `GET /health`;
- parses JSON and URL-encoded bodies with `MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES`;
- mounts `/api/v1`;
- adds the shared 404 and error handlers.

The listener binds to `BIND_HOST` (default `0.0.0.0` in the service schema). The deploy engine overrides this to `127.0.0.1`; direct exposure of port 4102 is a configuration error.

Middleware layers:

| Layer | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- |
| `authLimiter` | Fixed 15-minute window, `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 20), on `/api/v1/merchant/auth`. |
| `onboardingLimiter` | 60-second window, `API_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 300), on `/api/v1/merchant/onboarding`. |
| `apiLimiter` | 60-second window, `API_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 300), on the protected merchant router. |
| `externalLimiter` | 60-second window, `EXTERNAL_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 120), on `/api/v1/external`. |
| `requirePgLiveToken` | Requires `Authorization: Bearer pg_live_...` by prefix only. Applied to the whole external router. |
| `coreForward` `requireAuth` | Rejects a missing `Authorization` header for protected portal routes. Defaults to required; auth/onboarding routes opt out with `requireAuth: false`. |
| `requireBearer` | Helper used by dispute evidence and merchant user routes to require a header before multipart work. |
| `requireAuthHeader` | Exported from `api/public/auth.ts` but a no-op; it is not a security control. |

There is no edge session parser, role guard or token verifier in `merchant-back`. An arbitrary non-empty bearer token reaches core for every protected portal route.

### 3.2 Forwarding behavior

`merchant-back/api/forward.ts` implements a stricter forwarder than admin's:

1. Requires `Authorization` unless `requireAuth === false`.
2. Validates route params and query with Zod.
3. Validates the public body with `schema`.
4. Applies `bodyMapper()` to translate product vocabulary into the core body.
5. Applies `bodyFrom()` when the route replaces the body entirely.
6. Re-validates the translated body with `coreSchema` when configured, so a request that core would reject is stopped at the edge.
7. Calls `callCoreResponse()` with request id, resolved client IP, user agent and the bearer token.
8. Returns the core body with the declared status, or the core status when `relayStatus: true`.

The external router also has its own PG-live prefix check. It does not hash or validate the token; core does the authoritative token lookup and IP check.

### 3.3 Uploads

`merchant-back/api/upload.ts` uses Multer memory storage with `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`, one file and at most 32 fields. `forwardUpload()` and the dispute route call `assertAllowedUpload()`:

- checks the declared MIME type against `UPLOAD_ALLOWED_MIME`;
- checks magic bytes for PNG (`89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`), JPEG (`FF D8 FF`) and PDF (`25 50 44 46 2D`);
- enforces the size cap;
- computes SHA-256;
- forwards raw bytes with `x-upload-filename`, `x-upload-content-type`, `x-upload-sha256`, `x-upload-size` and base64url `x-upload-metadata`.

Dispute evidence is converted into a canonical JSON body (`toCoreDisputeEvidence`) rather than raw bytes. The max evidence size is defined in `merchant-back/api/contract.ts`.

### 3.4 Route map

Portal auth is mounted under `/api/v1/merchant/auth`:

| Method | Path |
| :--- | :--- |
| POST | `/register`, `/verify-identity`, `/accept-invitation`, `/login`, `/google`, `/mfa/verify` |
| GET | `/me` |

Onboarding is mounted under `/api/v1/merchant/onboarding`:

| Method | Path |
| :--- | :--- |
| GET, PUT | `/join-request` |
| GET | `/kyb-revalidations`, `/beneficial-owners` |
| POST | `/kyb-documents` (multipart), `/beneficial-owners`, `/submit` |
| DELETE | `/beneficial-owners/:id` |

The protected portal API is mounted under `/api/v1/merchant`:

| Area | Routes |
| :--- | :--- |
| Wallets | `GET, POST /wallets`, `GET /wallets/:id`, `GET /wallets/:id/balance`, `GET /wallets/:id/statements`, `GET /wallets/:id/statements/:month/export` |
| Applications | `GET, POST /applications`, `GET, PATCH /applications/:id` |
| Links | `GET, POST /links`, `GET /links/:id`, `POST /links/:id/cancel`, `GET /links/:id/attempts` |
| POS | `GET, POST /pos/terminals`, `GET, PATCH /pos/terminals/:id`, `POST /pos/terminals/:id/screens`, `GET /pos/screens/:screenCode/stream` (SSE) |
| Payments | `GET /payments` |
| Disputes | `GET /disputes`, `GET /disputes/:id`, `POST /disputes/:id/evidence` (multipart) |
| Cash-outs | `GET, POST /cashouts` |
| Tokens | `GET, POST /tokens`, `PUT /tokens/:id/ips`, `DELETE /tokens/:id` |
| Credential sets | `GET, POST /credential-sets`, `GET, PUT /credential-sets/:id` |
| Team | `GET, POST, PATCH /users`, `PATCH /users/:id` |
| Stats | `GET /stats/overview` |

`merchant-back/api/protected/options.ts` exports `optionsRouter` for `GET /options/:kind`, but the router is not imported by `api/protected/index.ts` and has no live mount.

The external merchant server API is mounted under `/api/v1/external`:

| Method | Path |
| :--- | :--- |
| POST | `/links`, `/links/:key/cancel` |
| GET | `/links/:key`, `/payments/:reference` |

### 3.5 Authentication behavior and the Google gap

Portal auth routes are public at the edge (`requireAuth: false`) and forward to `/internal/merchant/auth/*`:

- `POST /register` validates phone/email, password, name and optional identity fields, then creates a registration.
- `POST /verify-identity` is retired: core always answers `410 IDENTITY_VERIFICATION_RETIRED`.
- `POST /accept-invitation` validates an invitation token and password.
- `POST /login` validates an identifier and password.
- `POST /google` validates a Google `idToken` shape and forwards it, but `core-back` answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` with `Google sign-in requires a configured OIDC provider` (`core-back/api/internal/merchant.ts:853`). The capability is not implemented at the core.
- `GET /me` and `POST /mfa/verify` forward the supplied bearer/challenge state to core.

The merchant portal session is a core-issued token. The edge never verifies its signature, expiry, revocation, MFA state or merchant status. Core verifies the signature, expiry, user status and authorities; it does not re-check MFA or a session revocation list on every call.

## 4. Contracts and invariants

- All portal business routes require an `Authorization` header at the edge; its validity is decided by core.
- The external API requires a `pg_live_` prefix at the edge; access-token validity, revocation and source-IP allowlist are decided by core.
- Every forwarded path stays under `/internal/merchant`; the shared client enforces this and core re-checks `CN=merchant-back`.
- The edge never accepts arbitrary core paths.
- Link creation accepts decimal-string amounts and ISO 4217 currencies; the edge does not do arithmetic and core re-validates amount, currency and fee model.
- Checkout money semantics do not apply here: merchant link creation is an owning operation.
- Uploaded KYB and dispute files are validated for MIME, magic bytes and size before the core call.
- Team/user and credential-set operations are forwarded with the caller's bearer token; the core enforces merchant roles and maker-checker where applicable.
- The POS SSE route requires a bearer header, then proxies the core stream.
- List queries accept any positive `page` (no arbitrary upper bound) and cap `pageSize` at 200, so deep pages on large merchant datasets are forwarded rather than rejected with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`; deep offset pages remain an offset-pagination cost (GAP-006).

## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface

### Environment

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NODE_ENV` | `development` | Runtime mode. |
| `PORT` | `4102` | Backend listener port. |
| `BIND_HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address; deploy overrides to `127.0.0.1`. |
| `CORE_BACK_URL` | required | First core node, absolute HTTPS. |
| `CORE_BACK_URLS` | optional | Core pool. |
| `MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH`, `MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_PATH`, `MTLS_CA_CERT_PATH` | required | Edge mTLS material. |
| `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | `30000` | Core request timeout. |
| `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` | loopback only (`127.0.0.0/8,::1/128`) | Trusted forwarded-IP peers. |
| `MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES` | `2097152` | JSON limit. |
| `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | `10485760` | Multipart limit. |
| `UPLOAD_ALLOWED_MIME` | `image/png,image/jpeg,application/pdf` | Allowed upload MIME types. |
| `PG_LIVE_TOKEN_PREFIX` | `pg_live_` | External API bearer prefix. |
| `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` | `20`, `900000` | Auth limiter maximum and configured window (window is not used; 15 minutes is fixed). |
| `API_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, `API_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` | `300`, `60000` | Portal/onboarding limiter. |
| `EXTERNAL_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, `EXTERNAL_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` | `120`, `60000` | External API limiter. |
| `POS_STREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` | `900000` | POS SSE proxy timeout. |

### Deployment surface

`deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts` writes `BIND_HOST=127.0.0.1`, `PG_LIVE_TOKEN_PREFIX=pg_live_`, the core URL list and mTLS paths. The public merchant vhost proxies `/api/` to `127.0.0.1:4102` with `client_max_body_size` sized for KYB uploads and buffering disabled for the POS stream. The edge `.env` has no database or KMS secret.

## 6. Operational usage

```bash
cd merchant-back
bun install
bun run start
bun run dev
bun test
bun run typecheck
```

- Public reachability is through `https://merchant.<domain>/api`; the backend port must stay loopback-only.
- For POS issues, verify the Nginx stream route disables buffering and the proxy read timeout exceeds the cashier idle window.
- For upload failures, check `UPLOAD_ALLOWED_MIME`, magic bytes, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` and the core-side upload limits.
- For external API `401 INVALID_API_TOKEN`, the edge did not see a `pg_live_` bearer; for a core rejection, inspect the core token/IP state.
- Google login currently returns 501 by design of the core; use password or invitation flows.

## 7. Status and deviations

### Implemented

- Two-audience routing with separate rate limits and external token prefix gate.
- Full portal and external route surface, including multipart KYB and evidence uploads.
- Public-to-core schema validation and canonical body mapping.
- MIME/magic-byte/size validation and hashed raw upload forwarding.
- mTLS pool, retries, LSN header propagation and channel confinement.
- POS SSE proxy with buffering disabled.

### Partial

- Portal authentication is only a presence check at the edge; all session and authority enforcement is in core.
- External token validation is prefix-only at the edge.
- Google sign-in is exposed but not implemented by core.

### Missing / deferred

- Google OIDC provider integration in core.
- Edge session revocation/MFA cache.
- Route-level merchant role guards at the edge.
- A live `GET /options/:kind` mount for the merchant portal.
- SSE resume/replay or polling fallback at the edge.

### Known bugs / risks

- `requireAuthHeader` is a no-op and should not be mistaken for a guard.
- The auth limiter uses a hard-coded 15-minute window; `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` has no effect.
- (Superseded) `resolveClientIp` now honours forwarded headers only from trusted peers, requires a single valid IP and prefers `x-real-ip` over `x-real-client-ip`; the edge always overwrites `x-real-client-ip` towards core. Historical note: `x-real-client-ip` was preferred over `x-real-ip` in `merchant-back/lib/net/index.ts`. When the backend is loopback-bound this is safe; if it is ever exposed and a direct peer is inside `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, the peer can spoof its client IP.
- The options router is dead code; a frontend calling `/api/v1/merchant/options/:kind` receives a 404.
- The external prefix check is not a credential check; do not log or expose token values.

## 8. Verification and tests

```bash
cd merchant-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
```

Key suites:

- `merchant-back/test/core-forwarding.test.ts`: forwarding, status relay and body handling.
- `merchant-back/test/core-contract.test.ts`: public-to-core mappers and canonical schemas.
- `merchant-back/test/core-internal-client.test.ts`: pool and consistency behavior.
- `merchant-back/test/mtls-client.test.ts`: channel confinement and error mapping.
- `merchant-back/test/merchant-kyb-and-external.test.ts`: upload validation and external API behavior.
- `merchant-back/test/env-isolation.test.ts`: no database/KMS material at the edge.

These suites do not require PostgreSQL or Redis. The Google route is expected to forward and surface core's 501; a successful Google login has no implementation to test.

## 10. Change history

- 2026-11-03: initial canonical part at `5a24f6f+working-tree`.
- 2026-11-06: removed the arbitrary `page <= 10000` cap from `zListQuery` and the five list query schemas that duplicated it (`payments`, `links`, `cashouts`, `disputes`, wallet statements); `pageSize` stays capped at 200. Regression tests forward page 23397 on all six merchant list routes.

## 11. Cross-node POS updates (2026-11-03)

The core POS SSE stream now subscribes to the Redis-backed `realtime:attempt` and `realtime:pos` topics. A cashier request processed by a merchant-back/core pair on one host reaches a paired screen whose stream is held by a merchant-back node on the other host. The existing 3-second database poll remains as a fallback.

## Security hardening (2026-11-05)

- **Token creation.** Malformed CIDRs and ranges broader than /8 (IPv4) or /32 (IPv6) are rejected. Scopes are lowercase `resource:action`, unique, at most `TOKEN_MAX_SCOPES` (20); core restricts them further to `link:write`, `link:read`, `payment:read`. `expiresAt` must be a future ISO date within `TOKEN_MAX_TTL_DAYS` (365); default `TOKEN_DEFAULT_TTL_DAYS` (90). `pg_live_` tokens must be `pg_live_` plus 43 base64url characters.
- **External limiter** keys on token hash plus IP.
- **Uploads** require a bearer token and Content-Length (`411`) and are size-checked (`413`) before buffering; `UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` applies. Website fields accept http(s) only.
- **Cash-out create** keeps and forwards `idempotencyKey` (body or `Idempotency-Key` header) to core.
- **Auth** POSTs have a per-account limiter in addition to the per-IP limiter. `/verify-identity` is retired (410).
- Redaction and `redactUrl` cover PII keys and path tokens.

## Gap resolutions (2026-11-05)

- **Logout and session cookie (GAP-019, RESOLVED).** `POST /api/v1/merchant/auth/logout` forwards to core `POST /internal/merchant/auth/logout` (session `jti` revocation) and clears the cookie. `SESSION_COOKIE_MODE` (default `false`) and `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` (default `true`) are validated in `merchant-back/lib/env`; in cookie mode the token is set as the `pg_merchant_session` HttpOnly, `SameSite=Strict` cookie (path `/api/v1/merchant`, 12 h), the body carries `sessionCookie: true`, and cookie-authenticated writes require `x-pg-csrf: 1`. The cookie is ignored when the mode is off; login/MFA are exempt from the CSRF conversion so a stale cookie cannot block sign-in. The mode is off by default.
- **Audience and breaker (GAP-020, GAP-021).** Merchant sessions carry `aud=payment-gateway-merchant`; a session minted for another channel is refused by core (`401 SESSION_AUDIENCE_INVALID`). The upstream client uses `CORE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 3`.

## Remediation round 2 (2026-11-08): limiters and session shape

`lib/authLimiters.ts` mirrors the admin account limiters; `lib/security/sessionCookie.ts` exports `assertMerchantSessionShape`, which `api/upload.ts` applies (with the existing limiter and size cap) before any body is buffered.

## 8. Merchant report proxy (2026-11-10)

`merchant-back/api/protected/reportEngine.ts` is mounted at `/report-engine` and forwards:

- `GET /catalog` to `/internal/merchant/report-engine/catalog`, forwarding `page`, `pageSize`, `search`, `sortKey` and `sortDirection`;
- `GET /autocomplete/:sourceKey` to the merchant autocomplete route;
- `POST /catalog/:code/execute` to the merchant execute route.

The edge validates the catalog query shape and the public execute shape (`inputs`, `locale`, `renderMode`). Core enforces the merchant authority, audience scope, forced merchant ID and report safety. A client-supplied merchant ID is rejected by the strict edge schema and would be overwritten by core even if it reached it.


## Dispute attachments

`GET/POST /api/v1/merchant/disputes/:id/attachments`, `GET .../:attachmentId/content` and `DELETE .../:attachmentId` proxy the shared-vault evidence routes. Uploads use the raw-byte forwarder; content uses the streaming proxy. Downloads are refused by core while the object is quarantined.

## v38-v39 sandbox namespace (2026-11-13)

`/api/v1/merchant/sandbox/*` is a dedicated namespace forwarded only to `SANDBOX_CORE_BACK_URLS`. `/overview`, `/seed-demo`, `/seed-history`, `/reset`, `/wallets/:id/*`, `/payments/:id/*`, `/disputes/:id/resolve`, `/reconciliation/*`, `/fake-rails/*` and `/webhooks/test-ping` map to the sandbox control routes; list/create resources (`/wallets`, `/applications`, `/links`, `/payments`, `/tokens`) map to the sandbox core's `/internal/merchant/*` (same router, separate database). `/mirror/*` raw-forwards to `/internal/merchant/*` for Live-parity pages, including a dedicated multipart dispute-evidence route and the POS SSE stream. `/api/external/v1/*` accepts `pg_live_*` and `pg_test_*` and selects the Live or Sandbox pool from the prefix. The client keeps one pool per URL set, so failover cannot cross planes.

<a id="edgecheckout"></a>

> **Part ID:** `edge.checkout` · **Status:** `partial` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-13 · **Verified against:** `5a24f6f+working-tree`

# Checkout Edge BFF

## 1. Purpose and scope

`checkout-back` is the public checkout and inbound-webhook edge. It serves anonymous payers and external payment gateways:

- payer link resolution and attempt lifecycle under `/api/v1/pay/*`;
- the checkout status SSE stream;
- browser return handling under `/api/v1/return/*`;
- raw inbound gateway webhooks under `/api/v1/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken`.

It owns edge schema validation, the zero-monetary-field assertion, raw webhook capture, header allowlisting, environment translation, client IP propagation, rate limiting, redirect construction and mTLS forwarding to `/internal/checkout/*`. It owns no database, no session, no money resolution and no gateway signature verification.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The checkout edge is deliberately read/execute-only. A payer can select a rail and submit form data, but can never create a link, change a link or supply an amount or currency. `core-back` resolves money from `payment_links` by `linkKey`.

Inbound webhooks are treated as untrusted. The design calls for capturing the raw bytes and headers, forwarding them unchanged to the core inbox, and returning the gateway's configured ack quickly. The core verifies the signature, IP allowlist and replay window. The design's blueprint says the inbox returns the ack in under 10 ms; the as-built core performs verification inline before acking.

The return URL is an untrusted browser hint. Core inspects the attempt, triggers an inquiry where appropriate, and the edge redirects the browser to the checkout status page.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Process and mount order

`checkout-back/index.ts`:

- disables `x-powered-by`;
- sets `trust proxy` to false;
- emits no CORS headers unless `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is set (same-origin by default; credentials disabled), plus hand-written security headers;
- installs request logging;
- serves unauthenticated `GET /health`;
- mounts `/api/v1/inbound` with `inboundRouter` **before** the JSON body parser, so the inbound router can install its own raw parser;
- then installs JSON and URL-encoded parsers (`MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES`);
- mounts `/api/v1` with the pay and return routers;
- adds the shared 404 and error handlers.

The listener binds to `BIND_HOST` (default `0.0.0.0`). The deploy engine writes `127.0.0.1`; Nginx is the public listener.

### 3.2 Middleware and guards

| Layer | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- |
| `payLimiter` | 60-second window, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 120), on the pay router. |
| `returnLimiter` | 60-second window, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, on the return router. |
| `inboundLimiter` | 60-second window, `INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 600), on the inbound router. |
| Raw parser | `express.raw({ type: () => true, limit: MAX_INBOUND_BODY_BYTES })`, applied after the inbound limiter; only GET/HEAD/POST are accepted; parser errors return 413/400. |
| `assertNoMonetaryFields` | Recursively rejects forbidden monetary keys (amount, currency, total, fee, commission, price, net/gross/debit/credit amounts, and close variants) with `400 AMOUNT_NOT_ACCEPTED`. Applied to initiate, confirm, resend, cancel and client-event. |
| Schema validation | Zod schemas for link keys, attempt ids, rail codes, sub-modes, form data, OTPs, evidence, idempotency keys and client events. |
| Header allowlist | Inbound forwards only `content-type`, `user-agent`, `x-signature`, `x-gateway-signature`, `x-hub-signature-256`, `x-moomalat-signature`, `x-timestamp` and `x-nonce`. `content-length` is deliberately NOT forwarded (2026-11-08): `express.raw` inflates gzip/deflate/br/zstd bodies, so the inbound length no longer describes the bytes the edge writes to core; forwarding it let the surplus be parsed as the next request on the pooled keep-alive connection (request smuggling). The shared client now also drops caller-supplied framing/hop-by-hop headers and computes `content-length` from the real body. |
| Environment translation | `sandbox`, `test`, `uat` map to core `SANDBOX`; `live`, `production` map to `LIVE`; anything else is rejected. |

There is no edge authentication. Anonymous payers and external gateways are the intended callers. The link key, attempt id/token, OTP and idempotency key are the edge-visible capabilities; core validates each against database state.

### 3.3 Forwarding behavior

Payer routes call `callCore()` directly with a method, path, body and context. They do not use a generic forwarder. The context includes the request id, resolved client IP, user agent and no bearer token.

`GET /pay/:linkKey` resolves public link data. `POST /initiate` validates the rail code, optional sub-mode, form data and idempotency key, then forwards. `GET /logs/:attemptId` returns public attempt state. `POST /confirm`, `/resend`, `/cancel` and `/client-event` validate their schemas and forward.

`GET /pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/status` calls `proxyCoreStream()` with a 10-minute timeout. The core endpoint itself polls PostgreSQL every 2 seconds, emits an SSE `status` event when the status changes, and ends on a terminal status or after the deadline. The edge retries a failed stream handshake on another core node but cannot resume an established stream.

Inbound `ANY /inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken`:

1. Validates the gateway identifier, environment and path token shape.
2. Reads the raw `Buffer` and the original `content-type`.
3. Translates the environment.
4. Calls `callCoreRaw()` with method, raw bytes, content type, allowlisted headers, request id, client IP and a 10-second timeout.
5. Relays the core status code, content type and body.

The edge does not parse the webhook body, compute a signature, or decide whether the event is genuine. Core stores the event, resolves the channel and attempt, performs synchronous verification, updates the event and then returns the channel ack status/body. If core returns an error, the edge relays it; no local ack is fabricated.

Browser return `GET|POST /return/:attemptToken`:

- validates the attempt token;
- calls core with the query for GET or `{ hint: "browser_return" }` for POST;
- builds `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL` + `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH` with `attempt_token` and an optional `reference`;
- redirects with 302.

### 3.4 Route map

| Method | Edge path | Core path |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| GET | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey` | `GET /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey` |
| POST | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/initiate` | `POST /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/initiate` |
| GET | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId` | `GET /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId` |
| GET | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/status` | SSE proxy of `GET /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/status` |
| POST | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/confirm` | `POST /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/confirm` |
| POST | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/resend` | `POST /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/resend` |
| POST | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/cancel` | `POST /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/cancel` |
| POST | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/client-event` | `POST /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/client-event` |
| ANY | `/api/v1/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken` | `ANY /internal/checkout/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken` (raw bytes) |
| GET, POST | `/api/v1/return/:attemptToken` | `GET, POST /internal/checkout/return/:attemptToken` |

## 4. Contracts and invariants

- No payer schema accepts `amount`, `currency` or any normalized monetary field. The recursive assertion rejects nested occurrences before forwarding.
- The payer can submit only the link key, rail code, sub-mode, form data, idempotency key, OTP and untrusted client event hints.
- The edge never resolves money, fees or currency; core reads the authoritative link.
- Inbound bodies are forwarded byte for byte. The edge must not normalize JSON or re-encode forms.
- Only the allowlisted inbound headers cross the boundary. `authorization`, `cookie` and arbitrary `x-*` headers are dropped.
- Core is the only place where gateway signatures, replay windows, IP allowlists and channel/environment bindings are verified.
- Client event aliases (`COMPLETE_CALLBACK`, `ERROR_CALLBACK`, widget aliases) are normalized to `completeCallback`, `errorCallback`, `widgetEvent` and `returnHint`.
- The return redirect destination comes only from configured `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL` and `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH`, not from client input.
- SSE responses must disable buffering; Nginx sets `proxy_buffering off` for the status route.

## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface

### Environment

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NODE_ENV` | `development` | Runtime mode. |
| `PORT` | `4103` | Backend listener port. |
| `BIND_HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address; deploy overrides to `127.0.0.1`. |
| `CORE_BACK_URL` | required | First core node, absolute HTTPS. |
| `CORE_BACK_URLS` | optional | Core pool. |
| `MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH`, `MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_PATH`, `MTLS_CA_CERT_PATH` | required | Edge mTLS material. |
| `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | `30000` | Default core timeout (inbound explicitly uses 10 seconds). |
| `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` | loopback only (`127.0.0.0/8,::1/128`) | Trusted forwarded-IP peers. |
| `MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES` | `1048576` | JSON limit. |
| `MAX_INBOUND_BODY_BYTES` | `1048576` | Raw webhook limit (was 3 MiB). |
| `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:5103` | Redirect base. |
| `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH` | `/pay/status` | Redirect path. |
| `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` | `120`, `60000` | Pay and return limiters. |
| `INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, `INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` | `600`, `60000` | Inbound limiter. |

### Deployment surface

`deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts` writes `BIND_HOST=127.0.0.1`, `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL=https://<CHECKOUT_DOMAIN>` and `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH=/pay/status`. The checkout Nginx vhost proxies `/api/` to `127.0.0.1:4103`, disables buffering for the SSE route, and applies `client_max_body_size` sized for the inbound raw limit. The edge `.env` contains no database or KMS secret.

## 6. Operational usage

```bash
cd checkout-back
bun install
bun run start
bun run dev
bun test
bun run typecheck
```

- Public reachability is through `https://pay.<domain>/api`; port 4103 stays loopback-only.
- To test a webhook locally, send the exact gateway bytes and signature headers to the inbound route. The edge preserves bytes and the allowlisted headers; the core verification result determines the processing outcome.
- A gateway retry is expected after a non-2xx edge/core response. Dedupe is by `channel.id + SHA-256(rawBody)` in core; the edge does not dedupe.
- For SSE problems, check Nginx buffering, the core 10-minute deadline and the 2-second poll interval. The edge does not send keepalive comments of its own.
- For a redirect loop, verify `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL` and `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH`.

## 7. Status and deviations

### Implemented

- Public pay, return, SSE and inbound route surface.
- Zero-monetary-field assertion with nested scanning.
- Raw inbound capture with byte preservation and strict header allowlist.
- Environment and client-event vocabulary translation.
- Core pool, retries, LSN propagation and channel confinement.
- Rate limits per route family.
- Browser redirect to the configured checkout status page.

### Partial

- Inbound webhooks are processed synchronously. The design describes a queue-and-fast-ack inbox; the code stores the event, runs verification inline, updates the event and only then ack's.
- SSE is a core-side database poller, not a transition-bus subscription.
- The edge's stream retry covers handshake failure only.

### Missing / deferred

- Asynchronous webhook verification with a fast ack.
- Stream resume/replay, `Last-Event-ID` support or a polling fallback.
- Edge-side operational or diagnostic routes.
- Signature pre-validation at the edge (intentionally left to core).

### Known bugs / risks

- The 10-second inbound timeout can return `504 CORE_TIMEOUT` while core continues writing the event and processing it. The gateway may retry; core dedupe should suppress duplicate effects, but the observable response is ambiguous.
- Synchronous verification puts crypto, IP lookup and replay checks on the webhook request path, so a slow verification consumes the gateway's timeout budget and an inbound worker.
- If the core ack status or body is misconfigured, the edge faithfully relays it; there is no fallback ack.
- The return handler issues a 302 after core responds. A core error is surfaced as an error response, not a redirect with an error state.
- `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL` accepts HTTP or HTTPS in the edge schema. In production it should be HTTPS.
- The default `BIND_HOST` is `0.0.0.0`; only the deploy engine's override to loopback prevents direct exposure.

## 8. Verification and tests

```bash
cd checkout-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
```

Key suites:

- `checkout-back/test/checkout-zero-trust.test.ts`: no amount/currency acceptance, field rejection and translation.
- `checkout-back/test/core-internal-client.test.ts`: pool, retry, headers and LSN.
- `checkout-back/test/mtls-client.test.ts`: channel confinement and error mapping.
- `checkout-back/test/error-and-logger.test.ts`: error envelopes and request logging.
- `checkout-back/test/env-isolation.test.ts`: no database/KMS material at the edge.
- `checkout-back/test/exhaustive/05-api-matrix/checkout-zero-trust-matrix.test.ts`: route matrix.

The suites are local and do not require PostgreSQL/Redis. A live gateway webhook requires the core, a configured channel and the gateway signature fixture.

## 10. Change history

- 2026-11-03: initial canonical part at `5a24f6f+working-tree`.

## 11. Cross-node SSE bridge (2026-11-03)

- `core-back` republishes every `attempt:transition` event on the Redis-backed `realtime:attempt` topic.
- The checkout status stream subscribes to that topic and emits `event: status` immediately; the existing 2-second database poll remains as a fallback.
- The merchant POS stream subscribes to `realtime:attempt` and `realtime:pos`, filtering by merchant id, so a screen on one host receives an update processed by a core node on the other host.

## Security hardening (2026-11-05)

- **Inbound.** The limiter runs before the raw body parser; buckets are per resolved IP plus channel and a coarse per-IP bucket (5x). Only GET/HEAD/POST; body limit `MAX_INBOUND_BODY_BYTES` default 1 MiB (was 3 MiB); body-parser errors return 413/400. Core errors map to public codes `INBOUND_REJECTED`, `INBOUND_NOT_FOUND`, `INBOUND_CONFLICT`, `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `INBOUND_UNAVAILABLE`; 401/403/404/410 collapse to 404.
- **Pay routes.** Confirm accepts only `otp` (evidence ignored); BLOCK/HOLD responses carry no internal reasons.
- **Window envs** `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` and `INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` are wired. Redaction masks link keys, attempt tokens, `/logs/` ids and inbound path tokens in logs.

## Gap resolutions (2026-11-05)

- The checkout upstream client uses the same `CORE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 3` consecutive-failure threshold before a core node leaves rotation (GAP-021). Checkout sessions use the `payment-gateway-checkout` audience (GAP-020).

## v38 sandbox checkout (2026-11-13)

`sbx_*` link keys and `SANDBOX` inbound environments select `SANDBOX_CORE_BACK_URLS`; `pl_*` and LIVE inbound stay on the Live pool. The inspector routes list accounts, patch an account balance/status and reveal/simulate an attempt; all refuse a non-`sbx_` key with `403`. An unconfigured sandbox node is `503 SANDBOX_NODE_UNAVAILABLE`, never a silent Live fallback.

# Admin UI System

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part owns the design system and shell used by `admin-front`: visual tokens, self-hosted fonts, Vuetify theme/default configuration, the 13 required UI primitives and their extras, the 248 px navigation drawer and 56 px app bar, the split-screen authentication layout, and the cross-workspace rollout rules.

It does not own page-specific business logic, route authority decisions, table data contracts, or the guide content. Those are covered by `01-route-and-page-catalog.md`, `02-tables-filters-exports.md`, and `03-guide-and-academy.md`. It also does not replace the per-service rendering rules in the merchant and checkout parts.

The system is shared by four Vue 3 + Vuetify 3 TSX applications at different levels of adoption:

| Workspace | Adoption |
| :--- | :--- |
| `admin-front` | Full reference implementation: tokens, fonts, primitives, shell, table surface, compliance gate. |
| `merchant-front` | Mirrors tokens, fonts, Vuetify defaults, primitives, table surface, and the 248/56 shell with merchant navigation. |
| `checkout-front` | Uses tokens, fonts, Vuetify defaults, and a focused payer layout; it does not use the admin shell or the full navigation system. |
| `fake-rails-front` | Partial rollout: fonts, tokens, UI primitives, tables, row actions, and `SectionFields` exist, but it keeps its own portal/hosted layouts and is outside the admin compliance test. |

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The historical UI design starts from an anti-"AI-generated UI" premise. The target is a restrained fintech back office: a neutral canvas, hairline borders, flat surfaces, tabular numerals, a single semantic status dot or primary action, and no decorative gradients or stacked card shadows.

The key intent from `design/90-archive/superseded-ui/portal_ui_abstraction_and_modern_fintech_redesign.md` and `design/06-ui/portal_ui_abstraction_and_modern_fintech_redesign_2.md` is:

1. **Neutral architectural canvas.** Light background `#F8FAFC`, surface `#FFFFFF`, dark background `#09090B`, dark surface `#121215`. Color is reserved for semantic signals.
2. **Typography with a purpose.** Plus Jakarta Sans for Latin/LTR, Cairo for Arabic/RTL, and JetBrains Mono for references, UUIDs, hashes, and money-adjacent technical strings. All fonts are self-hosted; no CDN is required.
3. **Compact, flat Vuetify defaults.** Ripple off, cards flat and rounded, buttons 36 px with no text transform, inputs outlined/compact with automatic detail hiding, and a restrained dialog scrim.
4. **A precision shell.** A 248 px permanent drawer on desktop, a 56 px flat app bar, keycap-style active navigation, collapsible section groups, breadcrumbs, a global search entry point, help entry point, theme/locale controls, and an operator identity card.
5. **A split-screen auth surface.** Institutional brand and security posture on one side; the login panel on the other.
6. **A primitive layer instead of page-level Vuetify soup.** Pages compose `PageHeader`, `StatusBadge`, `MoneyDisplay`, `MonoRef`, `MetricStrip`, `SurfaceCard`, `FormModal`, `FormField`, `SlideOverDrawer`, `DescriptionList`, `SegmentedTabs`, `EmptyState`, and `JsonDiffViewer`. The unified table surface is the fourteenth deliverable even though the design prose sometimes calls it a fourteenth primitive.
7. **Disciplined tables.** 40 px single-line rows, no rainbow row tints, one primary row action plus an overflow menu, a sticky action column, a row-level right-click/`Shift+F10` context menu that reuses the same action model, collapsible filters, and XLSX export through the shared pipeline.
8. **No global scaling transform.** A previous whole-app `transform: scale(0.9)` caused fixed-position and RTL problems and was removed. The old `SCALING_FEATURE.md` files were deleted; do not reintroduce them.

The implementation plan records one correction to the design prose: the blueprint says "14 primitives" but names 13 components. The 13 named exports plus the unified table surface are the actual contract checked by the compliance test.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Tokens and global styles

`admin-front/src/styles/fintech-minimal.css` is the canonical token sheet. It defines:

- Canvas, surface, hover, active, and glass backgrounds.
- Primary, secondary, muted, and faint ink colors.
- Subtle, strong, and focus borders.
- Primary and interactive accents.
- Success, warning, danger, info, and neutral status backgrounds, text, borders, and dots.
- Radii from 4 px to 10 px and low-spread shadows.
- Explicit screen, card, table toolbar, filter, chip, and footer padding tokens.
- Sans LTR, sans RTL, and monospace font-family tokens.

`admin-front/src/styles/globals/app.scss` supplies shared application behavior and selectors such as `.pg-skip-link`, focused main content, `hoverable` helpers, and the comment documenting the removed global transform. `admin-front/src/styles/command-palette.css` styles the global search palette. `admin-front/src/styles/settings.scss` is the Vuetify Sass entry point.

The same token sheet and font assets are mirrored in `merchant-front`, `checkout-front`, and `fake-rails-front`.

### 3.2 Fonts

`src/assets/fonts/fonts.css` registers self-hosted families:

| Family | Role | Weights present |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Plus Jakarta Sans | Latin/LTR UI | 200-800 normal and italic |
| Cairo | Arabic/RTL UI | 200-900 normal |
| JetBrains Mono | References, code, technical strings | 400-700 |

No external font request is required. `tests/e2e/admin/a11y.spec.ts` and the shell tests cover rendered accessibility and layout rather than font network loading.

### 3.3 Vuetify theme and defaults

`admin-front/src/plugins/vuetify.ts` is the canonical Vuetify configuration and is copied almost verbatim to merchant and checkout.

- Light theme: background `#F8FAFC`, surface `#FFFFFF`, primary `#0F172A`, secondary/accent/info `#2563EB`, success `#16A34A`, warning `#D97706`, error `#DC2626`.
- Dark theme: background `#09090B`, surface `#121215`, primary `#F8FAFC`, secondary/accent/info `#3B82F6`, success `#22C55E`, warning `#F59E0B`, error `#EF4444`.
- Locale: Arabic is RTL, English is LTR; fallback is English; the adapter is `adaptedLocale`.
- Icons: MDI default set plus the custom `i` set and aliases from `src/utils/iconSet`.
- Global defaults: ripple off.
- Component defaults: flat cards with `rounded: "lg"`; 36 px, `rounded: "md"`, no-transform buttons; outlined compact text fields/selects/autocompletes/textareas/comboboxes with `hideDetails: "auto"`; small rounded chips; a `rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.45)` dialog scrim.
- `VDateInput` receives an outlined default through the blueprint defaults block.

Theme mode is `system | light | dark`. `utils/theme` resolves the persisted mode (localStorage `theme`; absent means `system`) against `prefers-color-scheme`; `state/theme` applies it to Vuetify, listens to `matchMedia` changes while in `system` mode, and syncs across tabs. `plugins/vuetify.ts` uses `initialTheme()` for `defaultTheme` and `main.ts` calls `initTheme()` before mount, so every route (including the login page) starts in the operating-system theme with no light flash. `ThemeMenu` is the explicit three-option menu (System, Light, Dark) used by the shell, the auth layout and the merchant landing header; the old `toggleTheme` remains as a compatibility cycle (system -> light -> dark).

### 3.4 Primitives and extras

`admin-front/src/components/ui/index.ts` is the primitive barrel. The compliance test requires these 13 named exports:

| Primitive | Responsibility |
| :--- | :--- |
| `PageHeader` | Page title, subtitle, badge, breadcrumbs, optional actions/end slot; also defines help props that are currently unused by pages. |
| `StatusBadge` | Human-readable status pill with semantic tone and optional dot; centralizes status formatting and tone inference. |
| `MoneyDisplay` | Decimal-safe money rendering with currency, size, sign, and tabular formatting. |
| `MonoRef` | Monospace reference/UUID/hash display with copy affordance. |
| `MetricStrip` | Compact KPI strip used on dashboards and operational pages. |
| `SurfaceCard` | Flat hairline card with padding/title slots; `SurfaceCardText` is its body extra. |
| `FormModal` | Standard modal shell with title, body, footer, submit/loading/error behavior. |
| `FormField` | Static label, hint, error, required marker, and maker-checker hint wrapper. |
| `SlideOverDrawer` | Right/end slide-over shell used for details and contextual help. Open drawers keep a module-level stack and take a z-index from their position in it (base 1100, step 4, below Vuetify dialogs/menus), so the drawer opened last is always on top even when it is an always-mounted sibling of its parent (Vuetify otherwise gives earlier-registered items the higher z-index). |
| `AccountLinesTable` (`components/ledger`) | Server-paginated posting lines of one GL account with side/reference-type/date filters, search and totals of the filtered set; used by the wallet statement and the GL account drawer (`financeGlAccountLines`, `walletStatement`). |
| `DescriptionList` | Label/value lists with money, mono, and column options. |
| `SegmentedTabs` | Compact tab switch used for periods, roles, languages, and modes. |
| `EmptyState` | Empty/error-adjacent illustration-free state block. |
| `JsonDiffViewer` | Structured JSON patch/diff presentation. |

Additional exported primitives/extras are `SurfaceCardText`, `MetaPill`, `FormChecklist`, and `SummaryExportCard`. Legacy wrappers `StatusChip` and `MoneyText` remain as compatibility shims over `StatusBadge` and `MoneyDisplay`.

`src/components/ui/__tests__/ui-abstraction-compliance.test.ts` is the UI compliance gate. It asserts the required exports, absence of unlayered universal padding/margin resets, no rainbow row backgrounds, presence of `TableRowActions`, no raw `VDialog`/`VChip`/`VCard` in route pages, `PageHeader` usage on standard route pages, no gradients in the table/header/card system, and the v2 `SectionFields`, `ScreenContainer`, and `.pg-table-card` classes.

### 3.5 Shell

`admin-front/src/layouts/default.tsx` implements the authenticated shell:

- A skip link targeting `#pg-main-content`.
- A 56 px flat app bar with menu toggle, brand, breadcrumbs, live ledger invariant pill (for `profit.read` or `liquidity.read`), global search trigger (`Ctrl+K`/`Cmd+K`), help button, theme mode menu (System/Light/Dark), language menu, and user menu.
- A 248 px `VNavigationDrawer`, permanent on desktop and temporary below the compact breakpoint. It contains brand/environment badge, guide search pill, collapsible navigation sections, and an operator card with role and maker/checker dots.
- Route progress bar, focused `VMain`, global search palette, guide search modal, and contextual help drawer.
- The `?` key opens help when the user is not typing in an input; `Escape` closes the topmost overlay.

`admin-front/src/layouts/sections.tsx` owns the visible navigation groups and both `routesAuthorities` and `routesRoles`. The shell hides a section when every route in it is hidden, so an empty group header never renders.

`merchant-front/src/layouts/default.tsx` mirrors the 248/56 geometry with merchant navigation, guide search, help, locale buttons, and an operator card. `checkout-front/src/layouts/checkout.tsx` is intentionally a single focused payer column, not the admin shell.

### 3.6 Authentication layout

`admin-front/src/layouts/auth.tsx` implements a split-screen institutional layout:

- Brand mark, platform name, and "Admin Back Office" subtitle.
- Security posture heading and explanatory copy.
- Three posture badges: TLS 1.3 mTLS Verified, AES-256-GCM Hardware Vault, Four-Eyes Governance.
- A live status line.
- A main panel slot for the login form.

The auth shell also carries the three-mode theme menu in its top-right corner. `initTheme()` runs before mount and `plugins/vuetify.ts` uses `initialTheme()`, so the login page follows the OS theme on first paint and tracks OS changes while in System mode.

The auth shell is presentation only. Authentication, MFA, and session authority enforcement live in the edge and core services.

### 3.7 Fake Rails rollout

`fake-rails-front` is an optional deploy target. The deploy engine only builds and serves it when `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED` is true, with a production guard (`FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION`) and required SSH/certificate/credential settings.

Its UI rollout is partial by design:

- Fonts, token sheet, `components/ui` primitives, table components, row actions, and `SectionFields` are present.
- It uses `layouts/portal.tsx` and `layouts/hosted.tsx`, not the admin 248/56 shell.
- It has no admin route, admin guide, academy, or admin authority model.
- The admin compliance test does not scan it, so the anti-slop and primitive rules are not automatically enforced there.
- Admin users do not control Fake Rails from the admin portal; seeded rails appear as ordinary catalog records.

### 3.8 Removed app scaling and stale files

The application no longer applies a global `transform: scale()` to `#app`. The removal is documented in `admin-front/src/styles/globals/app.scss` and checked by `tests/e2e/admin/shell.spec.ts`, `tests/e2e/merchant/shell.spec.ts`, and `tests/e2e/checkout/pay.spec.ts`, which assert that the computed transform is `none`.

However, the stale files are still physically present:

- `admin-front/src/styles/README.md`
- `merchant-front/src/styles/README.md`
- `checkout-front/src/styles/README.md`

`scripts/project-design/check.ts` explicitly fails while these files exist. The files still claim a current app-scaling feature and contain unrelated scratch notes. This is a documentation/cleanup gap, not current behavior.

## 4. Contracts and invariants

1. **Token names are stable.** Pages should consume `--pg-*` tokens rather than hard-coded colors.
2. **No global #app transform.** No scale/zoom transform may be reintroduced on the application root.
3. **Shell geometry is 248/56.** The admin and merchant desktop drawer is 248 px wide; the app bar is 56 px high.
4. **The 13 named primitives must remain exported** from `src/components/ui/index.ts`, and the unified table surface must remain under `src/components/Table`.
5. **Standard route pages use `PageHeader`.** Public/login/not-found pages are excluded from the compliance scan.
6. **Route pages do not use raw `VDialog`, `VChip`, or `VCard`.** They compose primitives instead. Component-level files may use Vuetify internally.
7. **Action columns do not stack multiple `VBtn` elements.** They use one primary action plus `TableRowActions` overflow items.
8. **Checklist flags are runtime-config controlled.** `areChecklistsVisible()` reads `window.__PG_RUNTIME_CONFIG__.showChecklists`, then the legacy `showSnapshotExportChecklist`, then `VITE_SHOW_CHECKLISTS`, then the legacy Vite alias, defaulting to true. `areHelpPanelsVisible()` reads `showHelpPanels`, then `VITE_SHOW_HELP_PANELS`, defaulting to true.
9. **Deploy is the source of truth for admin visibility.** `deploy/deploy.ts` writes both build-time Vite values and `runtime-config.js`; runtime values take precedence.
10. **English and Arabic catalogues stay in sync.** The UI is RTL-aware and uses Vuetify's locale adapter plus the app catalogue.

## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface

| Surface | Location |
| :--- | :--- |
| Vuetify configuration | `admin-front/src/plugins/vuetify.ts`, `merchant-front/src/plugins/vuetify.ts`, `checkout-front/src/plugins/vuetify.ts` |
| Tokens | `*/src/styles/fintech-minimal.css` |
| Global styles | `*/src/styles/globals/app.scss`, `admin-front/src/styles/command-palette.css` |
| Fonts | `*/src/assets/fonts/fonts.css` and the adjacent font files |
| Primitives | `*/src/components/ui/**` |
| Tables | `*/src/components/Table/**` |
| Shells | `admin-front/src/layouts/default.tsx`, `merchant-front/src/layouts/default.tsx`, `checkout-front/src/layouts/checkout.tsx` |
| Auth layout | `admin-front/src/layouts/auth.tsx` |
| Compliance test | `admin-front/src/components/ui/__tests__/ui-abstraction-compliance.test.ts` |
| Deploy flags | `ADMIN_SHOW_CHECKLISTS`, `ADMIN_SHOW_SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_CHECKLIST`, `ADMIN_SHOW_HELP_PANELS`, `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED`, `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION` |

## 6. Operational usage

- Adding a page: use `ScreenContainer`, `PageHeader`, and the relevant primitives; add a table config only if the page uses the shared table server mode; add a route and navigation entry separately.
- Adding a status: use `StatusBadge` and keep the tone mapping centralized.
- Rendering money: use `MoneyDisplay`/`MoneyText` or decimal-backed utilities; never format money with floating point.
- Adding a drawer/modal: use `SlideOverDrawer`/`FormModal` so focus, padding, and footer behavior stay consistent.
- Totals rows go in a `<tfoot>` of a `.pg-unified-table`/`.pg-table-card` table: the shared stylesheet gives them the body-row padding, edge insets and a top rule (before 2026-11-07 a `tfoot` had no padding and its label touched the table border).
- Changing the theme: edit `plugins/vuetify.ts` and the `--pg-*` tokens together; do not add page-local hard-coded palettes.
- Learning surfaces: the Guide (`styles/guide.css`) and the Academy (`styles/academy/*.css`, see `03-guide-and-academy.md` §7.6) are built from these primitives and tokens. A feature area may add its own stylesheet under `src/styles/` imported from `main.ts`, but must not inject runtime `<style>` blocks, introduce a second palette, or cap the page width below the `ScreenContainer`; only reading text takes a measure (75 ch).
- Deploy-time visibility: set `ADMIN_SHOW_CHECKLISTS` and `ADMIN_SHOW_HELP_PANELS` in `deploy.env`; the deploy engine writes `runtime-config.js`. Rebuilding the SPA is not required for the runtime flags to change.

## 7. Status and deviations

### Implemented

- Admin, merchant, checkout, and partial Fake Rails token/font rollout.
- Vuetify theme, defaults, RTL locale, and MDI/custom icon setup.
- 248/56 admin and merchant shells with responsive temporary drawers.
- Split-screen admin auth layout.
- 13 required primitives plus `SurfaceCardText`, `MetaPill`, `FormChecklist`, and `SummaryExportCard`.
- Compliance test enforcing primitive usage, no raw page-level dialog/chip/card, no gradients, no universal reset, and table/action discipline.
- Removal of the global app-scaling transform.
- Runtime checklist/help-panel flags written by deploy.

### Partial

- Fake Rails UI adoption is partial and not compliance-tested.
- The 13-primitive layer is copied per workspace rather than shared as a package; merchant and checkout copies can drift.
- The design prose inconsistently calls the table surface a fourteenth primitive; the code treats it as a separate table subsystem.

### Missing / deferred

- No shared component package or generated primitive sync.
- No automated visual regression suite for the token system.
- No in-repo enforcement of the 13 exports for Fake Rails.

### Known bugs / risks

- **Documentation gap:** `SCALING_FEATURE.md` and `notes.md` were removed; the check script now fails if they are reintroduced.
- **Documentation gap:** the design blueprint says 14 primitives; the actual contract is 13 named exports plus the table surface.
- **Delivery risk:** per-workspace copies of primitives/tokens require manual synchronization.
- **Delivery risk:** Fake Rails can diverge because the admin compliance gate does not scan it.

- 2026-11-09 — Added system/light/dark theme modes across all four portals: `utils/theme` + `state/theme` resolve the persisted mode against `prefers-color-scheme`, `initialTheme()`/`initTheme()` apply it before mount (login included), a live `matchMedia` listener follows OS changes in System mode, and the explicit `ThemeMenu` replaces the light/dark toggle in the shell, auth layout and merchant landing. See `TRACKER.md`.
- 2026-11-03 — Initial canonical part created from the v1/v2 UI designs and working-tree code. Records the 13-primitive contract, 248/56 shell, Fake Rails partial rollout, removed app scaling, and the still-present stale files.

## Security hardening (2026-11-05)

- Blob previews whitelist png/jpeg/pdf and open with `noopener`; `ApiImage` renders raster images only; `resolveUploadPathWithMat` was removed.
- `console.log` is gated through `utils/devLog.ts` (DEV builds only).
- A fresh clone should `cp .env.example .env`; the real `.env` is no longer tracked.
- Catalogue keys added (EN and AR): "This file type cannot be previewed." and the full-backup confirmation text.
- **Logout and cookie sessions (GAP-019, RESOLVED).** The user store logout calls `POST v1/admin/auth/logout` (`urlsMap.authLogout`) through `revokeServerSession` (best effort, never throws) and always clears the local session. `utils/security/sessionToken.ts` handles the cookie mode: a login payload with `sessionCookie: true` is kept as the non-secret `cookie-session` sentinel and requests send `X-Pg-Csrf: 1` instead of a bearer token.
- **XLSX 0.20.3 (GAP-029).** `xlsx` is pinned to `https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/xlsx-0.20.3.tgz` (the maintained SheetJS build; the npm registry copy 0.18.5 is vulnerable) and `@types/xlsx` was dropped. The shared XLSX pipeline is unchanged. `@prisma/client` is still listed in `admin-front/package.json` although nothing imports it (residual).

## No raw operational JSON; structured builders (2026-11-06)

**Rule:** operational data is never shown as `JSON.stringify`/`<pre>`, and never edited in a JSON textarea. Allowed exceptions: raw HTTP wire traces (`gateways/ai-import`, the step/webhook trace blocks of `operator-cases/[id]`), data exports (`audit-logs` CSV/XLSX columns, the platform-settings backup file), and plain-text message bodies (rail instructions, notification template body, restore reason).

- **`JsonDiffViewer`** (rewritten) takes `diff: unknown`: an RFC-6902 array, `{operations}`, `{before, after}` or a plain payload (`DRAFT_AML_RULE`, `CREATE_ADJUSTMENT`...). The pure model `components/ui/jsonDiffModel.ts` humanises paths (`/payoutBankDetailsJson/iban` -> "Payout Bank Details · IBAN"), flattens nested objects to sub-rows, classifies money keys (`*Amount|*Ceiling|*Fee|*Balance|*Volume` -> `MoneyDisplay`), status strings (`StatusBadge`), lists (chips) and dates. `JsonValueCell`/`JsonValueList` render the same values as key/value rows. `components/JsonPatchDiff` is now a thin wrapper.
- **`summarizeAuditChange(before, after)`** (`utils/auditSummary.ts`) returns the humanised labels of the changed top-level keys (ignoring identical values and timestamps); `components/AuditChangeChips.tsx` shows up to 3 chips plus "+N more" in the audit-log table, Merchant 360 and the case timeline.
- **Builders** (`components/builders/**`, each with a pure model under `builders/model/` and unit tests): `CostModelBuilder` (+`formatCostModel`: `1.25% + 0.500 LYD (min…, max…)`), `RouteScopeBuilder` + `MismatchPolicyBuilder` (`tolerance_amount`, the only key the settlement engine reads), `MaintenanceWindowsBuilder` (absolute UTC `start`/`end`; a route is hidden while `start <= now < end`), `ParserConfigBuilder`/`ColumnMappingBadges` (statement sources), `AmlParamsBuilder`/summaries (7 rule types; `scope` is edited as a structured tree and the UI states that the engine does not evaluate it), `PlatformSettingTypedEditor` + `SettingValueView` (typed editors for the decision register OD-1..OD-11 and the policy keys; unknown keys fall back to a structured tree editor that preserves them), `LogoAssetPicker`, `ChipListInput`, `OptionChips`, `RepeatableRows`, `KeyValueSummary`, `StructuredValueEditor`. Every builder round-trips unknown keys losslessly.
- **Commission tiers:** `CommissionTiersEditor` (`pages/finance/pricing/components`) edits `{ upTo, flat, percent }` (percent is a fraction) and is shown for TIERED only (the calculator ignores tiers for FLAT/PERCENTAGE/HYBRID). The create form also carries min/max fee, fee bearer, rounding mode and optional merchant/application scope.
- **Shared drawers** (`components/ledger/JournalEntryDrawer`, `GlAccountDrawer`; `pages/merchants/components/WalletDetailDrawer`, `ApplicationDetailDrawer`) are opened by an id prop (`null` = closed) and emit `close`/`changed`. Governed actions share `ReasonModal` (>=10 characters) and a 202 handler that explains "submitted for approval" and links to `/approvals`.
- **i18n slices:** `constants/i18n/{commerce,ledgerOps,forms,builders}.ts` are merged by `plugins/i18n.ts` after the main catalogue; each new string has an `[English, Arabic]` pair and unit tests assert EN/AR sync. Table filter configs live in `components/Table/registry/{commerce,ledgerOps,forms}.ts` and are spread into `tableRegistry`.
- Compliance gate (`components/ui/__tests__/ui-abstraction-compliance.test.ts`): every standard route page uses `PageHeader` (helper components belong in `components/` subfolders), no raw `VCard`/`VDialog`/`VChip`.

## Remediation round 2 (2026-11-08): bundle size and translation gate

- **Lazy heavy chunks (GAP-060).** `utils/xlsx` is a lazy facade (the exceljs/xlsx chunk loads on the first export click) and charts load through `components/EChart/lazy.tsx` (`defineAsyncComponent`); `tests/unit/admin-bundle-lazy.test.ts` fails if the dashboard, profitability page, gateway health drawer or table header import the heavy libraries statically.
- **Translation gate (GAP-061).** `tests/unit/i18n-catalogue.test.ts` (scanner `tests/unit/helpers/i18nScan.ts`) fails on a literal `t()` key with no catalogue entry that is not in the shrink-only baselines `tests/unit/fixtures/i18n-missing-*.json`, and on a key whose Arabic value conflicts across catalogue files (the last spread silently won). The 18 conflicts were resolved; the existing missing keys stay in the baselines and are filled over time (`UPDATE_I18N_BASELINE=1` rewrites a baseline after a fix).

## Dark teleported overlays (2026-11-10)

Vuetify teleports dialogs, menus and drawers under a `.v-overlay__content` / `.v-navigation-drawer` element that receives the theme class and CSS variables but not a base text color. Custom surface components (`FormModal`, `SlideOverDrawer`, SafeguardDialog, the guide search surface, and any raw dialog content) therefore inherited the body's black text while sitting on the dark surface. `fintech-minimal.css` now sets `color: rgb(var(--v-theme-on-surface))` on `.v-overlay__content` and `.v-navigation-drawer__content`; component-specific text colors and status tones still override it. The same rule is mirrored in the merchant, checkout and Fake Rails portals, and `tests/unit/dark-overlay-colors.test.ts` guards all four stylesheets.

## Object & Asset Storage page

`/system/object-storage` (`pages/system/object-storage/index.tsx`) uses the shared
`ScreenContainer`, `PageHeader`, `MetricStrip`, `SegmentedTabs`, `SurfaceCard`,
`ApiTable` (with the built-in `TableFilters` toolbar), `TableRowActions`,
`SlideOverDrawer`, `DescriptionList` and `FormModal` primitives. The root uses
the standard 18 px section gap, the table cards are the `ApiTable` surfaces
(no nested `SurfaceCard`), and the page-header end slot carries the object,
quarantine and legal-hold summary badges beside Refresh. It has four tabs:
cluster/daemon health with maintenance jobs in a titled `SurfaceCard` and the
result in the shared `.pg-code-block`; object explorer with active locks;
quarantine/AV queue; and the access audit trail. Authority-gated actions:
`system:storage:read` (view), `system:storage:admin`
(maintenance/rewrap/GC/scrub/AV scan), `system:storage:legal-hold`
(place/lift hold with a written reason).

<a id="admin-uiroutes"></a>

> **Part ID:** `admin-ui.routes` · **Status:** `partial` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-13 · **Verified against:** `5a24f6f+working-tree`

# Admin Route and Page Catalog

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part records every protected admin route, the merchant portal routes, and the public checkout routes as they are defined in the router tables. It identifies each route's purpose, UI authority gate, role restriction, and contextual-help mapping, and it records where the UI gate is absent even though the backend still authorizes the request.

It does not define the backend authority matrix or duplicate the API surface. It also does not claim that a UI gate is a security boundary: `core-back` and the edge BFFs re-check every protected request.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The route design follows five rules:

1. **One explicit router table per SPA.** Admin, merchant, and checkout use `createRouter` with explicit route records; admin does not use file-based routing.
2. **Navigation and route gates are separate.** `layouts/sections.tsx` decides what is visible; `routesAuthorities` decides whether a direct navigation is allowed. A hidden item is not automatically protected, and a missing route gate is not automatically denied.
3. **Parent names drive active state and help.** Detail routes set `meta.parentName` so the parent navigation item is highlighted and the contextual-help drawer resolves the parent's guide mapping.
4. **Roles are layered on authorities.** Admin AML routes additionally require a `COMPLIANCE` or `MLRO` role. No other admin route has a role restriction.
5. **The backend is authoritative.** UI checks are advisory and server-side authority checks remain the real boundary.

The historical operator-case design also expects a dedicated operator-case inquiry schedule route; that is implemented as `GatewayInquirySchedules` rather than a separate top-level module.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Admin router composition

`admin-front/src/router/index.ts` defines:

- One protected parent at `/` using `layouts/default`, with 37 child route records.
- One visitor-only login route at `/login`.
- One catch-all `NotFound` route.
- A global `beforeEach` guard that redirects unauthenticated users to `Login` with a `redirect` query, redirects authenticated visitors to `Dashboard`, checks `routesAuthorities[name]`, and then checks `routesRoles[name]`.
- A global `afterEach` that clears route loading/error and dynamic-import retry state.
- A dynamic-import retry path for stale chunk errors.

`admin-front/src/layouts/sections.tsx` groups visible navigation into Overview, Onboarding, Governance, Operations, Finance, Gateways, and Learning. Sections and route items are filtered by their `if` callbacks. Empty sections are removed.

## 4. Contracts and invariants

1. **Protected route count is 38.** The generated catalog and tests must treat the 38 children under `/` as the protected admin surface; `/login` and `NotFound` are excluded.
2. **Merchant protected route count is 16.** Public landing/login/register/not-found are excluded.
3. **A UI gate exists only when the authority array is non-empty.** `[]`, `undefined`, and a missing key all behave as "no UI gate".
4. **Authority checks use OR semantics.** `hasOneOfAuthorities` accepts any listed authority.
5. **Role checks are additional.** AML routes require an allowed role after the authority check.
6. **Unauthenticated protected navigation goes to `Login`.** Admin preserves a `redirect` query; merchant does not.
7. **`meta.parentName` controls active navigation and contextual help.** Detail routes often use the parent's guide chapter.
8. **The backend re-checks authorities.** No UI route table is a security authority.

## 6. Operational usage

- Adding an admin page: add the explicit router record, the navigation item, the authority entry, and a `context-map.json` screen/route-name entry in the same change.
- Adding a detail page: set `meta.parentName` so navigation/help resolve to the parent; if the parent has no context-map screen, add the route name to the owning screen or `General`.
- Adding a merchant page: add the route, section item, `routesAuthorities` entry (unless intentionally open), and the merchant `ROUTE_HELP` entry.
- Adding a checkout page: keep the router minimal; do not assume the `Dashboard` route exists.
- Testing a route: verify both the hidden-navigation case and the direct-URL case; a hidden nav item is not a route gate.

- 37 protected admin routes with explicit components and names.
- 16 protected merchant routes plus public landing/login/register/not-found.

- Parent-aware navigation, breadcrumbs, and contextual-help lookup.
