> **Part ID:** `testing.multi-machine-matrix` · **Status:** `partial` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-04 · **Verified against:** `f7ecd82+working-tree`

# Multi-Machine Topology and Stress Matrix

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part owns the executable multi-machine lab harness under `deploy/test-matrix/`: the JSON lab config and its JSON Schema/Zod validator, intensity presets, topology derivation from declared machines and roles, deploy-config rendering, SSH bootstrap, teardown, the 12 gates, the open-loop stress workload and the certification report.

It replaces the hard-coded two-machine (HOST_A/HOST_B, T1–T8) lab. The previous lab is still expressible: `deploy/test-matrix/machines.two-host-lab.example.json` derives the same eight shapes and exposes them under the aliases `T1`–`T8`.

It does not own the production deploy engine (`07-deploy`), the storage adapters (`01-core-back/06-storage-engine.md`) or the ledger invariant (`01-core-back/03-ledger.md`).

## 2. Design intent

The design source `design/05-testing/multi_machine_topology_and_stress_test_plan.md` referenced earlier does not exist in the repository (dangling reference removed from the frontmatter on 2026-11-05); the archived plan under `design/90-archive/superseded-testing/` is the lineage. Key decisions:

- Machines (any N ≥ 1) and their roles are data. Topologies are generated by placement rules per family, not listed per host.
- Test intensity is data: a preset (`smoke`, `standard`, `soak`, `chaos`, `certification`) plus deep-merged overrides. Every workload size and SLO threshold comes from the resolved intensity.
- No secret is stored in the JSON or the repository. The sudo password is referenced by env-var name; lab-internal secrets are generated per lab at runtime.
- A gate passes only on measured evidence. Not-applicable or not-implemented checks are `SKIP` and never count as a pass.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Lab config (`labConfig.ts`, `machines.schema.json`)

`labConfigSchema` (Zod 4, strict objects) validates:

| Key | Content |
| :--- | :--- |
| `version` | `1` |
| `lab` | `name`, optional `lanCidrs` (default: each machine's `privateIp/32` + loopback), `markerFile` (default `/etc/pg-lab-matrix`) |
| `ssh` | shared `user`, `port`, `keyPath`, `generateKeyIfMissing`, `sudo` = `{mode:"nopasswd"}` or `{mode:"password", passwordEnv:"LAB_SUDO_PASS"}` |
| `machines[]` | `id`, IPv4 `address`, optional IPv4 `privateIp`, `sshPort`, `roles` ⊆ {controller, app, edge, db, cache, logs, backup, object-store, vault}, `labels`, `capacity.maxNodesPerTier` (default 3) |
| `services` | `objectStore` (MinIO machine/port/bucket/image/provision, optional `accessKeyEnv`/`secretKeyEnv`), `vault` (machine, basePath) |
| `topologies` | `families`, `include`, `exclude` (ids or aliases), `maxPerFamily`, `shardCount` |
| `intensity` | `preset` + `overrides` |

Semantic rules (superRefine): unique machine ids, addresses and private IPs; at most one `controller`; at least one `app`, `db`, `cache`, `logs`, `backup`; service machines exist and carry the matching role; `objectStore` is required; an existing (non-provisioned) store needs credential env refs. Before schema validation `findLiteralSecrets()` rejects any key that looks like a secret (`password`, `secret`, `token`, …) unless it ends in `Env`, with a hint naming the `...Env` replacement. Errors are aggregated and printed as `json.path: message`.

`machines.schema.json` is generated from the Zod schema by `bun run test-matrix:schema`; a unit test fails when it drifts. `configHash()` is the sha256 of the parsed, key-sorted config (formatting-insensitive) and is written into every report.

### 3.2 Intensity (`intensity.ts`)

Knobs: `durationSec`, `rampUpSec`, `targetTps`, `concurrency`, `requestTimeoutMs`, `hotLink{attempts,concurrency,useCount}`, `data{seedProfile,seedYearsSpan}`, `searchQueries`, `readSamples`, `gates` (`"all"` or ids), `continueOnGateFailure`, `attempts`, `chaos{enabled,allowDestructive,faults[{type,everySec,downSec}]}`, `slo{minTps,maxP95Ms,maxP99Ms,maxErrorRate,searchP95Ms,chaosMaxErrorRate,recoverySec,backupTimeoutSec,queueDrainSec}`.

`resolveIntensity()` deep-merges overrides onto the preset (arrays replace), re-validates, records the overridden paths, and rejects `primary-pitr` without `allowDestructive` and `hotLink.useCount > attempts`. The CLI `--intensity=` replaces the preset and keeps the overrides. The `certification` preset carries the archived strict targets (500 TPS, p95 < 35 ms, search p95 < 25 ms) that were previously behind `LAB_STRICT_PERF=true`.

### 3.3 Topology derivation (`topologyDerivation.ts`)

| Family | Variants | Placement |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `single-host` | one per machine with app+db+cache+logs+backup | 2 core, 1 admin, 1 merchant, 2 checkout, primary + local replica, Redis, audit/log, WAL-G |
| `split` | each (app machine, other db machine) pair | all compute on the app machine; primary/Redis/audit/log off it; Barman preferred |
| `replicated` | one per db machine as primary (needs ≥ 2 db) | local + every cross-host replica; Redis/logs off the primary; backup engine alternates WAL-G/Barman |
| `dmz` | one per `edge` machine | merchant/checkout/Fake Rails on the edge; core, admin, storage and backup on private machines |
| `mesh` | one (needs ≥ 2 machines) | every compute tier on every app machine (capacity-clamped) |
| `scale` | one | mesh + `rolling_update`; half the core/checkout nodes are scalable |
| `chaos` | one | mesh with WAL-G on the primary when possible; chaos gate enabled |

Ports are allocated per machine (core 4000+, admin 4101+10k, merchant 4102+10k, checkout 4103+10k, Fake Rails 4400, backup 4090, PostgreSQL 5432+ in primary/replica/audit/log order, Redis 6379), so co-located instances never collide. WAL-G is only ever placed on the primary's machine. Families that produce nothing are reported with a reason. With exactly two machines, `T1`–`T8` aliases map to `single-host@A`, `split@A/B`, `replicated@A`, `replicated@B`, `dmz@B`, `mesh`, `scale`, `chaos`. Unknown include/exclude keys are an error listing the derived ids.

### 3.4 Rendering and secrets (`topologies.ts`, `labSecrets.ts`, `generateTopologyConfigs.ts`)

`renderTopologyEnv()` produces a deploy env for the real engine: the shared SSH user/key/sudo for every tier, node specs `nodeId@address:sshPort:privateIp:port`, `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` when WAL-G and the audit DB are on different machines, `SYNTHETIC_SEED_PROFILE`/`SYNTHETIC_YEARS_SPAN` from the intensity, and `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` sized from `targetTps`. Lab secrets (KMS key, backup key, PG/replication/Redis/audit/log passwords, Fake Rails credentials, MinIO credentials) are CSPRNG-generated once per lab into `configs/lab-secrets.<lab>.json` (0600, git-ignored). Deploy envs are written to `configs/<lab>/deploy.<slug>.env` (0600) and re-validated with `loadDeployConfig` before any deploy.

### 3.5 Bootstrap, remote and teardown (`hosts.ts`, `remote.ts`, `teardown.ts`)

- Bootstrap verifies key-based `BatchMode` SSH and sudo on every machine and stops with the exact `ssh-copy-id` command when a machine is not authorized. It never prompts, never uses a password helper and never disables host-key checking.
- Peer keys (`~/.ssh/id_ed25519_pg_peer`) are created on db/backup/vault machines and authorized on the other peers with `from="<declared private IPs>"`.
- MinIO runs with credentials from a 0600 `--env-file`, not command-line arguments.
- `LabRemote` resolves hosts only among declared machines and adds `runAsync()` so fault/scale actions do not block the load generator.
- Teardown requires the marker file on every host before any destructive step and reports refused hosts; it only drops PostgreSQL 18 clusters.

### 3.6 Gates (`gates.ts`)

| # | Id | Measured verdicts |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | `provisioning` | PM2/backup-daemon state, core and edge mTLS probes, no-cert and wrong-channel rejection; DMZ: positive core reachability + every private storage port BLOCKED from the edge |
| 2 | `storage-routing` | `readSamples` reads served by replicas (or primary when none); RYOW with a paused replica must be served by the primary |
| 3 | `seeder-invariants` | seeded attempts > 0, Fake Rails `/health` HTTP 200, ledger invariant |
| 4 | `checkout-stress` | hot link: decisions, never oversold, exactly `useCount` wins; sustained open-loop load: achieved TPS ≥ `minTps`, p95/p99, error rate, every checkout node served traffic; ledger invariant |
| 5 | `realtime-sse` | SSE stream open + cross-node transition received |
| 6 | `workers` | stale non-terminal expired attempts; inbound/outbox drain within `queueDrainSec` (SKIP when the queue was empty) |
| 7 | `audit-chain` | UPDATE/DELETE rejected; `verify_audit_chain()` valid and covers every row |
| 8 | `log-db-outage` | only the log cluster is stopped; checkouts within error budget; step logs flushed after recovery; attempts grew by ≥ successes |
| 9 | `search` | p95 over `searchQueries`; SUPPORT search must succeed and not expose AML groups |
| 10 | `backup` | overview reachable, WAL archiving healthy, full backup completes within `backupTimeoutSec`, drill accepted |
| 11 | `scale` | scale-in at 1/3 and scale-out at 2/3 of a sustained run; error budget; restarted nodes serve traffic |
| 12 | `chaos` | scheduled faults (`core-restart`, `core-kill`, `replica-stop`, `redis-stop`, `log-db-stop`) under load; each injected and restored; error rate ≤ `chaosMaxErrorRate`; recovery within `recoverySec`; ledger invariant |

Velocity/AML rules are suspended only for the throughput gates and the exact set is restored afterwards. A provisioning failure stops the topology; other failures stop it only when `continueOnGateFailure=false`; unrun gates are `NOT_RUN`.

### 3.7 Runner and report (`cli.ts`, `report.ts`)

`cli.ts <validate|plan|bootstrap|run|teardown|schema>`; `--config` (default `$LAB_MATRIX_CONFIG` or `test-matrix/machines.local.json`), `--topologies`, `--intensity`, `--attempts`, `--dry-run`, `--skip-bootstrap`, `--skip-teardown`, `--keep-data`. `run` writes and validates configs, bootstraps, and per topology: teardown → vault dir → `deploy.ts --fresh` (plus `--update` for `rolling_update`) → gates → diagnostics on failure → retry up to `attempts`. Reports go to `test-matrix/reports/<runId>/report.{md,json}` with run id, config path + sha256, resolved intensity + sha256, git commit, machines, skipped families, per-topology attempt and passed/failed/skipped/not-run counts. Output is redacted for every secret-looking key and every known secret value.

## 4. Contracts and invariants

1. The lab JSON never contains a secret; literal secret keys are rejected.
2. Lab hosts are disposable only when they carry the marker file; teardown refuses unmarked hosts.
3. A topology is CERTIFIED only when it deployed, no gate FAILED or NOT_RUN, and at least one gate PASSED.
4. Every money-writing gate asserts zero double-entry drift (compared as an exact decimal string) and `gl_account_shards == journal_lines` (full outer join, so accounts missing on either side count).
5. Every report records the config hash and the resolved intensity.

## 5. Verification

```bash
cd deploy
bun run typecheck
bun test ./test/testMatrix.test.ts
bun run test-matrix:validate --config=test-matrix/machines.example.json
LAB_SUDO_PASS=... bun run test-matrix:plan --config=test-matrix/machines.two-host-lab.example.json
LAB_SUDO_PASS=... bun run test-matrix --config=... --topologies=T1 --intensity=smoke
```

Verified 2026-11-04: `cd deploy && bun run typecheck` passes; `bun test` 232 pass / 0 fail (31 in `test/testMatrix.test.ts`); `validate` and `plan` succeed for both example configs. No live lab run was executed.

## 6. Known gaps

- Live execution of the redesigned harness is pending lab availability.
- Admin-authenticated gates (2, 9, 10) depend on resolving the 403 seen in the last live run.
- `primary-pitr` chaos and restore-drill completion are SKIP until implemented.
- Per-host SSH users and Redis replication need deploy-engine support before the harness can derive them.
- Several archived-plan scenarios (webhook/confirm race, injected worker queues, 50-client SSE/POS pairing, pagination timing, network faults) are listed in the frontmatter gaps and are not yet gates.

## 7. Change history

- 2026-11-03: two-machine T1–T8 lab (`testing.two-machine-matrix`).
- 2026-11-04: replaced by the JSON-configured multi-machine harness (`testing.multi-machine-matrix`); hard-coded lab credentials removed.

## Gate 10 and the backup engine (2026-11-06)

`gateBackup` triggers a full backup, polls it, triggers a restore drill and polls `/system/backups/overview` until `latestDrill.id` equals the drill id and its status is `PASSED` or `FAILED` (same timeout as the backup), then asserts `status === "PASSED"`, `Number(doubleEntryDrift) === 0`, `balanceMismatches === 0` and `auditBrokenLinks === 0`; the former hard-coded SKIP is gone. The WAL check reads the overview's `walArchiveHealthy` (added by core). `LAB_BACKUP_MODE=pg-native` selects the engine. The dedicated-backup-host and host-loss scenarios are now exercised for pg-native by `deploy/backup-daemon/test/lab/two-host.lab.test.ts` (see `deploy.backup` section 3.7): all 8 steps passed on one LAN pair. That lab is separate from this matrix harness and is not part of CI.

<a id="testingdeploy-stress"></a>

> **Part ID:** `testing.deploy-stress` · **Status:** `partial` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-05 · **Verified against:** `1d91a3a+working-tree`

# Deploy Stress Harness

## 1. Purpose

`deploy/stress` drives the **real** `deploy/deploy.ts` against **this machine's real services** (PostgreSQL, PgBouncer, Redis/Valkey, MinIO, the backup daemon, PM2, nginx, Fake Rails) under database load, portal traffic, injected faults and config tampering, and asserts on what the services actually did. Nothing is mocked: process identity, `pg_settings.pending_restart`, journal lines and measured outage windows are the evidence. It exists because the unit tests mock the runner and therefore could not see that every deploy restarted PgBouncer three times at 90 s each (see `deploy.storage` section 16).

## 2. How it works

- `bun run stress` (from `deploy/`) reads `deploy/deploy.env` (`--env=` to override) and never modifies it. Every scenario deploys a throw-away copy with its overrides (`stress/env.ts`, parsed with the engine's own `parseDeployEnv`) and always re-deploys the original in cleanup. Derived env files carry the lab's secrets and are deleted when the run ends.
- Deploys run as child processes (async) so in-process load generators keep running: `startDbLoad` holds long-lived pooled connections through PgBouncer (small query every 50-250 ms, idle in between, which is exactly the shape that hangs a stock `systemctl restart pgbouncer`) and records errors and per-worker outage time; `startAvailabilityProbe` hits the four portal vhosts every 100 ms (a connection error or 502/503/504 is "down"; a 404 from the backend means it is up).
- A snapshot (`stress/probes.ts`) captures every service's identity in one sudo round trip (postmaster start time, `pending_restart` count, archive-command hash, `MainPID` + start timestamp of PgBouncer/MinIO/the daemon/nginx, Redis `run_id`) plus the deploy user's `pg-` PM2 apps. Two snapshots differing on a bounce key prove a service was restarted.
- Reports: `stress/reports/<runId>/report.{md,json}` (commit, host, seed, per-scenario checks and measurements); per-deploy logs in `stress/.work/<runId>/`. Both are git-ignored.
- `--destructive` gates the scenario that drops databases; `--intensity`, `--budget-factor` and `--seed` scale load, time budgets and the soak's reproducible fault choice.

## 3. Scenarios

| Id | Asserts |
| :--- | :--- |
| `noop-redeploy` | Repeated no-op deploys start/restart nothing, change no service identity, flag no slow command, keep a Redis sentinel key, raise zero DB-client errors, stay within budget. |
| `pgbouncer-reload` | A pool-size change reloads PgBouncer (same process, SIGHUP in the journal, new value on disk, zero client errors); restoring it is also a reload. |
| `pgbouncer-restart-under-load` | `systemctl restart pgbouncer` with 30 live clients is fast and the unit stops on SIGINT; `--force-restart` of PostgreSQL + PgBouncer completes in seconds and every client recovers. |
| `postgres-pending-restart` | `PG_RAM_GB=16` restarts PostgreSQL exactly once (`shared_buffers` 4GB), PgBouncer follows, nothing stays `pending_restart`; repeating it bounces nothing; the original value is restored. |
| `redis-config-change` | An unchanged redeploy keeps the Redis process and a cache key; a `maxmemory` change restarts it and is applied. |
| `chaos-recovery` | Nine faults, each repaired by one deploy: kill -9 PgBouncer, stop PostgreSQL/Redis/MinIO/the daemon, corrupt `pgbouncer.ini`, delete the PgBouncer drop-in and signature, hand-edit `postgresql.conf` and `pg_hba.conf`; then a final no-op bounces nothing. |
| `deploy-under-traffic` | DB clients see zero errors and each portal outage window is bounded while a full deploy runs. |
| `ssh-transport` | The whole deploy over real ssh + sudo-over-ssh + rsync-over-ssh (`127.0.0.2` as the hop, the real services stay on `127.0.0.1`); a no-op over ssh bounces nothing; multiplexing is not slower; no control master is left behind. |
| `multi-node-rolling` | Two nodes per tier with `--rolling-batch=1`: portals stay up; scaling back retires the orphaned PM2 apps. |
| `soak` | Seeded random fault + deploy cycles under DB load, then a closing no-op that must bounce nothing. |
| `fresh-database-stress-seed` (destructive) | Drops the application, audit and log databases, flushes Redis, deploys from empty with Fake Rails and the `STRESS` synthetic seed, takes a full backup through the daemon, then a no-op deploy must bounce nothing. |

## 4. Measured results (dev box, 8 cores, 31 GB, live data ~2.8 GB)

| Measurement | Before | After |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| Storage-tier no-op deploy | 4m53s | 5.1 s |
| Full no-op `--update` (build cache warm) | 5m14s (`--skip-build`) | 21-23 s |
| `systemctl restart pgbouncer`, 30 live clients | 90 s (SIGKILL after timeout) | 0.19 s |
| Forced restart of PostgreSQL + PgBouncer (`--force-restart`) | n/a | 4.8 s, longest client outage 2.0 s |
| Longest client outage across two PostgreSQL restarts | n/a | 2.6 s |
| Single-node portal outage during a full deploy | not measured | 0.41 s (`:8080/:8081/:8082`), 0.31 s (Fake Rails) |
| Rolling deploy, two nodes per tier | not measured | 0 s outage on every portal, 0 DB errors, 36 s |
| No-op deploy over ssh | not measured | 31 s multiplexed vs 80 s with one connection per command |
| Soak (6 random faults) | n/a | 15,664 queries, longest single-client outage 3.1 s |

## 5. Defects the harness found in the engine

- **Redis alias unit:** on Arch `redis.service` is a symlink to `valkey.service`; the new unit detector picked `redis`, and `systemctl enable` refuses linked units, so a stopped Redis could not be brought back. Detection now ignores symlinks and the start path does `enable || true` then `start`.
- It also confirmed, with live evidence, the original defects fixed in `deploy.storage` section 16 (SIGTERM hang, unconditional restarts, the flip-flopping `archive_command`).

## 6. Running it

```bash
cd deploy
bun run stress:list
bun run stress                          # non-destructive
bun run stress -- --destructive         # + fresh database + STRESS seed + backup
```

Operator notes live in `deploy/stress/README.md`.

<a id="futurevoucher"></a>

> **Part ID:** `future.voucher` · **Status:** `missing` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-03 · **Verified against:** `5a24f6f+working-tree`

# Voucher Provider Management System (Future)

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part preserves the complete design for a separate Voucher Provider Management System. It is **not current behaviour**. There is no voucher service, no Prisma schema, no route, no frontend page and no test in this repository.

The system would let an administrator plug in multiple voucher providers without per-provider code: configure authentication, purchase query stacks and voucher extraction, build a catalog tree, attach providers and product lists, issue bearer tokens to client applications, and let clients browse and buy vouchers with best-price routing and safe fallback.

This part is the canonical future design. If the feature is implemented, move it out of `09-future-and-unimplemented/` and update `project-design/TRACKER.md`.

## 2. Design intent (future, not current)

### 2.1 Goals and non-goals

Goals:

- Data-driven provider integration: auth, product listing, purchase and extraction are configuration, not code.
- Best-price routing with admin-controlled priority ties.
- Safe money handling: no double purchase, no lost voucher, full audit trail.
- A simple back-office for providers, catalog, assets, services and tokens.

Non-goals:

- Wallets, balances or accounting. Client systems keep their own accounts; this system keeps records, audits and logs.
- Markup or margin. Client systems add those.
- Currencies other than LYD.
- Multi-instance deployment in the first version (designed for, not built).
- A scripting language inside provider configuration.

### 2.2 Actors

- **Administrator:** configures everything through the back office.
- **API client:** an external system using a permanent bearer token to read the catalog and purchase vouchers.
- **Provider:** a third-party voucher supplier with its own HTTP API.
- **Operator:** reads transactions, logs and statistics.

### 2.3 Architecture

- Admin API and UI: CRUD for providers, listings, assets, services, tokens and users; read-only views for transactions, logs and stats.
- Public Voucher API: bearer-token-protected catalog and purchase endpoints.
- Provider Gateway: a registry of `ApiConsumer` instances, one per provider, handling auth, token refresh and request execution.
- Query Engine: runs a provider's purchase query stack and extracts the voucher.
- Catalog Resolver: builds the aggregated, ranked product listing for a service and caches it for a short TTL.
- Asset, Token and Audit services.
- PostgreSQL 18 using `@prisma/adapter-pg` and `pg`, with native UUID, JSONB and BYTEA where applicable.
- Money as `NUMERIC(18,4)`, never floating point.
- A single instance initially. In-memory caches sit behind an `InvalidationBus` interface: in-process emitter first, Redis pub/sub later, without changing callers.

Configuration keys:

- `API_LISTING_CONCURRENCY`: pool size for API-listed products, default 15, typical 15-20.
- `CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`: default 60.
- `CURRENCY=LYD`.

Purchases do not use a pool; each purchase runs its own requests.

## 3. As-built architecture

There is none. The repository contains no `voucher` workspace, no provider tables, no voucher routes and no voucher UI. The only related current code is the gateway half of the Smart AI spec importer, which is a reusable pattern, not a voucher implementation.

## 4. Contracts and invariants (future)

### 4.1 Data model

All tables have `id`, `created_at` and `updated_at`. All money is LYD, so there are no currency columns. Secret columns are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM using a key from the environment or KMS.

Providers:

- `Provider`: unique `name`, `blocked`, `auth_method` (`NONE`, `PERMANENT_TOKEN`, `REFRESH_TOKEN`, `USERNAME_PASSWORD`, `BASIC_AUTH`), `auth_config` JSON validated per method with encrypted secrets, and `auth_apply` JSON describing how credentials attach (default header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`).
- `ProviderMeta`: `provider_id`, `key`, `type` (`string|number|boolean|json`), `value`. Free parameters used by queries and auth, such as a merchant id.
- `ProviderQuery`: `provider_id`, unique `order_index`, `method`, full `url`, `content_type`, optional `success_check`, `timeout_ms`.
- `ProviderQueryParameter`: `query_id`, `place` (`HEADERS|QUERY|BODY`), `type`, `key` (recursive-set path), optional `selector`, `constant_value`.
- `ProviderExtraction`: one per provider with optional `secret_selector`, `id_selector`, `serial_number_selector`.
- `ProviderExtractionMeta`: `key`, `selector`.

A provider with no queries is never used for purchases.

Catalog:

- `Asset`: `name`, `mime` (`png|svg`), `size_bytes`, `storage_key`, `sha256`.
- `Listing`: optional `parent_id`, `kind` (`SUB_CATEGORY|SERVICE`), `name_ar`, `name_en`, optional `asset_id`, `priority_index`, `service_id` when kind is `SERVICE`. A service may appear under several listings.
- `Service`: `name`, `type` (`SECRET|BILL`), `blocked`, `form_enabled`.
- `ServiceMeta`: `key`, `type`, `value`.
- `ServiceFormField`: `key`, `type` (`date|date-time|time|number|string|from-list`), bilingual labels, `required`, `order_index`, `options` for from-list (`{value,label_en,label_ar}`), optional `rules`.
- `ServiceProvider`: `service_id`, `provider_id`, `priority_index`, `listing_source` (`FIXED|API`), unique on `(service_id, provider_id)`.
- `FixedProduct`: `service_provider_id`, `amount`, `price` (provider price), `face_value`, plus `FixedProductMeta`.
- `ApiListingConfig`: `method`, `url`, `list_selector`, `amount_selector`, ordered `face_value_selectors` joined by spaces, `price_selector`.
- `ApiListingMetaSelector`: `key`, `selector`, copied into product meta so it can be passed to purchase.
- `ApiListingParameter`: `place`, `key`, `type` (`PROVIDER_META|AUTH_TOKEN|CONSTANT`), `selector`. `AUTH_TOKEN` fails validation when the auth method has no token.

Access and operations:

- `AccessToken`: `name`, `token_hash`, `last_four`, `ip_whitelist_enabled`, `revoked_at`, `last_used_at`. Plaintext is never stored.
- `AccessTokenIp`: `token_id`, `cidr`.
- `VoucherTransaction`: unique `reference`, `idempotency_key` unique per token, `token_id`, `client_ip`, `service_id`, `service_provider_id`, final `provider_id`, `amount`, `price`, optional `expected_price`, `face_value`, `form_data`, `status` (`PENDING|SUCCEEDED|FAILED|UNKNOWN`), `error_code`, `result_ciphertext`, `result_meta`, `started_at`, `finished_at`.
- `TransactionAttempt`: one row per provider tried and per query executed: transaction id, provider id, query order, redacted request, redacted response, HTTP status, duration, outcome.
- `AuditLog`: admin action, who, before/after, IP.
- `User`: admin user with role.

Referential rules:

- Provider delete only when no `ServiceProvider` rows exist.
- Service delete only when no `ServiceProvider` rows exist; its listings are removed in the same transaction.
- Asset delete only when no listing references it.
- Listing delete for a service listing (service remains) or an empty sub-category.
- Transactions are never hard-deleted; they snapshot names and prices so history survives edits.

### 4.2 Provider authentication

- `NONE`: no credentials.
- `PERMANENT_TOKEN`: a token string.
- `REFRESH_TOKEN`: refresh URL, method, token, period, access-token selector and refresh parameters (`{type,key,selector,place}` with types `META`, `REFRESH_TOKEN`, `CONSTANT`).
- `USERNAME_PASSWORD`: same refresh flow built from `USERNAME` and `PASSWORD` parameters.
- `BASIC_AUTH`: username/password, `Authorization: Basic base64(user:pass)`.

Common settings: `auth_apply` (header name, scheme prefix or query/body key), `refresh_period_ms` (default 30 minutes), `refresh_on_error_statuses` (default 401, 403).

The runtime registry must fix the historical sample's defects:

- `recursiveSet` must not reset sibling containers and must not mutate the setter array.
- Cache lookup must precede the database await and store the creation promise to avoid duplicate consumers and timers.
- Concurrent 401s must share one single-flight refresh.
- Use chained `setTimeout` with jitter instead of overlapping `setInterval` async work.
- Every request needs an `AbortController` timeout (default 10 s for auth/listing).
- Retry on auth error only when the request could not have been processed.
- Support `content_type` per query, not always JSON.
- Make the auth header configurable and default `isAuthError` to 401/403.
- Persist a rotated refresh token.
- Implement `USERNAME_PASSWORD` and `BASIC_AUTH`.
- Read text first, parse JSON only when appropriate, and keep raw text in the redacted log.
- Never log auth headers, passwords or tokens.

### 4.3 Purchase query stack

Queries run in ascending `order_index`. Each parameter writes into headers, query or body at a dot path, with numeric segments creating arrays.

Parameter types:

- `PROVIDER_META`: selector over provider meta.
- `REQUEST_META`: selector over product meta.
- `AMOUNT`, `PRICE`, `FACE_VALUE`: values of the chosen product.
- `PREVIOUS_REQUEST_DATA`: selector over the previous response; invalid on the first query and rejected at save time.
- `SERVICE_ADDITIONAL_DATA`: selector over submitted `form_data`.
- Recommended additions: `CONSTANT` and `TRANSACTION_REFERENCE`.

Execution:

```text
ctx = { providerMeta, productMeta, amount, price, faceValue, formData, reference }
prev = null
for query in stack ordered by order_index:
    request = build(query, ctx, prev)
    response = consumer.request(request)
    assert success(query, response)
    log attempt (redacted)
    prev = response.data
voucher = extract(prev, providerExtraction)
```

Query strings use array indices by default. The final response is the extraction source unless `source_query_order` points to an earlier response.

Success detection: each query has an optional HTTP status set (default 2xx) and an optional `{selector, equals|exists|not_equals}` body check. A missing required selector is a failure.

Extraction: `secret_selector` is required for SECRET services. An extraction failure after a successful provider call is the worst case: the voucher was bought but not read. Keep the raw redacted response, mark the transaction `UNKNOWN` and alert.

Save-time validation rejects: first-query `PREVIOUS_REQUEST_DATA`, duplicate `order_index`, non-absolute URLs, invalid selectors and unknown parameter types. A dry-run builds requests without sending them.

### 4.4 Listings, assets, tokens and services

Listings:

- Root or sub-category parent; sub-category or service listing.
- Bilingual names required; image optional; `priority_index` sorts siblings ascending, ties by id.
- A service may appear under several listings with different names/images/priority.
- The admin sees one level at a time and can add inline.
- Cycles are prevented by choosing parents only at creation and verifying moves are not into a descendant. Suggested maximum depth is 6.
- Public visibility: a service listing is visible when the service is not blocked and has at least one unblocked provider with a non-empty query stack and non-empty product list. A sub-category is visible when it has a visible descendant. Admins see hidden items with a status badge.

Assets:

- PNG or SVG with a unique name.
- List, add, view with zoom/metadata, replace content, delete when unreferenced.
- Upload via multipart with client and server validation of extension, declared MIME, magic bytes, size (suggested 1 MB PNG, 200 KB SVG) and PNG dimensions.
- SVG is active content: sanitise on upload (strip script, event handlers, external references and `foreignObject`) and serve with `image/svg+xml`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- Store under a content-derived key; replacing content writes a new object and swaps the pointer (`?v=sha256`).

Access tokens:

- List, create, revoke; tokens are shown once.
- Format `vp_` + 32 random bytes base64url.
- Store only SHA-256 and last four characters.
- IP whitelist supports IPv4/IPv6 single addresses and CIDR. Trust `X-Forwarded-For` only from a configured proxy.
- Tokens grant catalog/purchase access only, never admin routes.
- Update `last_used_at` with debounce.
- Optional later: scopes, rate limits and service allowlists.

Services:

- List, add (`name`, `type`), update, delete when unlinked; detail view with recent transactions, form setup, meta, block/unblock and provider links.
- Form fields: key, type, bilingual labels, required, order. `from-list` options are `{value,label_en,label_ar}`. Rules are an ordered descriptor list compiled into a Zod schema from a whitelist; never evaluate admin code. Optional in v1.
- Form schema cached per service and invalidated on change; the same descriptor is returned to clients.
- Provider links: choose unlinked providers, set `priority_index` (higher wins ties). Product list is either FIXED products with meta or an API listing config with list/amount/face-value/price selectors, meta selectors and parameters. A link with an empty product list is never selected. Switching source requires confirmation. Provide a Test Fetch button.

### 4.5 Catalog resolution and purchase

Catalog resolution for a service:

1. Blocked service -> `404 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (same as not found).
2. Load unblocked providers with non-empty query stacks; none -> `404 SERVICE_HAS_NO_PROVIDERS`.
3. FIXED products come directly from the query.
4. API products are fetched in a bounded concurrency pool (`API_LISTING_CONCURRENCY`, default 15) with per-provider timeouts. A failing provider is skipped and logged.
5. Map keyed by `amount` plus `face_value` to `{amount, candidates[]}`. Each candidate has provider id, service-provider id, priority, price, face value and meta.
6. Rank candidates by price ascending, then priority descending.
7. Drop empty entries; sort by amount ascending.
8. Cache for 60 s, invalidated on provider block, service change or product edit. Purchases read the cache.

The public response exposes only `product_key` (opaque), `amount`, `face_value` and the best `price`. Provider ids, meta and priorities are never exposed.

Purchase request:

```http
POST /v1/purchases
Idempotency-Key: <client key>
{
  "service_id": "...",
  "product_key": "...",
  "expected_price": "10.0000",
  "form_data": { "...": "..." }
}
```

Validation:

1. Token valid, not revoked, IP allowed.
2. Service not blocked; `form_data` valid.
3. Candidates loaded; provider/service blocked flags re-checked against the database.
4. If `expected_price` is supplied and differs from the best candidate, `409 PRICE_CHANGED` with the current price. If omitted, no price check.
5. Idempotency: existing key returns the stored result or `409 IN_PROGRESS`.

Execution:

1. Insert the transaction as `PENDING` before any provider call.
2. Take the best candidate, load the query stack and run it, logging every query.
3. On success, extract, encrypt the secret, mark `SUCCEEDED`, return.
4. On failure, apply the fallback rule.

Fallback is allowed only when the failure is definitive and happened before the provider could act: first query, connection failure before send, 4xx or explicit error body, or auth failure after the refresh retry. If `expected_price` was supplied, a fallback candidate must also match it.

Ambiguous or partial failures always become `UNKNOWN`, never a fallback: timeout or reset after send, 5xx, failure on a later query, or extraction failure. Mark `UNKNOWN`, return 202/502 with the reference and alert. Manual reconciliation is the only exit.

All eligible candidates definitively failed -> `FAILED` and `503 NO_PROVIDER_AVAILABLE`.

Never automatically retry a purchase that may have been accepted.

Duplicate protection: the client `Idempotency-Key` and our `reference` stop duplicates at our side. The reference can be sent to the provider through `TRANSACTION_REFERENCE`; provider-side idempotency and order-status endpoints are optional per provider.

Logging stores reference, token id, client IP, user agent, service, provider, amounts, form data, per-query redacted request/response, durations, status and error. Voucher secrets are stored only encrypted and masked in admin screens; reveal is audited.

Response:

```json
{
  "reference": "...",
  "status": "SUCCEEDED",
  "service_id": "...",
  "amount": "10.0000",
  "face_value": "10",
  "price": "9.5000",
  "voucher": { "secret": "...", "id": "...", "serial_number": "...", "meta": {} },
  "created_at": "..."
}
```

Provider identity is not returned to clients.

### 4.6 API surface

Public, bearer-token auth:

- `GET /v1/catalog`: visible root items.
- `GET /v1/catalog/{listingId}`: children of a sub-category.
- `GET /v1/services/{serviceId}/products`: ranked products, service details and form.
- `POST /v1/purchases`.
- `GET /v1/purchases/{reference}`.
- `GET /v1/purchases?from&to&status&page`: transactions of the calling token only.

Error envelope `{code, message, reference?}` with codes `UNAUTHORIZED`, `IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `SERVICE_HAS_NO_PROVIDERS`, `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `PRICE_CHANGED`, `NO_PROVIDER_AVAILABLE`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `PURCHASE_UNKNOWN`.

Admin API:

- Providers: list/create/get/update/delete; block/unblock; meta; queries CRUD and reorder; query parameters; extraction; dry-run.
- Listings: list by parent, create/update/delete, reorder.
- Assets: list/create/get/delete, replace file.
- Tokens: list/create/delete, IP list add/delete, whitelist toggle.
- Services: list/create/get/update/delete, block/unblock, form, meta, transactions, provider links, fixed products, API listing config and test fetch.
- Operations: transactions list/detail with attempts, logs, stats, users, audit.

### 4.7 Security and observability

Roles: `SUPER_ADMIN`, `CATALOG_ADMIN` (listings/assets/services), `PROVIDER_ADMIN` (providers/tokens), `OPERATOR` (read-only transactions/logs). Revealing a voucher secret requires explicit permission and is audited.

- Secrets encrypted at rest with a key id stored with each ciphertext.
- Client tokens stored only as hashes.
- SSRF: provider URLs are admin-entered; enforce HTTPS, optionally allowlist hosts, resolve DNS and block private/loopback/link-local ranges, disable redirects or revalidate each hop, cap response size.
- Rate limit per token and IP; stricter on purchases.
- Zod validation on every route; safe selector path grammar; reject `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype`.
- Audit all admin mutations with before/after snapshots and masked secrets.
- Redact secrets from stored requests/responses.
- Structured logs with the transaction reference as correlation id.
- Metrics per provider: success rate, latency percentiles, refresh failures, fallback count, UNKNOWN count.
- Alerts: UNKNOWN transaction, extraction failure, repeated refresh failure, provider error spike.
- Stats: volume by service/provider, success rates, top tokens.
- Later: auto-block a provider after N consecutive definitive failures.
- Backups include encrypted columns and a key-management plan.

### 4.8 Delivery plan

The design proposes four phases:

1. **Foundations.** Admin auth and roles, assets, listings, services and forms, access tokens.
2. **Providers.** Five auth methods, `ApiConsumer` registry, purchase query stack, extraction, save-time validation and dry-run.
3. **Catalog and purchase.** Catalog resolution with the bounded API-listing pool and cache, purchase idempotency, fallback rules, UNKNOWN handling and redacted logging.
4. **Operations.** Transactions, logs, stats, alerts; then Redis invalidation when moving to multiple instances.

Confirmed decisions from the design:

- `price` is the provider's price; margin and customer-facing prices belong to client systems.
- Routing is server-side over the cached ranked list.
- Reference-based duplicate protection is required; provider-side idempotency and status endpoints are optional.
- Access tokens are shown once only.
- `expected_price` is optional and yields `409 PRICE_CHANGED` on mismatch.
- A service can appear under several listings.
- All amounts are LYD; no accounting is kept.
- API-listed products use a configurable pool; purchases do not.

Acceptance for the whole programme: all four phases delivered, the catalog and purchase APIs exercised against at least two fake providers, idempotency/UNKNOWN/fallback tests passing, secrets encrypted and redacted, and an operations screen with transaction and audit search.

## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface (future)

There is no current schema, route, environment key or deployment service. If implemented, the design expects a separate service with its own PostgreSQL database, admin API/UI, public API, provider registry and file storage. It must not reuse `core-back`'s database.

## 6. Operational usage

Not applicable. No runnable component exists.

## 7. Status and deviations

### Implemented

Nothing.

### Partial

Nothing in this repository.

### Missing / deferred

The entire system: schema, migrations, provider registry, query engine, catalog resolver, purchase flow, public API, admin API, admin UI, asset pipeline, token management, audit, metrics, tests and deployment.

### Known bugs / risks

- **Documentation risk:** historical summaries may claim the voucher system exists. It does not.
- **Scope risk:** the design assumes a separate service; implementing it inside `core-back` would violate the current service boundaries and database ownership.
- **Security risk:** provider URLs are admin-entered and require the same SSRF discipline as the gateway engine.

## 8. Verification and tests

There are no voucher tests. Acceptance requires at minimum:

- Schema migration and referential-rule tests.
- Provider auth method and token-refresh tests.
- Query-stack execution, parameter and extraction tests.
- Catalog ranking and cache-invalidation tests.
- Purchase idempotency, fallback and UNKNOWN tests.
- Token/IP/audit/redaction tests.
- Asset magic-byte and SVG-sanitisation tests.
- An end-to-end fake provider integration.
- A load test for catalog concurrency and purchase throughput.

# Smart AI Spec Importer and Voucher Half (Future)

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part documents the Smart AI-assisted onboarding pattern and its two intended applications:

- **Payment gateway rails:** implemented in `core-back/engine/specImporter/**` and `admin-front/src/pages/gateways/ai-import/index.tsx`.
- **Voucher providers:** designed but absent.

The overall feature is partial: the gateway half works, the voucher half is missing. This part has frontmatter status `missing` because the voucher half is the subject and it does not exist. The gateway half is described as current evidence and as the reusable specification pattern.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

### 2.1 The BYO-AI workflow

Manually filling an eight-step gateway wizard or building a multi-query voucher stack from a PDF or Postman collection is slow and error-prone. Plugging an external LLM into the backend would violate the air-gapped/LAN security boundary and risk sending live credentials to a third party.

The design uses an offline "Bring-Your-Own-AI" workflow:

1. **Download the AI onboarding kit.** The admin downloads a self-contained Markdown transcript generated by the backend from the live schema. It contains role instructions, the exact JSON schema, closed lists of auth methods/parameter sources/transforms/crypto operations, two gold-standard examples, and a fill-in section for the provider docs and credential names.
2. **Generate the spec externally.** The admin gives the transcript plus the provider documentation and credential field names to any external AI. The AI outputs one strict `integration-spec.json` with embedded `test_vectors`.
3. **Upload and verify.** The backend runs a four-layer verification before writing anything:
   - Layer 1: JSON/Zod schema and `spec_version`.
   - Layer 2: semantic and security guard (HTTPS, no private/loopback SSRF, no `PREVIOUS_REQUEST_DATA` on step 1, `MOVES_MONEY` retry policy `NEVER`, type-safe selectors/transforms).
   - Layer 3: offline vector simulation of request builders, crypto signers and response extractors against the embedded vectors.
   - Layer 4: collision check for gateway/provider/rail code.
4. **Bind secrets and activate.** Verification returns `requiredCredentials`. The UI renders password inputs for those keys. Import writes the full configuration in one transaction as a draft/blocked record, then the admin runs the live credential check or API-listing test and promotes it through maker-checker (gateway) or unblock (voucher).

### 2.2 Three refinements

- **Credential shape vs actual secrets.** The transcript must instruct the AI to use credential names/types or dummy sandbox values, never live secrets. The spec declares `required_credentials` (for example `[{ key: "MID", is_secret: false }, { key: "MerchantSecretKey", is_secret: true, encoding: "HEX" }]`). The portal collects the real values.
- **Embedded self-test vectors.** The AI must extract 2-3 sample request/response payloads from the provider docs into `test_vectors`. The backend simulates them before any live call and returns an `aiRepairPrompt` on failure.
- **Always import as draft/blocked first.** The spec creates a `DRAFT` gateway version or a `blocked=true` voucher provider. Activation is a separate, verified step.

### 2.3 Spec differences between the two systems

| Spec section | Payment gateway | Voucher system |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Identity | gateway code/name/operator/country/aliases/kind; SANDBOX/LIVE URLs and allowed hosts | provider name/base URL; provider meta rows |
| Auth | `gateway_auth` (ten methods) plus credential manifest, owner type and settlement target | auth method (`NONE`, `PERMANENT_TOKEN`, `REFRESH_TOKEN`, `USERNAME_PASSWORD`, `BASIC_AUTH`), auth apply, credential manifest |
| Catalog | rail code, bilingual name, collection mode, capabilities, rail fields, rail route limits/cost model | service link, `FIXED` products or `API` listing config with list/amount/price/face-value selectors |
| Execution | crypto profiles, flows across ten phases with `TransformPipe[]`, confirmation channels, status rules, error maps | purchase query stack with ordered queries, parameters, success checks and extraction |
| Vectors | sample initiate/confirm/webhook payloads, expected canonical status, signature string and wire amount | sample API-listing and purchase responses, expected extracted secret/serial/price |

### 2.4 Five reusable milestones

1. Unified spec Zod schema and cross-field semantic validator.
2. Dynamic AI transcript generator from live enums, transform whitelist and examples.
3. Offline vector simulator and dry-run verifier.
4. Atomic spec materializer.
5. Admin portal smart-AI wizard.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Gateway half (implemented)

`core-back/engine/specImporter/` contains:

- `specSchema.ts`: the Zod spec schema, enums and inferred types.
- `specValidator.ts`: schema, semantic, SSRF, retry, selector and crypto-reference checks.
- `SpecSimulator.ts`: offline vector simulation and verification report.
- `SpecMaterializer.ts`: atomic transactional import into draft gateway configuration.
- `TranscriptBuilder.ts`: dynamic Markdown kit generation.
- `index.ts`: public exports.

Admin routes in `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts`:

- `GET /gateways/ai-transcript`
- `POST /gateways/spec-verify`
- `POST /gateways/spec-import`

Admin UI:

- `admin-front/src/pages/gateways/ai-import/index.tsx`
- URL map entries `gatewayAiTranscript`, `gatewaySpecVerify`, `gatewaySpecImport`.
- The current admin guide (Book 6) documents the download -> external AI -> upload -> four-layer verification -> secret binding flow.

Tests:

- `core-back/test/spec-importer.test.ts` covers schema defaults, unknown auth methods, wrong version, transform list parity, SSRF, host allowlists, first-step `PREVIOUS_RESPONSE`, `MOVES_MONEY` retry, unknown crypto/placeholder, weak inbound channel, missing vectors, unimportable step types, aggregated defects, golden spec, initiate vector, wrong extraction/status/wire amount, signature vector, Layer 4 collision, self-contained kit, tailored examples and the secret warning.
- `core-back/test/spec-materializer.test.ts` covers draft import in one transaction, `NEW_VERSION`, duplicate `CREATE_NEW` refusal and invalid spec refusal.

The gateway half is real. It is the model to copy, not a voucher implementation.

### 3.2 Voucher half (missing)

There is no:

- `back/lib/specImporter/**` or equivalent voucher module.
- Voucher spec schema, validator, simulator, materializer or transcript.
- `POST /api/admin/providers/spec-verify` or `spec-import`.
- `front/src/pages/providers/ai-import`.
- Voucher database, provider registry or query engine.
- Voucher tests.

The voucher design therefore remains a specification. It must not be described as current.

### 3.3 Why the pattern is reusable

The gateway importer separates five concerns cleanly:

1. **Schema** (`specSchema.ts`) is independent of the UI and route layer.
2. **Semantics** (`specValidator.ts`) returns structured, AI-friendly diagnostics with `{path, code, message, aiFixHint}`.
3. **Simulation** (`SpecSimulator.ts`) executes request builders, transforms, signers and extractors in memory against `test_vectors`. It needs no network.
4. **Materialisation** (`SpecMaterializer.ts`) re-runs verification inside the backend, encrypts secrets and writes one transaction.
5. **Transcript** (`TranscriptBuilder.ts`) is generated from the live schema so the closed lists cannot drift.

A voucher port would keep those five boundaries and replace the inner domain payload:

- Identity: provider name, base URL, meta.
- Auth: five voucher methods and `auth_apply`.
- Execution: ordered purchase queries, place/type/key/selector/constant parameters, success checks and extraction.
- Catalog: service link source `FIXED` or `API`, listing selectors, product meta and purchase parameters.
- Vectors: sample listing and purchase responses with expected extraction.

The shared concerns (credential manifest, SSRF guard, secret redaction, offline simulation, atomic materialisation, repair prompt) should be extracted rather than copied blindly. The design says the architecture, UI flow and verification pipeline are about 90 percent identical.

## 4. Contracts and invariants (future voucher half)

1. The voucher spec version is explicit and checked.
2. URLs are absolute HTTPS and pass the same private/loopback/metadata SSRF guard.
3. `PREVIOUS_REQUEST_DATA` is invalid on the first query.
4. A purchase query that may move money is never retried automatically.
5. Selectors and recursive-set keys use a safe dot-path grammar; `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` are rejected.
6. Auth methods are a closed list; `AUTH_TOKEN` listing parameters require a token-producing auth method.
7. `required_credentials` contains names and shapes only, never values.
8. Import is atomic and creates a blocked provider.
9. Verification runs again inside the backend during import.
10. Secrets are encrypted with the Vault before persistence and redacted from logs.
11. The transcript is generated from live enums and the actual transform/parameter whitelist.
12. Every vector must execute offline; a failing vector returns a copyable repair prompt.

## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface

### 5.1 Current gateway half

| Surface | Location |
| :--- | :--- |
| Transcript | `GET /internal/admin/gateways/ai-transcript` behind `admin-back` |
| Verify | `POST /internal/admin/gateways/spec-verify` |
| Import | `POST /internal/admin/gateways/spec-import` |
| UI | `admin-front` route `/gateways/ai-import` |
| Engine | `core-back/engine/specImporter/**` |
| Tests | `core-back/test/spec-importer.test.ts`, `spec-materializer.test.ts` |

### 5.2 Future voucher half

| Surface | Location |
| :--- | :--- |
| Transcript | `GET /api/admin/providers/ai-transcript` |
| Verify | `POST /api/admin/providers/spec-verify` |
| Import | `POST /api/admin/providers/spec-import` |
| UI | `front/src/pages/providers/ai-import/index.tsx` |
| Engine | `back/lib/specImporter/**` |
| Data | Provider, meta, queries, parameters, extraction, service link |

These paths are design targets, not existing files.

## 6. Operational usage

For the gateway half:

1. Open `/gateways/ai-import`.
2. Download the AI onboarding transcript.
3. Give the transcript and partner docs to an external AI. Never include live secrets.
4. Upload `integration-spec.json` and run verification.
5. If a layer fails, copy the repair prompt back to the AI.
6. Bind the declared credentials.
7. Import as draft and run the live credential check.

For the voucher half: not applicable; no component exists.

## 7. Status and deviations

### Implemented (gateway half)

- Spec schema, semantic/SSRF validator, offline simulator, atomic materializer, transcript builder.
- Three internal admin routes and the admin UI page.
- Tests for the golden spec and failure paths.

### Partial

- The reusable pattern is not extracted into a shared module; a voucher port would duplicate code unless refactored.
- The current transcript/examples are gateway-specific.

### Missing / deferred (voucher half)

- Everything listed in section 3.2.
- A shared `specImporter` package usable by both systems.
- A voucher transcript with provider/auth/query/listing/extraction examples.
- A voucher simulator for listing and purchase vectors.
- A voucher materializer and admin wizard.
- Voucher tests.

### Known bugs / risks

- **Documentation risk:** the existence of the gateway importer may be misread as the voucher feature existing.
- **Duplication risk:** copying the gateway module without extracting shared guards would create two security implementations.
- **Secret risk:** an AI transcript that includes real credentials would leak them to a third-party model.
- **Drift risk:** a hand-written voucher transcript would fall out of sync with the live schema.

## 8. Verification and tests

Gateway half:

- `core-back/test/spec-importer.test.ts` (about 29 declarations) covers schema, semantics, SSRF, vectors and transcript.
- `core-back/test/spec-materializer.test.ts` (4 declarations) covers atomic import and collision/version behaviour.

Voucher half: none. Acceptance requires the voucher module, routes, UI, schema, simulator, materializer and a test suite mirroring the gateway coverage plus voucher-specific listing/purchase/extraction vectors.

# Deferred and Partial Features

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part is the catch-all register for missing or partial features that are not large enough for their own future part. It distinguishes:

- `missing`: designed or expected but absent.
- `partial`: present but narrow or incomplete.
- `deferred`: intentionally postponed with a recorded decision.

The voucher system and the voucher half of the Smart AI importer have dedicated parts in this directory. They are listed here for completeness but their full design lives in those parts. The admin guide v2 is implemented and is documented under `03-admin-front/06-guide-v2.md`.

This file is not current-behaviour documentation for the missing items. Each entry states what exists today and what acceptance would require.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The historical design backlog identifies several P0/P1 gaps: schema counts, attempt lifecycle, engine phases, ledger scenarios, transforms, CQRS, replica reads, pagination, audit outbox, backup scheduling, deploy prune, PM2 templates, storage mTLS, admin/merchant routes, fake rails, voucher, exhaustive tests and stale frontend notes. The admin guide v2 item is now implemented.

Most factual counts are now fixed in the canonical parts. The remaining items below are behavioural or architectural gaps that require code work, not a doc edit.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Deferred feature register

| ID | Feature | Status | Current evidence | Acceptance criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| D-02 | Admin Guide v2 | `implemented` | 14 books/137 articles/154 terms/26 cards/32 situations/5 simulators/8 routes with generated content, context help and safeguards | See `admin-ui.guide-v2`; only the Arabic article set remains outstanding |
| D-03 | Smart AI voucher importer half | `missing` | Gateway importer only in `core-back/engine/specImporter/**` | See `future.smart-ai-voucher`; voucher schema/validator/simulator/materializer/transcript/UI/tests |
| D-04 | Merchant Google OIDC login | `deferred` | `core-back/api/internal/merchant.ts` `/auth/google` returns `501 GOOGLE_IDENTITY_NOT_CONFIGURED` | Configure issuer/client/audience, verify ID tokens, map identities, test success/failure |
| D-05 | Keyset pagination | `partial` | `core-back/lib/listQuery.ts` supports cursor pagination (2026-11-04) but only merchant `/payments` uses it; the other lists still use `skip/take` | Add stable cursor keys, cursor encode/decode, index coverage, API compatibility and tests at high offsets |

| D-15 | Synthetic seeder breadth | `partial` | 55 collections/9 generators; only payment/adjustment ledger refs; profile volumes not fully enforced | Cover remaining models or document the intentional subset; enforce profile volumes; add audit tests |

### 3.2 Merchant Google OIDC (D-04)

Current code parses `{ idToken }` and throws `501 GOOGLE_IDENTITY_NOT_CONFIGURED`. The merchant frontend renders a Google button, so a user can reach a dead end. Acceptance requires issuer, client id, audience and JWKS configuration, ID-token signature/claim verification, identity linking or creation rules, replay/expiry checks, audit logging, bilingual errors and tests for valid, expired, wrong-audience and unverified-email tokens.

### 3.3 Pagination (D-05)

`parseListQuery()` normalizes `page`, `pageSize`, search, sort and filters, then `buildListQuery()` returns `skip: (page - 1) * pageSize` and `take`. Every list endpoint uses offset pagination. The design's keyset pagination is not implemented.

Acceptance:

- Stable sort keys with a unique tie-breaker.
- Opaque cursor encoding/decoding with validation.
- Backward-compatible page/pageSize or a documented versioned change.
- Indexes that support the cursor predicates.
- Tests for inserts/deletes between pages, duplicate sort values and high offsets.
- A measured improvement on a large dataset.

### 3.4 CQRS read models (D-06)

`lib/storageEngine/ledgerPosterFactory.ts` emits `ledger.entry_posted`, but `lib/storageEngine/outboxWorkers.ts` handles it as `async () => undefined`. Only `attempt.transitioned` updates `rm_merchant_daily_stats` and `rm_route_daily_volumes`. There is no `rm_wallet_statements`, and dashboards do not read the read models.

Acceptance:

- A ledger projection handler with idempotent upserts.
- Defined rebuild/backfill procedure.
- Dashboard/list queries that consume the read models.
- Lag/consistency monitoring.
- Tests for duplicate events, out-of-order events and rebuild parity.

### 3.5 Replica reads (D-07)

`readStore` supports primary, replica and `{ atLeastLsn }` modes, with lag thresholds, round-robin and primary fallback. The read-store tests are broad but use fake replica handles. Only global search and three merchant list endpoints use it; most reads stay on the primary.

Acceptance:

- A documented routing matrix per endpoint.
- Read-your-own-writes through a commit LSN header where needed.
- Live replica tests for lag, failure and fallback.
- Dashboard/list/export parity tests.
- Metrics for servedBy and replica lag.

### 3.6 Storage mTLS (D-08)

Certificates are generated and distributed by `pkiManager.ts`, but PostgreSQL and Redis configurations do not consume them. The stale-claims register keeps this open.

Acceptance:

- PostgreSQL `ssl=on` with the internal CA and client certificates.
- Redis TLS with the same trust chain.
- Certificate rotation procedure.
- Negative tests for missing/wrong/expired certificates.
- A deployment smoke test proving the encrypted connection.

### 3.7 Backup scheduling and restore (D-09, D-10, D-20)

The backup daemon supports full, delta and drill runs, a policy, a catalog and restore-drill verification. The design's "weekly drill at Tripoli 03:00" and "hourly Redis BGSAVE" are not current behaviour. The scheduler is UTC and Redis is part of a triggered backup.

Acceptance for D-09: a documented schedule with timezone, hourly Redis policy if retained, retention and alerting tests.

Acceptance for D-10: a staging/production drill that records restore duration, replayed LSN, row counts, zero ledger drift, shard parity and audit-chain integrity, and stores a signed report.

Acceptance for D-20: retention policy for audit outbox, inbound events, logs and backups; a purge job with dry-run, batching, metrics and tests.

### 3.8 Fake rails fidelity and seeding (D-11 to D-14, D-18)

The detailed evidence is in the fake-rails parts. The minimum acceptance path is:

1. Make route keys and seeded gateway codes identical for all supported rails.
2. Fix the webhook path and token to the real inbound channel.
3. Add inbound auth/signature verification and per-gateway route tests.
4. Either seed the seven missing gateways or remove them from the descriptor catalogue.
5. Make the embedded widget loadable under the checkout CSP with SRI.
6. Keep the backend loopback-only or add TLS; redact stored wire logs.

### 3.9 Synthetic seeder breadth (D-15)

The seeder covers a documented subset and has safety gates. Acceptance requires either full model coverage or an explicit, tested subset contract; enforcement of profile volumes; correct ledger reference coverage; and a post-seed audit that fails on any uncovered invariant.

### 3.10 Testing gaps (D-16, D-17, D-19)

The suite catalog documents the missing suite 09, the absent suite 11 directory and the large gap between the claimed and actual test volume. Acceptance requires:

- A suite directory or a renamed gate with an explicit substitution.
- A measured test inventory that replaces the 38,500 claim.
- Real merchant IDOR and checkout Zod fuzz matrices.
- Live UI journeys that do not mock every API.

## 4. Contracts and invariants

1. A feature listed as `missing` must not be described as current anywhere else.
2. A `partial` feature must name the narrow adoption and the remaining gap.
3. A `deferred` feature must state who decided to postpone it or point to the tracker/decision log.
4. Acceptance criteria must be testable, not aspirational.
5. Fixing an item requires updating this file, the dedicated part if any, and `project-design/TRACKER.md`.

<a id="futureledger-archive"></a>

> **Part ID:** `future.ledger-archive` · **Status:** `missing` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-08 · **Verified against:** `working-tree`

# Ledger Archive and Shard Repair Anchors (Future)

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part records a design decision for a feature that does **not exist yet**: moving old journal lines out of `journal_lines` into an archive to keep the live table small, and what that means for the per-shard checkpoints and for shard repair (`core.ledger` sections 3.6 and 3.10). It is not current behaviour. When archiving is implemented, move this part out of `09-future-and-unimplemented/` into `01-core-back/` and update `project-design/TRACKER.md`.

## 2. Owner decision: the archive is the default source of truth for a repair

Once old lines are archived, a shard's balance can no longer be recomputed from the live table alone. A repair of a damaged shard (RECOMPUTE or REBASELINE) has two possible sources:

1. **Archive plus live** — sum every line that ever existed: the archived lines of the shard plus its live lines. This is the strongest source.
2. **Anchor plus live** — start from the shard's last trusted checkpoint (its balance at the archive cut) and add the live lines after it. This is cheap and needs no archive access, but it is only as trustworthy as that checkpoint.

**Decision (2026-11-08):** a repair uses **archive plus live by default**. The **anchor shortcut is used only when the deployment explicitly enables it through a deploy environment variable** (to be named when the feature is built, for example `LEDGER_SHARD_REPAIR_USE_ANCHOR`, default `false`, defined in `core-back/lib/env/index.ts`, `deploy/lib/configSchema.ts`, `deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts` and the deploy env examples). With the variable off, a repair that cannot read the archive must refuse, never fall back silently to the anchor.

## 3. Requirements for the feature

These are what makes either source safe:

- **Archive only below a verified checkpoint.** A shard's lines are archived up to a sequence number whose checkpoint was proven (`CheckpointService.captureShard`) at that moment.
- **A per-shard anchor.** Record `archived_through_seq`, the balance at that point and a manifest of the archived range (line count, signed sum, content hash). The archive is verified against the manifest before the live rows are deleted.
- **The archive is immutable and independently readable.** An archive that cannot be read must make a default-mode repair fail with a clear error.
- **Repair planning is source-aware.** `planShardRepair` takes the line source (archive plus live, or anchor plus live), checks that the archive agrees with the anchor manifest in the default mode and reports any difference, and records the source used in `gl_shard_repairs.details_json` and the audit row.
- **The other deep checks follow the same rule.** The restore drill parity query and the deploy gate count only the lines above the archive anchor (the same way they already honour `baseline_seq`), or read the archive in default mode.
- **Append-only protection.** The archive path needs its own guards: the ledger triggers still reject deletes, so the archiver is a deliberate maintenance operation (`pgw.ledger_maintenance`), audited, and never part of the general retention worker.
- **`baseline_seq` stays compatible.** A re-baselined shard keeps its exemption for the damaged history; the archive anchor must not be placed below an unrepaired gap.

## 4. Verification when implemented

Real-PostgreSQL tests with a small archive: repair from archive plus live equals the pre-archive repair result; the anchor mode equals it when the checkpoint was proven; a tampered archive (manifest mismatch) is detected; a default-mode repair refuses when the archive is unreadable; the restore drill and deploy gate pass on a shard with an archived prefix.

> **Part ID:** `companion.offline` · **Status:** `partial` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-07 · **Verified against:** `working-tree`

# Offline Android Companion

## 1. Purpose and scope

PG Companion (`companion-app/`, application ID `ly.paymentgateway.companion`) is a private,
offline-first Android application containing the complete Admin Interactive Guide and the
learner-facing Employee Academy. It is a new standalone workspace and does not import
runtime code from `admin-front`, `admin-back`, `core-back` or `deploy`.

It exists so staff can read the guide and practise Academy material away from the live admin
portal. It has no login, no server progress sync, no backend calls and no analytics. Official
certification exams are deliberately excluded because their question bank and answer keys
must never leave the server.

The approved blueprint is `design/06-ui/pg_companion_offline_android_app.md`; the
implementation contract is `companion-app/BLUEPRINT.md`.

## 2. Content pipeline

The app mirrors the true content during build:

1. `companion-app/scripts/sync-content.ts` runs the canonical extractors
   `admin-front/scripts/extract-guide-content.ts` and
   `admin-front/scripts/extract-academy-content.ts` with output paths redirected into
   `companion-app/.cache/`.
2. `scripts/build-bundle.ts` validates counts, ids, cross-document links, lesson reading and
   check references, lab references, exam-bank leakage, external URLs and private-key
   markers. It writes `public/content/bundle.json` and `manifest.json`.
3. The exam bank and server catalog stay in `.cache` and are never copied into the app.
4. `scripts/check-content.ts` re-runs the extractors and fails if the committed snapshot is
   stale, or if `admin-front` generated content has drifted.

The current snapshot contains 14 guide books, 137 articles, 154 glossary terms, 26 safeguard
cards, 32 situations, 60 quick answers, 19 error codes, 140 edge cases; and 8 Academy tracks,
11 modules, 51 lessons, 102 practice checks, 16 labs / 92 tasks, 11 drills and 7 learner pages.
The exam bank has 223 questions with keys but is not in the bundle.

## 3. Application

The client is Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite + Capacitor 8. It uses hash routing, no Vuetify, no
remote UI assets, and a self-contained markdown renderer with callouts, guide links,
glossary auto-linking, heading ids, table/diagram handling and simulator placeholders.
Article and lesson tables keep a `9.5em` minimum column width and scroll horizontally
inside a focusable wrapper (themed thin scrollbars, contained overscroll) on narrow
screens; cells use `overflow-wrap: normal`, so a long identifier or word is never broken
letter by letter.

The clarity renderer matches the Admin Guide: parenthetical reference dumps are removed from
sentences and collected into a per-section **Related** tray of typed pills; bare inline links
use a short natural title rather than the full article title; `:::summary` renders an
"In plain words" banner and `:::refs` renders a "Where to go next" footer; and tapping a
guide, screen or playbook pill opens a **reference preview sheet** with a short body,
**Keep reading here** and **Open full page →**. The sheet is dismissible by backdrop,
Escape or its close button.

Screens:

- Today: continue reading, deterministic daily brief, reading rhythm, role reading path.
- Guide: home, book, article reader, glossary, safeguard cards, playbook, 140 edge cases,
  quick answers/error codes, five simulators.
- Academy: tracks, modules, lessons, practice checks, all 16 labs with offline scoring,
  drills, help pages and a practice exam.
- Saved: article/lesson bookmarks, section bookmarks, highlights and notes.
- Search: offline MiniSearch over guide and academy.
- Settings: theme, text size, serif reading font, language/RTL, reading path, reminders,
  export/import, content updates, versions.

Progress, bookmarks, reading positions, highlights, reading days and settings use Capacitor
Preferences. Notes/highlights and downloaded content bundles use Capacitor Filesystem. No
critical state is stored only in WebView localStorage.

## 4. Reminders and reading experience

Reading reminders are opt-in, scheduled with `@capacitor/local-notifications` as inexact,
Doze-friendly one-shot reminders for a rolling window. The app re-arms them on launch/resume
and the plugin restores them after boot. Reminders are skipped when the user already read
that day or the chosen time falls inside quiet hours. Android 13+ notification permission is
requested only when the user enables reminders.

The reading experience avoids punitive streak mechanics. It shows a weekly reading rhythm,
with rest days allowed, a deterministic daily brief, focus mode, bookmarks, highlights,
notes, light/dark/sepia themes, adjustable typography, subtle completion feedback and native
app shortcuts (Continue, Search, Saved, Guide). Android installation is private; the APK and
content bundle must not be published publicly.

## 5. Updates and signing

Content-only updates are signed manifests plus a bundle:

- `bun run content:key` creates the Ed25519 content key in `.keys/` and writes the public key
  to `public/content/public-key.txt`.
- `COMPANION_UPDATE_BASE_URL=... bun run release:content` writes
  `release/content-<hash>.json` and `release/manifest.json` with a signature over the bundle
  SHA-256.
- The client verifies the pinned signature, bundle SHA-256 and bundle schema before writing a
  versioned file and switching the active pointer atomically. A bad update falls back to the
  APK bundle. Content updates are data-only and cannot execute code.
- Rollback protection (2026-11-08): the signature covers only the bundle SHA-256, so the manifest dates (`publishedAt`, `generatedAt`) are NOT authenticated and cannot be trusted to refuse an old bundle (an old genuine bundle plus its old signature, under a manifest with an edited future date, used to install). `installUpdate` therefore also compares the bundle's own `meta.generatedAt`, which sits inside the checksummed bytes, against the installed content (`assertBundleNotOlderThanInstalled`) and refuses an older one. The manifest check in `checkForUpdate` remains a courtesy pre-filter. A signature over a canonical `appId|contentVersion|contentHash|generatedAt|bundleSha256` string would also authenticate `contentVersion`/`minAppVersion`; it needs a versioned signature so installed apps keep accepting old manifests (open).

APK releases use a separate long-lived release keystore generated on first local build at
`.keys/companion-release.jks` (password in `.keys/keystore.env`, mode 0600, gitignored).
The same package name and signing key are required for in-place updates. The APK is signed
and verified with `apksigner`; `allowBackup` and cleartext traffic are disabled, and the
exact-alarm permission is removed because reminders are intentionally inexact.

`.github/workflows/companion.yml` builds and tests on content changes, publishes a private
release when the signing secrets are present, and can be run manually. The signing secrets (release keystore and content-signing key) are only exposed to builds of the default branch; any other ref builds and tests without signing or publishing. Content OTA needs a
private HTTPS endpoint; if one is not available, APK releases carry the latest content.

## 6. Build

`companion-app/build-apk.sh` (also `bun run apk`) performs content sync, content check,
typecheck, tests, web build, Capacitor sync, Gradle APK build, signing, `apksigner`
verification, copy to `release/` and SHA-256/build-info generation. It detects a JDK 21
installation (including `$HOME/.jdks/temurin-21`), Android SDK platform 36 and build-tools.
`--offline-snapshot`, `--debug`, `--install` and `--skip-tests` are available.

The 2026-11-06 build produced a 3.8 MiB signed APK with SHA-256
`75960424c47ca254a009a4c91156584a8c03a5eaaf15cf7ead245b66d4e1f013`.

## 7. Verification

- `bun run content:check` passes against the canonical extractors.
- `bun run typecheck` passes.
- `bun test` passes 23 tests: content integrity, markdown rendering (including parenthetical
  extraction, summary/refs callouts, section trays, preview-snippet helpers and the
  scrollable table wrapper), offline search and all 18 published lab-scoring vectors.
- Web Playwright smoke covers 24 routes at 360/390/768 px, light/dark/sepia, English/Arabic
  chrome, with no horizontal overflow or console errors.
- The release APK passes `apksigner verify`; the content manifest signature and bundle
  SHA-256 were independently verified.
- Not run: installation on a physical device or emulator, airplane-mode smoke, notification
  delivery after reboot, and real-device performance measurements.
